risks: Merged splat (b): joint SfM between canopy-top and under-canopy images is likely to fail or mis-register; densification conflicts degrade both views; floaters and a double canopy appear where the layers overlap.
Separate layer (c): decimetre misregistration (0.3–0.5 m with natural features) shows as ghosting unless the layer content is kept apart by cropping, or targets visible from both views are used.
Under-canopy RTK/GNSS is unreliable, and the BLK2GO has no GNSS, so commercial-style RTK fusion cannot be used.
Appearance mismatch: sunlit canopy top vs shaded understory (transmittance 2–90%), and different capture times, seasons or wind states between drone and ground capture.
Wind moves crowns between drone images, which adds SfM and splat noise in the canopy; overlap below about 80–90% gives holes.

Under-canopy drone flight: collisions with thin branches, GNSS-denied drift, prop wash moving foliage (background knowledge), low light causing blur; possible VLOS problems in dense or tropical forest.
Tropical: no takeoff space or VLOS under a 30–50 m canopy; pilot needs a clearing or edge; aerial layer covers canopy only.
Research methods for unified aerial-ground GS (Horizon-GS) carry non-commercial licenses and need 80 GB GPUs, so they are not usable on an RTX 3080 Ti 16 GB or in a Hexagon context.
Mobile render budget (about 0.5–1M splats) must be shared between layers, and the aerial layer can crowd out ground detail unless LoD and budget priorities are tuned.

Legal/dissemination: publishing aerial imagery from Swedish drone flights on the web may need a dissemination permit (spridningstillstånd) under the Swedish Act on protection of geographic information (2016:319); this could not be checked (search budget exhausted) and must be confirmed by the regulations research.
open_questions: Web search budget ran out during this research; Swedish dissemination-permit rules (spridningstillstånd) for drone aerial imagery, EU class label of the DJI Avata 360, and the exact CC0 license status of Lantmäteriet orthophoto and laser products are unverified.

For the 2026 handheld-LiDAR + UAV-imagery forest 3DGS paper (Remote Sens. 18(11):1696), the UAV altitude and whether it flew above or below canopy are unknown (full text blocked); per-view quality was not compared with separate layers.

There is no published quantitative study of a merged aerial + under-canopy ground splat in a forest versus separate layers; the forest-specific merge conclusions are inferred from urban evidence plus canopy-occlusion physics.
Actual canopy cover and species mix of the user's Swedish test stand (pine, spruce or birch dominated?) decide how much floor and how many trunks a drone would see.
Whether the BLK2GO's range (around 25 m) captures enough upper-crown points to ICP-register a drone canopy cloud in the Swedish stand, and certainly not in tropical canopies of 30–50 m.
Whether the viewer will offer an 'overview/fly-above' mode at all; if navigation stays at ground level, the aerial layer's visible value drops further.
questions_for_user: Will the viewer allow users to rise above the canopy (overview or fly mode), or is navigation always at walking height within LiDAR ground boundaries? This decides whether an aerial layer is worth building at all.
What dominates the Swedish test stand: Scots pine, Norway spruce or birch? Is it thinned or near a clearing or forest edge where bridging drone shots could be taken?
Is a free aerial context layer from Lantmäteriet open data (ALS point cloud, 1 m DTM, 0.16/0.4 m orthophoto) acceptable as a stand-in for the drone in the Swedish phase?
For the tropical phase, is documenting the canopy top (crowns, gaps, emergent trees) a goal, or only the understory experience? Do you have access to clearings or rivers for takeoff and VLOS?
Is georeferencing (placing the scene on a map, e.g. in LuciadRIA) a requirement? If yes, a drone with RTK/PPK, or ground targets surveyed by GNSS in a clearing, becomes the georeference source.

verdicts.claim: Wallace et al. 2016: UAV SfM gave <1 ground point/m² under denser canopy and a 0.12 m mean terrain difference vs UAV laser scanning (30x50 m eucalypt plot).
verdicts.correction: Confirmed by the abstract. The same abstract also says that both techniques 'are capable of providing information that can be used to describe the terrain surface ... in areas of relatively low canopy closure' and that SfM is 'an adequate low-cost alternative'. This supports the report's nuance for thinned or open Swedish stands. The reference was UAV-ALS, not conventional ALS.

verdicts.claim: Jayathunga et al. 2018: DAP-only R²=0.20 / RMSE 12.34 m where non-ground cover >0.95, vs R²=0.91 / RMSE 1.61 m with a LiDAR DTM.
verdicts.correction: The JAG 2018 abstract (fixed-wing UAV + LiDAR DTM, mixed conifer-broadleaf forest, Hokkaido) and the companion Remote Sensing 10(2):187 abstract both support the direction: DAP needs an accurate external DTM, and performance depends on canopy complexity. Neither abstract contains the specific numbers. The full text was 403, so the numbers are unconfirmed. Use only the qualitative statement.

verdicts.claim: Swinfield et al. 2019 (Maliau Basin, Sabah/Borneo): mapping the ground from SfM is 'often impossible' because rainforest canopy gaps are rare.
verdicts.correction: The quote is verbatim from the abstract. The site is wrong: the paper studies an Indonesian restoration landscape (Harapan Rainforest, Sumatra), not Maliau Basin, Sabah. Additional findings the report omitted: SfM systematically UNDERestimated top-of-canopy height (mean bias about 5 m) against a LiDAR-DTM-referenced model. At multi-hectare scale, SfM and LiDAR TCH were 'very similar even without GCPs', but GCPs were essential for small-scale registration. This supports using targets/GCPs for the tropical aerial layer.

verdicts.claim: Roşca et al. 2018 (Guyana, 650 trees/ha): UAV SfM vs TLS top-of-canopy agreed within 0.5 m on 71–77% of pixels, overestimated gap heights (99th pct +11.42 m), missed small gaps, and showed positive bias over >85% of area in 7 of 14 gaps.
verdicts.correction: All numbers confirmed (Interface Focus 8(2), 2018; 30x40 m plot). Post-harvest the 99th-percentile overestimate grew to +21.10 m. Quote: small gaps 'are completely missed by the UAV TCM'.

verdicts.claim: TreeDGS: Matrice 4E at 70/90 m with obliques, GSD about 1.84 cm, 365 images/plot, loblolly pine plantation, DBH RMSE 4.79 cm; breast-height band 'frequently occluded'; fully occluded stems not recoverable; 20 min GS on RTX 5090 32 GB.
verdicts.correction: All confirmed, including the exact 'frequently occluded by crowns, branches, and understory vegetation' sentence. The report understates one point: aerial 3DGS BEAT a drone-LiDAR baseline (Inertial Labs RESEPI + Hesai XT-32: 7.66 cm → 4.79 cm, about 37.5% lower RMSE) and fitted 189/189 test trees. In open managed pine, oblique drone imagery therefore sees stems better than the report implies. Total per-plot processing was about 83 min (50 min matching + 20 min GS + 13 min fitting) on 32 GB VRAM, so a 16 GB 3080 Ti would need image downscaling. No code release is stated.

verdicts.claim: DRAGON: plain COLMAP registered only about 50% of a drone+ground set; registration succeeds when intermediate-level 'bridge' images exist; DRAGON reaches 97.47%.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed (Table II; quote verbatim).

verdicts.claim: AerialMegaDepth (CVPR 2025): DUSt3R placed <5% of aerial-ground pairs within 5° rotation error, about 56% after fine-tuning.
3DGS intermediate-view matching paper (arXiv 2509.19898): SIFT and SuperGlue gave 0 correct matches on several aerial-ground pairs.
verdicts.correction: Table 6: SIFTGPU 0/27 and 0/0 on pairs 2, 4–7; SuperGlue 0/0 on pairs 4–7. The proposed method recovered 845 correct matches on pair 1.

verdicts.claim: Horizon-GS (CVPR 2025): joint aerial+street training gives conflicting densification and underperforms separate training; needs ContextCapture poses + transitional views; A100 80 GB, about 4 h/scene; Inria non-commercial license; Linux/CUDA research code.
verdicts.correction: The technical claims are confirmed verbatim ('reconstructing either aerial or street views alone has achieved much better results than training them together'; A100 80G; about 4 h; transitional views + ContextCapture). The repo says 'Please follow the LICENSE of 3D-GS', which is the Inria non-commercial license. Correction: the README includes a Windows-specific install step (SET DISTUTILS_USE_SDK=1), so the code is not Linux-only. The license and hardware remain the real blockers.

verdicts.claim: XGRIDS Lixel CyberColor aerial-ground fusion requires RTK fix on both the handheld scanner and the drone, plus vertical 'photo tower' ascents; building case study; about 5 h on RTX 5090/128 GB.
verdicts.correction: E38 says 'Any deviation from an RTK Fixed state will cause compilation failures' and prescribes 3–4 ascent series at 1 s intervals (K1 + Mavic 3E). Heliguy: K1 + Matrice 4E, takeoff/landing shots 'tie the ground scan to the aerial photos', images every metre while climbing to 70 m at building corners, Ryhope Engines Museum, Ryzen 9950X3D + RTX 5090 + 128 GB, about 5 h. The workflow is also tied to XGRIDS scanners (K1/L2), so it is irrelevant for BLK2GO data regardless of RTK.

verdicts.claim: Remote Sensing 18(11):1696 (2026) fused handheld SLAM LiDAR with UAV imagery in one 3DGS forest twin (PSNR 24.94, SSIM 0.773, LPIPS 0.231; DBH R² 0.848, RMSE 2.705 cm) via LiDAR anchors, not joint image matching.
verdicts.correction: Metrics confirmed (Zhou et al., 'LiDAR-Guided Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting for Forest Digital Twins', published 2026-05-24). The abstract qualifies that the results were obtained 'in open-canopy forest environments'. The report omits this, and it limits the result's relevance to dense spruce or tropical stands. UAV altitude is still unknown (MDPI full text returns 403).

verdicts.claim: Casseau/Fallon (IROS 2024): markerless aerial-to-terrestrial forest registration via treetops/stems reaches 0.44 m (Evo, FI) and 0.31 m (Stein am Rhein, CH); dense canopy makes treetop detection harder; combined clouds cover a larger range of tree heights.
verdicts.correction: Numbers and both quotes are confirmed. Two corrections: (1) both clouds are LIDAR. The aerial data is ULS (Velodyne HDL-32E on Avartek Bower / DJI M600) and the ground data is a backpack Hesai XT32. These figures are therefore an optimistic proxy for registering a PHOTOGRAMMETRIC drone canopy (which has noisier gaps and SfM height bias) to BLK2GO data. (2) The arXiv entry has no venue or journal reference; 'IROS 2024' is unsupported.

verdicts.claim: Above/under-canopy ULS registered with targets in Leica Cyclone gave 0.4 cm mean error (Forest Ecosystems 2021, s40663-021-00290-3).
verdicts.correction: The abstract (Wang et al. 2021, 'Seamless integration of above- and under-canopy UAV laser scanning') describes one UAV flight above AND under the canopy, with GNSS-IMU positioning, 2–4 cm DBH RMSE and 4–7 cm stem-curve RMSE. It does not mention target registration in Cyclone or 0.4 cm. The cm-level target claim needs the full text before it is used as a planning number.

verdicts.claim: Spark 2.0 (about 2026-04-15) sorts all SplatMeshes in one global sort, does joint LoD across multiple splat objects under one budget (500K–2.5M), 16M page table, .RAD streaming, SplatMesh.opacity global multiplier, SplatEdit/SDF cropping; MIT.
verdicts.correction: Blog dated 2026-04-14. Quotes confirmed: 'LoD rendering across multiple splat objects simultaneously, traversing multiple trees jointly'; budget 'default 500K – 2.5M depending on your device type'; 'default 16 M splats' page table; opacity is a 'Global opacity multiplier'. MIT license. The repo CDN links reference v2.3.1, so pin a 2.x version. Caveat from the docs: 'The sort order lags the render by at least one frame'. This is relevant for fast height-based fades.

verdicts.claim: PlayCanvas unified rendering sorts all GSplat components together in one global sort; unified since v2.11; budget about 1M mobile / 3M+ desktop.
verdicts.correction: Quote confirmed; the v2.11.0 release notes list the 'Initial implementation of unified gsplat rendering' and a global-sorting example. Budgets confirmed. Not verified: whether unified mode is the default or must be enabled per component. The planner should treat it as possibly opt-in, because non-unified components are ordered per component.

verdicts.claim: mkkellogg GaussianSplats3D is no longer actively developed and points to Spark (MIT).

Finnish autonomous under-canopy drone: 1.15 kg, D435 + Orin NX, 1 m/s, 2.25–2.75 m, 34–42 m flights, 100% / 87.5% success (650 / 2,000 trees/ha), stops from thin dry spruce branches, ATE 0.34–0.50 m, DBH RMSE 3.33 cm, 79% stem completeness.
verdicts.correction: All confirmed. ATE was 0.50 m in the medium stand and 0.34 m in the difficult stand. Trajectories were smooth in 0% of difficult-stand flights. Now peer-reviewed in Int. J. Remote Sensing (2025-12-03, doi 10.1080/01431161.2025.2579803).

verdicts.claim: Krisanski 2020: consumer drone below canopy gave DBH RMSE 1.1–2.1 cm.
verdicts.correction: Eucalyptus forest, 99 stems; RMSE 0.011 m and 0.021 m. Authors note that success depends on operator expertise and that scale must come from somewhere when GPS is unavailable.

verdicts.claim: DJI Avata 360 (2026-03-26): 455 g, 2x 1/1.1-inch, 8K/60 360, 120 MP, omnidirectional sensing + forward LiDAR, prop guards, about 23 min, USD 719 with RC 2; EU class label unverified.
verdicts.correction: DJI's spec page lists 'Class C1 (EU)', which resolves the open question. In the EU it can fly in the Open category A1 with a C1 label (operator registration and the standard online training apply; that part is background knowledge). The Drone Girl says it is 'not officially available in the United States via official websites'. EU pricing was not checked; USD 719 (RC 2) and USD 979 (Fly More) are US third-party figures.

verdicts.claim: Antigravity A1: 249 g (C0), 8K/30 360, front+down sensing only, no prop guards, effective resolution about 2.7K–4K per direction, from USD 1,599.
verdicts.correction: It is C0 ONLY with the standard battery. With the high-capacity battery (291 g) it is EU C1. The reviewer says usable per-direction resolution is about '2.7K or even 1080', so the 4K upper bound is not supported. Sensing is front and down only, and off in Sport mode (confirmed). Bundles: USD 1,599 / 1,899 / 1,999. Launched 2025-12-04.

verdicts.claim: Publishing Swedish drone aerial imagery on the web may need a dissemination permit (spridningstillstånd) under Act 2016:319 (unverified in report).
verdicts.correction: Lantmäteriet (current pages, Oct 2026): a permit is required to 'publicera, sälja eller dela material som avbildar Sverige från luften'. This covers drone photos, video, laser data and elevation data. It is free of charge. Processing currently takes 'cirka 65 arbetsdagar' (about 3 months). Permits are granted only for material actually submitted, and you may then distribute only the returned material and 'skapa följdprodukter' (derivatives, e.g. a splat) from it. Sharing via cloud services you do not fully control counts as dissemination. There is a FOREST exemption, but only if the landowner commissioned the material or was the photographer, there are no vehicles or human activity other than forestry, and there are no power lines. It explicitly does not apply to a 'mer utzoomad vy där omgivningarna syns' (a zoomed-out view that shows the surroundings), and that is exactly the 'context/surroundings' use case. Sea areas need a separate Sjöfartsverket permit. No 2024–2026 rule changes were found on these pages.

verdicts.claim: Lantmäteriet orthophotos became open data on 2025-02-03 (0.16/0.4 m), served via STAC; CC0 assumed.
verdicts.correction: Newsletter nr 2 2025 confirms only that the STAC service 'Ortofoto Nedladdning' has existed since February 2025. Resolution, the exact date and the CC0 license were not on the fetched pages, and the product PDFs did not parse. Lantmäteriet states that its free data follows the EU High-Value Datasets rules, which require CC BY 4.0 or more permissive, so reuse in the viewer is very likely fine. Confirm the license string per product. Because Lantmäteriet itself publishes the data, the dissemination question does not apply to these products.

verdicts.claim: Forest UAV-SfM needs very high overlap: Frey et al. 2018 best at ≥95% forward overlap; 90% forward / 85% side at 120 m (Forests 2024).
verdicts.correction: Frey 2018: best results with overlap >95% AND resolution >5 cm. 'Higher image overlaps and coarser GSDs have a clearly positive influence'. Wind and terrain elevation were the most important environmental factors. Forests 15(12):2135 (thinned Pinus radiata): optimum 90/85 at 120 m; 80 m flights were 'more error-prone' for marginal GSD gain. Dandois 2015: once DTM alignment was accounted for, there were 'no significant differences ... in height error at different levels of lighting, altitude, and side overlap'. The report's lighting emphasis is therefore weaker for geometry; it still matters for splat appearance. These findings contradict the report's 30–70 m AGL protocol (see recommendation_assessment).

verdicts.claim: Tomaštík 2017: photogrammetric terrain usable (<20 cm vertical) only under partially open canopy.
verdicts.correction: Abstract: terrain under 'fully-closed forest canopy' cannot be reconstructed; it can be measured only in gaps or leaf-off. Accuracy was sub-decimetre horizontal and <20 cm vertical. GCP quality matters more than GCP quantity.

verdicts.claim: UAV LiDAR understory DEM: MAE ≤0.17 m, RMSE ≤0.24 m for canopy cover <0.9 (J. Mountain Science 2024).
verdicts.correction: The paper exists ('Impacts of UAV–LiDAR flight altitude and forest canopy on the estimation accuracy of understory terrain', J. Mountain Science), but it is dated 2025, not 2024. The abstract is elided and the full text is behind a Springer login, so the numbers are unconfirmed.

verdicts.claim: RTK under canopy ranges from cm-level to metres ('review of 25 studies').
verdicts.correction: The source is a 2026 MASTER'S THESIS literature review, not a peer-reviewed review. Range: 1.88 cm (RTK rapid-static, Swedish conifer forest) to 34.33 m RMSE. The direction stands; the source tier is low.

verdicts.claim: Iglhaut et al. 2019 review: SfM accurate on visible crowns; main limitation is ground surface.
verdicts.correction: The review exists (Current Forestry Reports 2019). The abstract is broadly positive about SfM and does not state the ground limitation; that point would be in the body, which was not read. Low risk, since Tomaštík and Swinfield independently support it.

verdicts.claim: DJI Zenmuse L2: 5 returns and 4x12 cm spot at 100 m.
verdicts.correction: 5 returns is confirmed. The spot size was not shown on the fetched page. L2 is no longer DJI's newest LiDAR: Zenmuse L3 (1535 nm, up to 950 m at 10% reflectivity, dual 100 MP mapping cameras) is marketed for the Matrice 400 only.

verdicts.claim: Canopy transmittance: Scots pine 0.12–0.89, Sitka spruce 0.04–0.40; Amazon about 96% cover / 4% gap / 5.7% PAR; tropical canopy blocks up to 96% of laser shots, 673 ground returns of >600k.
verdicts.correction: All three sources (ResearchGate, ScienceDirect, GIM International) returned 403. The values are plausible and consistent with the verified Swinfield and Roşca results, but they should be cited as unverified.

missed_developments.claim: The Swedish dissemination permit, not only flight rules, is a schedule-critical constraint for any web-published drone layer (options b and c, and Avata 360 'bridge' shots).
missed_developments.details: A permit takes about 65 working days and is granted only for material that has been submitted. Derivative products may be built only from the returned material, so the aerial splat should be trained on Lantmäteriet-returned images or re-checked. Uploading to cloud services you do not fully control counts as dissemination, so keep processing local (the project already does). The forest exemption (landowner-commissioned or landowner-photographed, no vehicles or non-forestry human activity, no power lines) does NOT cover zoomed-out views showing the surroundings. This rules out using the exemption for the 'context/surroundings' layer. Whether people carrying a BLK2GO count as 'human activity' is unclear. Plan: submit drone imagery right after flying, publish internally (or locally only) in the meantime, and use Lantmäteriet's own open data as the context layer, which needs no permit.

missed_developments.claim: DJI Terra (v5.x) now has built-in 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction, a turnkey way to build the separate aerial splat for option (c).
missed_developments.details: DJI Terra advertises 'Photorealistic Gaussian Splatting'. The trial notes say users who applied before v5.0.0 can reapply for GS, so the feature dates from about v5.0. Not verified: export formats (PLY?), GPU requirements, license limits and whether it handles non-DJI images. It is an alternative to open-source trainers when the drone is a DJI Enterprise model (M4E). Check its export and licensing terms before relying on it.

missed_developments.claim: TreeDGS shows aerial oblique 3DGS outperforming drone LiDAR for DBH in an open managed pine plantation.
missed_developments.details: DBH RMSE was 4.79 cm vs 7.66 cm for a Hesai XT-32 ULS baseline, with 189/189 trees fitted. In thinned Scots pine stands, which are common in Sweden, a drone with obliques may capture more stem and ground content than the report's 'canopy only' framing implies. This raises the value of a test flight at a pine site, but does not change the merge-vs-separate conclusion.

missed_developments.claim: The only forest paper that merges handheld LiDAR + UAV imagery into one 3DGS was validated in OPEN-CANOPY forest only.
missed_developments.details: Zhou et al., Remote Sensing 18(11):1696 (2026-05-24): 'outperforming baseline NeRF and standard 3DGS methods in open-canopy forest environments'. There is no evidence for spruce or tropical stands. This weakens using it as a precedent for option (b) beyond open pine or birch.

missed_developments.claim: A single UAV flying both above and under the canopy has been demonstrated with LiDAR (GNSS-IMU positioned), combining canopy-top completeness with stem completeness.
missed_developments.details: Wang et al. 2021 (Forest Ecosystems): about 0.5 ha in about 10 min, 2–4 cm DBH RMSE. This shows aerial+under-canopy fusion works when a common positioning backbone exists (GNSS-IMU/LiDAR), not through image matching. This matches the report's recommendation to register via geometry or targets rather than joint SfM.

missed_developments.claim: DJI's current drone-LiDAR flagship is the Zenmuse L3 on the Matrice 400, not the L2.
missed_developments.details: Zenmuse L3: 1535 nm, up to 950 m at 10% reflectivity, dual 100 MP RGB, Matrice 400 only. This is a heavy enterprise platform. Its EU category was not checked; from background knowledge, the Specific category is likely (low confidence). If tropical under-canopy terrain is ever needed, budget for this class, or rent L2/L3 survey services.

missed_developments.claim: Leica BLK2FLY was not listed among Leica's current autonomous reality-capture products (low confidence).
missed_developments.details: The Leica laser-scanner product page fetched in Oct 2026 lists BLK360/SE, BLK2GO/PULSE, BLK ARC and RTC, with no BLK2FLY. If it is discontinued, there is no Hexagon-native drone sensor to lean on. Confirm through internal Hexagon channels.

missed_developments.claim: Search coverage limitation.
missed_developments.details: The shared WebSearch budget for this workflow ran out early in this fact-check. Missed-development coverage relied on direct fetches of known URLs, so newer 2025–2026 aerial-ground GS or forest-GS papers may exist that were not found.

verification.recommendation_assessment:
The core recommendations hold: (a) LiDAR + Insta360 for the first Swedish test, the drone as a later optional SEPARATE aerial layer (c), and no merged splat (b). The independently verified evidence agrees. Horizon-GS states that joint training is worse than separate training and needs transitional views, ContextCapture poses, an A100 80 GB and a non-commercial license. DRAGON (about 50% COLMAP registration without bridge images), AerialMegaDepth (<5% of pairs within 5°) and the 3DGS intermediate-view paper (0 correct SIFT/SuperGlue matches) confirm that aerial-ground matching fails. XGRIDS fusion needs an RTK fix on both devices and an XGRIDS scanner, so it cannot be used. The only merged forest result (RS 2026) was LiDAR-anchored and tested only in open canopy. The viewer claims (Spark 2.0 global sort with joint multi-object LoD and SplatMesh.opacity; PlayCanvas global sort) are confirmed.

Changes I would make:
1. Make the Swedish dissemination permit an explicit gate for the drone phase. It is not 'maybe'. Web publication of drone imagery or derived splats needs a Lantmäteriet permit (about 65 working days, free). Only the submitted and returned material may be used for derivative products. The forest exemption does not cover zoomed-out context views, so plan the submission into the schedule. This also strengthens the 'use Lantmäteriet open data as the context layer first' advice, since Lantmäteriet already publishes that data. Verify the per-product license (CC0 vs CC BY 4.0).
2. Correct the capture protocol altitude. '30–70 m AGL' is too low and is stated relative to the wrong reference. Frey 2018 (completeness better with coarser GSD and >95% overlap), Forests 2024 (120 m better than 80 m, 90/85 overlap) and TreeDGS (70/90 m) point to about 70–110 m AGL with ≥90/85 overlap plus obliques. State it as height above canopy top (aim for ≥45–60 m clearance). It is capped by the EU Open-category 120 m limit measured from the ground (background knowledge, high confidence). Over a 30–50 m tropical canopy, 30–70 m AGL would put the drone at or just above emergent crowns, which is unsafe and gives poor SfM.
3. Temper the registration accuracy ladder. The 0.31–0.44 m markerless figures are LiDAR-to-LiDAR (ULS vs backpack). A photogrammetric canopy registered to BLK2GO points will likely be worse, given SfM gap and height bias (Roşca, Swinfield). The '0.4 cm target registration in Cyclone' figure is unverified. Plan for GCP targets in gaps or edges as the primary method, and confirm that the BLK2GO can localise target centres to cm level.
4. Add the TreeDGS nuance. In thinned pine, oblique aerial GS recovered stems better than drone LiDAR, so a pine-site drone pilot may yield more trunk and ground content than 'canopy only'. This raises the value of (c) but does not justify (b).
5. Fix factual slips: Swinfield's site is Sumatra (Indonesia), not Sabah. Antigravity A1 is C1 with the high-capacity battery and about 2.7K/1080p per direction. Avata 360 is EU C1 (confirmed). The Horizon-GS repo has Windows install steps. The GNSS-under-canopy source is a master's thesis. The J. Mountain Sci. paper is from 2025.
6. Viewer: treat PlayCanvas unified mode as something to enable explicitly. Remember Spark's sort lags at least one frame during fast fades.
7. VRAM: '16 GB is enough for a separate aerial splat' depends on image count and resolution. TreeDGS used 32 GB for 365 images, so plan to downscale or tile the aerial training on the 3080 Ti.
8. Optionally mention DJI Terra 5.x built-in 3DGS as a turnkey aerial-layer path if a DJI Enterprise drone is chosen, after checking its export and license terms.

The tropical verdict (aerial layer only for canopy and context; drone LiDAR if terrain under canopy is needed) holds.

research.summary:
TOPIC: how to register drone imagery, or a model built from it, to a BLK2GO scan (local metric frame, no GNSS) and to the Insta360 ground splat. Also covers what this means for the shared coordinate frame and for georeferencing.

BOTTOM LINE: The most reliable way to register a drone model to an under-canopy handheld LiDAR scan is physical. Use shared targets (GCPs) that the drone sees from above and the BLK2GO scans in the same walk. Put them in a clearing, on a forest road or at the forest edge. Use them as control points in the drone bundle adjustment (BA), with coordinates measured directly in the LiDAR cloud. Expected drone-to-LiDAR accuracy is about 2-5 cm at the targets. Drone RTK/PPK is a big help: metric scale, near-cm horizontal placement, fewer GCPs needed, optional world placement. It does not remove the need for shared targets, because the BLK2GO frame has no GNSS. Three other methods should NOT be the primary one, only refinements or fallbacks: marker-free geometric registration (canopy/stems ICP), joint aerial-ground SfM with the Insta360 frames, and consumer-drone GPS alone.

WHY GEOMETRY OVERLAP IS POOR: The BLK2GO has 0.5-25 m range. From the ground it sees the forest floor, stems and the underside of the lower canopy. Drone photogrammetry sees the top of the canopy plus open ground only. UAV-SfM "cannot penetrate the vegetation to reach the ground", and it misses small gaps or overestimates canopy height in them (tropical study, Guyana). So under closed canopy the two clouds show different sides of the crowns, and ICP on them is biased or fails. Overlap really exists only in clearings, on tracks and at forest edges. Even LiDAR-to-LiDAR marker-free aerial-terrestrial registration in boreal/mixed forest reaches only 0.26-0.61 m point-to-point error (Casseau et al., IROS 2024, ALS vs MLS). Canopy-shape registration of UAV-LiDAR to TLS gives about 0.24 m RMSE (Forests 2025). Photogrammetry sees no stems, so expect the same or worse. Joint SfM of aerial and ground images is a hard open problem. Baseline DUSt3R localizes fewer than 5% of aerial-ground pairs within 5 degrees; fine-tuning on AerialMegaDepth lifts this to about 50-56% (CVPR 2025). That was on buildings; repetitive forest foliage would be worse. It needs bridging views: low oblique orbits at a clearing edge, or the 360 camera on a tall pole.

GNSS FACTS:
- Consumer drones without RTK: about 2.5 m horizontal and 4.5 m vertical RMSE with GPS only (Mini 4 Pro benchmark).
- DJI 'AbsoluteAltitude' / EXIF GPSAltitude on non-RTK drones is barometric and can be 5-50 m off. RelativeAltitude is about ±3 m.
- RTK drones such as the Matrice 4E (built-in RTK, C2, about €4,599) and the Mavic 3E with RTK module are specified at 1 cm + 1 ppm horizontal and 1.5 cm + 1 ppm vertical. RTK drones write ellipsoidal heights, not EGM96, unless the Pilot 2 ASL option is used.
- XMP RtkFlag: 50 = fixed, 34 = float, 16 = single point, 0 = none. Use only images with RtkFlag 50.
- In practice RTK-only blocks are about 2-4 cm horizontal but carry vertical bias. A Phantom 4 RTK study found up to 0.14 m vertical shift, removed by a single GCP, and vertical RMSD of 6-10 cm without GCPs.
- Sweden: SWEPOS network RTK costs 12,000 SEK/yr, 5,000 SEK per 90 days, 2,000 SEK per 30 days, or 5,000 SEK for 1,000 minutes. There is a free 10-day trial, and daily RINEX files are free for PPK. HxGN SmartNet also covers Sweden.
- Under forest canopy, even multi-GNSS RTK degrades to about 0.5-2 m. GCPs must be surveyed in the open or tied in through the LiDAR.

ALIGNMENT CHAIN (adds to the planned ground alignment):
- Existing edge: T_groundSfM->LiDAR, a Sim(3) from trajectory, hand-eye and ICP.
- New edge: T_droneSfM->LiDAR. Make it SE(3) with a scale check if the drone is RTK/PPK, otherwise a full Sim(3). Estimate it from shared targets, ideally inside a GCP-constrained BA (OpenSfM/ODM, Metashape, Leica Infinity). COLMAP has no GCP term in BA, so with COLMAP use pose priors plus a post-hoc Umeyama fit on triangulated target centres.
- Optional edge: T_LiDAR->World, a rigid fit with scale held at 1. Get it either from RTK-rover-surveyed target centres or from target coordinates taken out of the RTK drone model.
- Weakest links, in order: (1) features or targets that both sensors can see (they must be in openings); (2) BLK2GO SLAM drift between the plot and the clearing targets (spec 6-15 mm relative, unproven in forest); (3) drone vertical bias and datum/height-reference confusion (SWEREF 99/ETRS89 vs WGS84/ITRF is about 0.9 m in 2026; ellipsoid vs EGM96 vs RH 2000 heights differ by tens of metres); (4) doming in nadir-only blocks (add 20-35 degree obliques); (5) canopy moving in wind, and leaf or season changes between captures.
- Expected accuracy per step:
  - Target centre in BLK2GO: about 1-2 cm (low confidence).
  - Target in drone images: 0.5-1 px, about 1 cm at 1-1.5 cm GSD.
  - Drone BA with GCPs: about 2 cm horizontal, 3-4 cm vertical.
  - Drone-to-LiDAR at checkpoints: about 3-5 cm.
  - Marker-free: 0.2-0.6 m.
  - GPS only: metres. A non-RTK drone cannot place the LiDAR at all without targets.

GEOREFERENCING (optional): Keep the LiDAR local frame as the working frame W. Store one optional T_W->ECEF (EPSG:4978) together with its CRS and epoch metadata (SWEREF 99 TM EPSG:3006 + RH 2000 EPSG:5613 via the SWEN17_RH2000 geoid, 8-10 mm uncertainty). That 4x4 matrix becomes the 3D Tiles root.transform for Cesium (CesiumJS 1.139+ streams KHR_gaussian_splatting) and the georeference for LuciadRIA. Do the math in float64 and keep local coordinates small. With no LiDAR, W = local ENU from the drone RTK, or an approximate ENU from GPS priors flagged 'low-accuracy'. With splat only, W is the arbitrary SfM frame flagged 'unscaled' unless the user gives a scale bar. The same targets also let the ground splat register to the drone frame when LiDAR is absent.

PRACTICAL: Put 4-6 targets in the first LiDAR + Insta360 test anyway. They cost little, give independent checkpoints for the ground splat-to-LiDAR alignment, and prepare for the drone phase.

findings.claim: Under closed canopy the geometry the drone and the BLK2GO both see is minimal. Usable overlap is limited to clearings, tracks, forest edges and stems at edges.
findings.details: UAV-SfM cannot penetrate vegetation to reach the ground and cannot render a DTM directly. UAV top-of-canopy models overestimate canopy height in gaps (0.19-13.83 m differences) and miss small gaps entirely (tropical forest, Guyana, 650 trees/ha). The BLK2GO range is 0.5-25 m, so from below it sees floor, stems and the underside of the lower canopy, and does not see crown tops in tall forest. ICP of drone canopy against BLK2GO canopy compares opposite sides of the crowns, so the result is biased or wrong.

findings.claim: Marker-free aerial-terrestrial forest registration is decimetre-level at best, even with aerial LiDAR. With drone photogrammetry, expect the same or worse.
findings.details: Casseau et al. (IROS 2024) matched ALS canopy-height-model peaks to MLS stem centres with a deformable pose graph in a Finnish boreal forest and a Swiss mixed forest. Point-to-point error after optimization was 0.26-0.61 m. Dense forest made treetops hard to separate, and some tiles failed to match. A rough GNSS prior (5-10 m) was used to crop the search. Canopy-shape UAV-LiDAR/TLS registration: average RMSE 0.24 m vs 0.18 m for manual registration (Forests 2025). Photogrammetry does not see stems, so stem-based matching works only at edges.

findings.claim: Joint aerial-ground SfM, with drone and Insta360 frames in one reconstruction, is unreliable and should not be the primary registration path.
findings.details: AerialMegaDepth (CVPR 2025): baseline DUSt3R localizes fewer than 5% of aerial-ground pairs within 5 degrees rotation error. Fine-tuning on pseudo-synthetic aerial plus real ground data raises this to about 50-56%, and that was in urban scenes. Sky2Ground (2026) confirms that large altitude differences degrade pose estimation. In forests, repetitive foliage and canopy occlusion make it worse. Classical SIFT/COLMAP matching across nadir and ground views is not expected to work without bridging views (low oblique orbits at a clearing edge, or the 360 camera on a 5-8 m pole). That last point is background knowledge.

findings.claim: Consumer, non-RTK drone GNSS is metre-level and cannot register to the GNSS-less BLK2GO frame on its own.
findings.details: DJI Mini 4 Pro, GPS only, 61 m AGL: checkpoint RMSE 2.5 m horizontal, 4.5 m vertical. With 6 GCPs surveyed by RTK and a local base, RMSE drops to 2.0 cm H and 2.8 cm V; with DIY GCPs, 8.1 cm H and 7.1 cm V (blog benchmark, May 2026). The BLK2GO has no GNSS, so drone GPS gives orientation, approximate scale and world placement of the drone model only. It cannot place the LiDAR without shared targets or manual correspondences.

findings.claim: DJI altitude metadata is a trap. On non-RTK drones 'AbsoluteAltitude' and EXIF GPSAltitude are barometric and can be 5-50 m off. RelativeAltitude is about ±3 m. RTK drones write ellipsoidal (WGS84) heights, not EGM96.
findings.details: DJI XMP namespace drone-dji: GpsLatitude, GpsLongitude, AbsoluteAltitude, RelativeAltitude, GimbalYaw/Pitch/RollDegree, FlightYaw/Pitch/RollDegree, RtkFlag, RtkStdLon, RtkStdLat, RtkStdHgt, DewarpData (lens calibration). Barometric drift is about 1-2 m per 30 min, with steps at battery swaps. DJI FAQ: RTK aircraft record geodetic (ellipsoid) height relative to WGS84, not EGM96/2008. DJI Pilot 2 has an ASL option that writes EGM96 heights instead, so check the setting. Metashape and COLMAP read EXIF GPSAltitude by default.

findings.claim: RtkFlag values: 0 = no positioning, 16 = single point, 34 = RTK float, 50 = RTK fixed. DJI says not to use images with flag other than 50 directly for mapping.
findings.details: Filter or down-weight images at ingest using RtkFlag and RtkStd*. Feed the per-image std values into the ODM geo.txt accuracy columns or the COLMAP pose-prior covariance.

findings.claim: RTK drones give about 2-4 cm horizontal accuracy without GCPs, but vertical bias of 5-15 cm is common. One or more GCPs or checkpoints remain necessary.
findings.details: Matrice 4E and Mavic 3E RTK spec: 1 cm + 1 ppm H, 1.5 cm + 1 ppm V. Peer-reviewed Phantom 4 RTK study (nadir, 110 m): RTK-only horizontal RMSD 3.8 cm, vertical RMSD 6-10 cm, with a systematic 0.14 m vertical shift at the rural site that one GCP reduced to about 2 cm. GCP-only: about 1.9 cm H, 3.4-3.7 cm V. A blog example: RTK-only vertical RMSE 13.9 cm with +9.2 cm bias, vs 3.8 cm with GCPs.

findings.claim: RTK and PPK-capable drones in the right class: DJI Matrice 4E (built-in RTK, EASA C2, about €4,599 at an EU retailer, 4/3-inch 20 MP mechanical-shutter wide camera) and Mavic 3 Enterprise with RTK module. Consumer Mini, Air and Mavic Pro drones have no RTK or PPK.
findings.details: M4E: 49 min flight time, 1219 g. M4E and M3E log PPKRAW/.obs, .nav and Timestamp.MRK for PPK in DJI Terra, Emlid Studio, Propeller or Leica Infinity. Leica Infinity (v3.6.1+) post-processes DJI GNSS tracks, does UAV photogrammetry with GCP residual reports, and v4.3.1 supports the DJI Mavic 4. Infinity is a Hexagon tool the user may already have.

findings.claim: Swedish RTK infrastructure is available and cheap at project scale: SWEPOS network RTK, free RINEX for PPK, and HxGN SmartNet.
findings.details: SWEPOS Nätverks-RTK: 12,000 SEK per year per subscription (1-3 subscriptions), 5,000 SEK per 90 days, 2,000 SEK per 30 days, a 5,000 SEK 'pott' of 1,000 minutes valid 12 months, and a free 10-day trial for new customers. Daily RINEX files are free with an account. The post-processing subscription (virtual RINEX and Beräkningstjänsten) is 1,000 SEK per year per user. HxGN SmartNet (Hexagon) also covers Sweden.

findings.claim: RTK GNSS degrades badly under forest canopy, so GCPs must be surveyed in open-sky locations or tied in through the LiDAR.
findings.details: Review (Geodetski list): autonomous GNSS errors reach 15-30 m under dense canopy, and multi-GNSS RTK reports about 0.5-2.03 m. Fixed solutions can be rare under canopy. Vertical error is about twice horizontal, and error grows with canopy density and basal area. Put targets where the sky is open, which is also where the drone can see them.

findings.claim: Datum and epoch pitfall: SWEPOS RTK coordinates are SWEREF 99 (ETRS89) even when EXIF labels them 'WGS84'. ETRS89 vs WGS84/ITRF differs by about 0.8-0.9 m in Europe and grows about 2.5 cm per year.
findings.details: Mixing RTK (ETRS89) data with standard-GNSS or ITRF-based data, or with Cesium's WGS84 globe, causes a horizontal offset just under 1 m. Heights: SWEN17_RH2000 converts SWEREF 99 ellipsoidal heights (EPSG:4377 ellipsoidal) to RH 2000 (EPSG:5613) with 8-10 mm uncertainty. Projected CRS: SWEREF 99 TM (EPSG:3006). The project manifest must record CRS and epoch.

findings.claim: COLMAP (4.2.1, Sept 2026) uses GPS as pose priors and geo-registers with model_aligner, but it has no native GCP term in bundle adjustment.
findings.details: COLMAP extracts EXIF GPS during feature extraction. The data is used for spatial matching and stored as pose priors. The command 'colmap pose_prior_mapper --overwrite_priors_covariance --prior_position_std_x/y/z' weights the priors in incremental mapping (default std 1 m), and 3.13 made it robust to outlier priors. 'colmap model_aligner --ref_images_path f.txt --ref_is_gps 1 --alignment_type ecef|enu|plane --alignment_max_error 3.0' fits a Sim(3) to at least 3 camera centres. 4.0 integrated GLOMAP as global_mapper. 4.1 added spherical (equirectangular) cameras, the Caspar GPU BA backend and position priors in absolute pose refinement. 4.2 added gravity priors from EXIF orientation and multi-component global mapping. GCP alignment needs a custom step: triangulate target observations, then Umeyama/RANSAC Sim(3), or custom BA via pycolmap/pyceres. That step is background knowledge.

findings.claim: OpenDroneMap and OpenSfM support GCPs natively in bundle adjustment and accept per-image position accuracy. ODM also has an experimental --align to a reference LAS/LAZ or DEM.
findings.details: gcp_list.txt: a header line with PROJ string, EPSG code or 'WGS84 UTM zone', then rows of 'geo_x geo_y geo_z im_x im_y image_name [gcp_name]'. Recommended: at least 5 GCPs (8-10 for large areas), each in at least 5 images. geo.txt: 'image geo_x geo_y [z] [yaw pitch roll] [horz_acc vert_acc]' overrides EXIF with RTK-quality data. --force-gps combines high-precision image GPS with GCPs. OpenSfM uses GCPs both in the alignment step and as BA constraints. Feeding LiDAR-frame target coordinates under a local projection makes the drone model land directly in W. That use is untested and background knowledge.

findings.claim: Target sizing and layout: the target should be at least 5-10x the GSD (Pix4D AutoGCP needs at least 5x GSD; other Pix4D guidance says 20x). Use at least 5 GCPs spread over the area, each in at least 5 images. GCP survey accuracy finer than GSD/10 adds nothing.
findings.details: At 1-1.5 cm GSD the minimum is 10-15 cm. Recommend 40-60 cm black/white checker (2x2 or diagonal) rigid boards, also so the BLK2GO gets enough points for a plane fit and can see the intensity contrast. Intensity at B/W transitions in LiDAR is distorted. Retro-reflective material gives uniform high-intensity returns. Raising the board 10-20 cm off the ground, or adding a sphere, helps LiDAR segmentation and centre fitting (background knowledge). Keep at least 2 targets out of the solution as independent checkpoints.

findings.claim: Nadir-only drone blocks with self-calibration produce doming. Adding 20-35 degree oblique images greatly reduces it, which matters for a GCP-light registration.
findings.details: James & Robson 2014: doming comes from near-parallel views combined with mis-estimated radial distortion. Obliques can cut DEM error by up to two orders of magnitude without control. Higher overlap plus 20-35 degree obliques improved precision and accuracy by about 50% vs nadir-only.

findings.claim: Validation must use independent checkpoints. Internal and hold-out self-consistency does not detect globally coherent distortion.
findings.details: A 2026 arXiv paper shows hold-out self-validation stays at confidence 1.00 while true errors vary 14x, and misses coherent distortion. Report checkpoint RMSE (H, V, 3D) on targets not used in the fit, M3C2/C2C distances on the true overlap (clearing ground, edge stems), the scale ratio, and loop consistency between drone->LiDAR and drone->groundSfM->LiDAR.

findings.claim: BLK2GO accuracy that bounds the chain: range noise ±3 mm, relative accuracy 6-15 mm (SLAM), absolute about 20 mm indoors. Outdoor forest drift over a loop that reaches a clearing is unspecified.
findings.details: Targets in a clearing tie the drone to the LiDAR only near the clearing. Inside the plot, alignment quality depends on BLK2GO SLAM consistency. Close the loop and walk past each target.

findings.claim: Leica Cyclone REGISTER 360 PLUS has an Applied Control workflow (control file plus labelled targets, auto B&W and sphere target detection) and imports BLK2GO data. It is not documented whether control works on BLK2GO kinematic imports.
findings.details: The rcdocs pages describe Apply Control with target labelling and Smart Label, and residual viewing on the AppliedControl object. The georeferencing workflow in Cyclone FIELD 360 is documented for the RTC360 only. Plan a Python, CloudCompare or Cyclone 3DR fallback for picking targets and fitting the transform.

findings.claim: World placement for Cesium and Luciad reduces to one 4x4 local-to-ECEF matrix. Cesium now streams Gaussian splats in 3D Tiles via KHR_gaussian_splatting.
findings.details: Khronos released KHR_gaussian_splatting as a release candidate in Feb 2026 (ratification targeted for Q2 2026). The first CesiumJS implementation was 1.139, with hierarchical LOD splats in 3D Tiles as of Apr 2026. Put T_W->ECEF in tileset root.transform and keep tile content in local float32 coordinates. The root.transform mechanism is background knowledge.

recommendations.recommendation: Frame design: make the BLK2GO/Cyclone local frame the working frame W whenever LiDAR is present. Model all sources as nodes in a frame graph whose edges carry a Sim(3) 4x4 matrix with scale, a covariance or RMSE, the method used and a validation report. Store one optional T_W->ECEF (EPSG:4978) with CRS and epoch metadata (e.g. SWEREF 99 TM EPSG:3006 + RH 2000 EPSG:5613). Fallbacks: no LiDAR -> W = local ENU at the drone-RTK origin; drone without RTK -> ENU from GPS priors flagged low-accuracy; splat only -> SfM frame flagged 'unscaled' unless the user enters a known distance.
recommendations.rationale: The BLK2GO has no GNSS, so the LiDAR frame is the only metric frame common to the main use case. World placement is a separate, optional edge, so the viewer works without it and Luciad/Cesium can use it when present. Keeping provenance on each edge lets the UI show alignment quality per source.
recommendations.alternatives: Use SWEREF 99 TM or ECEF as the working frame. Rejected as the default: large coordinates cause float32 jitter, and it would require GNSS for every project.

recommendations.recommendation: Primary drone-to-LiDAR registration: shared physical targets. Use 5-8 rigid 40-60 cm B/W checker boards, slightly raised, in a clearing, track or forest edge next to the plot, spread in plan. The BLK2GO walks past each one in the same loop. Measure the target centres in the LiDAR cloud with a plane fit plus intensity or sphere centre, and use these W-frame coordinates as GCPs in a GCP-constrained drone BA (ODM/OpenSfM, Metashape or Leica Infinity). With COLMAP, use pose priors, then triangulate the targets, then a robust Umeyama Sim(3). Keep at least 2 targets as checkpoints.
recommendations.rationale: This is the only method with cm-level expected accuracy (about 2-5 cm) that does not depend on canopy geometry overlap or on GNSS under canopy. It needs no world survey at all.
recommendations.alternatives: Marker-free stem/CHM matching (0.2-0.6 m, fails in dense canopy). Drone GPS only (metres, and cannot place the LiDAR). Joint aerial-ground SfM (low success rate).

recommendations.recommendation: If the drone phase goes ahead, choose an RTK/PPK-capable drone (e.g. DJI Matrice 4E with built-in RTK, C2, about €4.6k, or a Mavic 3E with RTK module). Fly with SWEPOS network RTK (30-day at 2,000 SEK, or the 1,000-minute pot at 5,000 SEK), or do PPK with the free SWEPOS RINEX. Use only images with RtkFlag=50 and include 20-35 degree obliques. Use a consumer drone only with at least 5 targets and a full Sim(3) fit.
recommendations.rationale: RTK gives metric scale, about 2-4 cm horizontal placement, robustness when only a few targets are visible, and optional georeferencing. Obliques reduce doming. Vertical bias of 5-15 cm still requires at least 1-2 targets or checkpoints.
recommendations.alternatives: Consumer drone (Mini or Air class) with GPS priors and full GCP control: cheaper, but scale and absolute accuracy depend entirely on the targets.

recommendations.recommendation: Make georeferencing optional, in one of two ways. (a) Survey the target centres with an RTK rover (e.g. a Leica GS18 through Hexagon, on SWEPOS or SmartNet) in open sky, then fit T_LiDAR->world as a rigid transform with scale fixed at 1, checking the free-scale residual. (b) Without a rover, take the target coordinates from the RTK drone model. Convert with pyproj (SWEN17_RH2000 grid) and record whether coordinates are ETRS89 or ITRF.
recommendations.rationale: This gives the ECEF placement Luciad and Cesium need at 2-5 cm (rover) or about 5-15 cm vertical (drone RTK only). It avoids the 0.8-0.9 m ETRS89/WGS84 error and height-reference errors of tens of metres.
recommendations.alternatives: Skip georeferencing and show the model in a local Cartesian reference. This is fine for the first tests.

recommendations.recommendation: Use ICP and other geometric methods only as a gated refinement after the target-based solution. Run Open3D point-to-plane ICP restricted to cropped overlap (clearing ground, edge stems) with a small max correspondence distance (0.1-0.2 m). Accept the correction only if it is smaller than the target-based uncertainty and checkpoint RMSE does not get worse.
recommendations.rationale: Canopy geometry seen from above and from below does not correspond. Unconstrained ICP converges to biased solutions under canopy.
recommendations.alternatives: FPFH+RANSAC global registration, or tree-position graph matching, as a coarse fallback when there are no targets (expect 0.2-0.6 m).

recommendations.recommendation: Treat joint aerial-ground SfM, with drone and Insta360 frames in one model, as an experimental extra rather than the registration backbone. If tried, add bridging captures (low 5-20 m oblique orbits at the clearing edge, or the 360 camera on a 5-8 m pole) and learned matchers. Use the result only as a consistency check against the target-based drone->LiDAR transform.
recommendations.rationale: State-of-the-art aerial-ground pose estimation succeeds on only about 50% of pairs after special fine-tuning, in urban scenes. Forests are harder.
recommendations.alternatives: Register the drone and ground models separately to W through the targets. This is recommended.

recommendations.recommendation: Put 4-6 of the same targets in the FIRST LiDAR + Insta360 test, without a drone.
recommendations.rationale: They give independent checkpoints for the planned ground Sim(3)/ICP alignment, test target detection in the BLK2GO cloud and in 360 frames, and rehearse the drone-phase protocol at almost no cost. The drone itself still stays a later phase.
recommendations.alternatives: Validate the ground alignment only through ICP fitness and visual overlay. Weaker, because self-consistency misses coherent errors.

recommendations.recommendation: Validation report for every registration edge: checkpoint RMSE (H, V, 3D) on held-out targets; residuals of the targets used; scale ratio |s-1| (expect less than 0.001 with RTK); M3C2/C2C distances on the true overlap (CloudCompare); stem-centre residuals at edge trees; loop consistency drone->W vs drone->groundSfM->W where available. Show a quality badge per layer in the viewer.
recommendations.rationale: Hold-out and internal consistency cannot certify accuracy. Independent checkpoints and overlap distances are the evidence that counts.
recommendations.alternatives: None adequate.
