risks: No co-visible features or targets: if the plot has no clearing, track or edge, the drone cannot be tied to the BLK2GO better than 0.2-0.6 m (marker-free), or at all with photogrammetry under closed tropical canopy.

BLK2GO SLAM drift between the clearing (where the targets are) and the plot interior. The drone model is accurate at the targets, but the error grows inside the plot. Outdoor forest drift is unspecified.

Datum and height-reference mix-ups: SWEREF 99/ETRS89 labelled as 'WGS84' (about 0.9 m offset in 2026); DJI barometric AbsoluteAltitude (5-50 m errors); ellipsoidal vs EGM96 vs RH 2000 heights (tens of metres); the Pilot 2 ASL option changing what is written to EXIF.
Drone RTK vertical bias of 5-15 cm when there are no GCPs or checkpoints. Doming in nadir-only blocks.
RTK rover cannot fix under canopy (0.5-2 m errors), so world-surveyed GCPs are possible only in the open.
Joint aerial-ground SfM can fail silently or produce wrong poses (low success rate, repetitive foliage). It must not be the source of truth.
Unconstrained ICP of the drone canopy surface against the BLK2GO under-canopy returns converges to biased solutions.
Canopy moving in wind and foliage or lighting changes between drone and ground captures add noise to canopy-based registration and to the splat.
Target detection in BLK2GO data: intensity distortion at B/W edges, sparse points at range, ground clutter. Needs testing.
Cyclone Applied Control may not support BLK2GO kinematic data. A custom Python/CloudCompare path is needed.
License risks: ODM is AGPL; learned aerial-ground matchers (DUSt3R/MASt3R family) are likely non-commercial.
Float32 precision jitter if world (ECEF/SWEREF) coordinates are used directly in the viewer instead of a local frame plus a 4x4 transform.
open_questions: How large is BLK2GO SLAM drift in a forest loop of about 50-100 m that includes a clearing? Measure it with checkpoint targets in the first test.
Is the BLK2GO/Cyclone LAS export gravity-aligned (z-up from the IMU)? If yes, the drone-to-LiDAR fit is effectively 4-DoF plus scale, and the target layout can be smaller. Not verified.
Does Cyclone REGISTER 360 PLUS Applied Control or auto target extraction work on BLK2GO kinematic imports, or must target centres be picked in Python or CloudCompare?
How accurately can 40-60 cm checker boards be located in BLK2GO clouds (intensity vs geometry)? Is a sphere or raised-board design needed?
Can ODM/OpenSfM take GCPs in an arbitrary local (non-georeferenced) frame cleanly, or must a fake projected CRS be used? Not verified.
How were aerial-ground splat datasets such as Horizon-GS co-registered in practice? Not verified: the web-search budget ran out before this could be checked.
Does tropical canopy leave any usable gaps within reach of the BLK2GO (25 m range) for shared targets?
questions_for_user: Must the project be placed on a world map (Luciad/Cesium ECEF/SWEREF 99), or is a local LiDAR-frame model enough for now?
Can you borrow an RTK GNSS rover (e.g. a Leica GS18) and a SWEPOS or HxGN SmartNet login through Hexagon?
Can the test plot be chosen next to a clearing, forest road or forest edge where 5-8 targets are visible from the air and reachable on the BLK2GO walk?
If a drone is bought or borrowed, is an RTK-capable enterprise model (e.g. Matrice 4E, about €4.6k) acceptable, or must it be a consumer model?
Will you put 4-6 checker targets in the first LiDAR + Insta360 test, as checkpoints and as a rehearsal for the drone phase?

verdicts.claim: Under closed canopy, drone photogrammetry and the BLK2GO share very little geometry. UAV-SfM cannot reach the ground, overestimates gap heights by 0.19-13.83 m and misses small gaps (Guyana, 650 trees/ha).
verdicts.correction: The paper says verbatim that 'the UAV-SfM cannot penetrate the vegetation to reach the ground and so cannot render a DTM directly'. It reports mean gap-height excess of 0.19-13.83 m over TLS in 14 gaps, and says small gaps (G3, G2, G11) were 'completely missed'. Interface Focus 2018, central Guyana, 650 trees/ha with DBH >10 cm. The point that ICP would compare opposite sides of the crowns is the researcher's inference, but it is sound.

verdicts.claim: Casseau et al. (IROS 2024): marker-free ALS-to-MLS forest registration reaches 0.26-0.61 m point-to-point error after optimization, using a 5-10 m GNSS prior.
verdicts.correction: Numbers per mission, before -> after: Evo1 0.64->0.61, Evo2 0.28->0.26, Evo3 0.39->0.31, Evo4 0.36->0.37 (slightly worse), SaR1 0.78->0.39, SaR2 0.47->0.41 m. Manual validation RMSE was 0.21-0.41 m (Evo) and 0.24-0.26 m (SaR). The GNSS prior was 'about 5 m to 10 m'. Caveats: (1) these are ALS-MLS cloud point-to-point errors, not checkpoint RMSE. (2) The aerial sensor was LiDAR (Velodyne/drone ALS), which sees through the canopy. Photogrammetry would do worse, so treating these numbers as a best case is correct.

verdicts.claim: Canopy-shape UAV-LiDAR/TLS registration gives about 0.24 m RMSE (Forests 2025), against 0.18 m for manual registration.
verdicts.correction: Yu, Tang, Zhang, Dai, Cai, 'Automatic Registration of Terrestrial and UAV LiDAR Forest Point Clouds Through Canopy Shape Analysis', Forests 16(8):1347, 19 Aug 2025. The abstract gives 'an average registration accuracy of 0.24 m within 5.14 s'. The 0.18 m manual figure could not be checked (MDPI returned 403). This is LiDAR-to-LiDAR, not photogrammetry.

verdicts.claim: AerialMegaDepth (CVPR 2025): baseline DUSt3R localizes fewer than 5% of aerial-ground pairs within 5 degrees, and fine-tuning raises this to about 50-56%, in urban scenes.
verdicts.correction: The abstract says 'fewer than 5%' rising to 'nearly 56%'; quote 56%, not a 50-56% range. The data came from city-wide meshes (Google Earth) plus MegaDepth ground images, so it is urban. The repo shows no license, which is stricter than 'unverified'. It builds on DUSt3R/MASt3R, and MASt3R is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (confirmed). Treat it as non-commercial or all-rights-reserved.

verdicts.claim: Sky2Ground (2026) confirms that large altitude differences degrade pose estimation.
verdicts.correction: Wang et al., arXiv 2603.13740, CVPR 2026. It benchmarks MASt3R, DUSt3R, MapAnything and VGGT, and finds that satellite imagery 'often degrades performance'. Its SkyNet model improves RRA@5 by 9.6 and RTA@5 by 18.1 points absolute. The scenes are not forest.

verdicts.claim: Consumer non-RTK drone (Mini 4 Pro) benchmark: GPS-only 2.5 m H / 4.5 m V RMSE; with surveyed GCPs 2.0 cm H / 2.8 cm V; with DIY GCPs 8.1 / 7.1 cm.
verdicts.correction: The numbers match the blog (29 May 2026), but it is not a single benchmark. The article says its numbers 'are drawn from published field studies and documented operator tests' and that the methodology is 'representative'. Use it as indicative, low-to-medium confidence. The conclusion that consumer GPS cannot place the GNSS-less BLK2GO frame is still right; that follows from first principles.

verdicts.claim: DJI altitude metadata: on non-RTK drones AbsoluteAltitude/GPSAltitude is barometric and 5-50 m off; RelativeAltitude is about ±3 m; baro drift is 1-2 m per 30 min; RTK drones write WGS84 ellipsoidal heights, not EGM96; Metashape and COLMAP read EXIF GPSAltitude by default.
verdicts.correction: The DJI FAQ confirms that RTK aircraft record 'geodetic height (commonly known as ellipsoid height)', WGS84 by default, and not EGM96/2008. The other figures are weaker. '5-50 m' and '1-2 m/30 min' come from an uncited community page (PhotogrammetryCommunity, CC-BY). The 'barometric' attribution there quotes Agisoft support saying 'I assume it's a barometric altitude', so it is an assumption, not a DJI statement. Agisoft's own article says Metashape reads XMP AbsoluteAltitude first and falls back to EXIF, so 'Metashape reads EXIF GPSAltitude by default' is wrong. The Pilot 2 ASL option was not verified. The practical advice (do not trust absolute height, use RelativeAltitude plus a takeoff ellipsoidal height, or RTK) still holds.

verdicts.claim: RTK status codes: 0 none, 16 single, 34 float, 50 fixed. DJI says not to use images whose flag is not 50 directly for mapping.
verdicts.correction: The DJI FAQ gives these codes for column 13 of the Timestamp.MRK file and states 'When the flag of a photo is not 50, it is not recommended to use this photo directly for mapping.' The XMP RtkFlag tag uses the same codes (ExifTool lists RtkFlag, RtkStdLon, RtkStdLat and RtkStdHgt as XMP-drone-dji tags). Prefer the MRK file over XMP for PPK.

verdicts.claim: RTK-only drone blocks reach about 2-4 cm horizontal but carry 5-15 cm vertical bias. Phantom 4 RTK study (110 m, nadir): H about 3.8 cm, V 6-10 cm, a 0.14 m shift reduced to about 2 cm by one GCP, GCP-only about 1.9 cm H and 3.4-3.7 cm V.
verdicts.correction: Štroner et al., Sensors 2020. RTK-only vertical RMSD was 0.060 m (urban) and 0.103 m (rural). The rural systematic shift of 0.144 m fell to 0.020 m with a single GCP. GCP-only vertical was 0.034 m; RTK+GCP combined was 0.029 m. Horizontal RTK-only was 0.038 m (X) and 0.023 m (Y). The authors call RTK without external verification 'potentially very dangerous'. A real Matrice 4E field test (Texas, Aug 2026, blog) also fits: RTK-only 3.4 cm H and 13.9 cm V RMSE with +9.2 cm bias; with 5 GCPs, 2.4 cm H and 4.1 cm V.

verdicts.claim: DJI Matrice 4E: built-in RTK, EASA C2, about €4,599 at an EU retailer, RTK fix 1 cm + 1 ppm H / 1.5 cm + 1 ppm V, 1219 g, 49 min, 4/3-inch mechanical-shutter wide camera.
verdicts.correction: The DJI M4 FAQ says the RTK module 'is not removable', i.e. built in, and that the series is 'C2 certified by EASA'. Spec page: 1 cm + 1 ppm H, 1.5 cm + 1 ppm V; ±0.5 m GNSS hover; 1219 g; 49 min; 4/3 CMOS; mechanical shutter 2-1/2000 s. The retailer price today is €4,561, in stock. The Mavic 3 Enterprise is still offered on DJI's site; its RTK is an add-on module.

verdicts.claim: SWEPOS network RTK costs 12,000 SEK/yr, 5,000 SEK per 90 days, 2,000 SEK per 30 days, or 5,000 SEK for 1,000 minutes, with a 10-day free trial. Daily RINEX is free; the post-processing subscription is 1,000 SEK/yr.
verdicts.correction: All prices match Lantmäteriet. Daily RINEX files are free but need a user account. The 1,000 SEK/yr per user post-processing subscription covers Beräkningstjänsten, virtual RINEX and hourly/daily RINEX. An IoT card is included only with the annual subscription and the minute pot.

verdicts.claim: RTK GNSS degrades badly under forest canopy: autonomous GNSS 15-30 m, multi-GNSS RTK about 0.5-2.03 m.
verdicts.correction: Popovici et al. 2026, a structured critical review in Geodetski list. The authors call the ranges 'indicative, not statistically aggregated estimates'. The conclusion (survey targets in the open or tie them in through the LiDAR) stands.

verdicts.claim: SWEREF 99 (ETRS89) vs WGS84/ITRF is about 0.8-0.9 m and grows about 2.5 cm/yr. SWEN17_RH2000 converts SWEREF 99 ellipsoidal heights to RH 2000 with 8-10 mm uncertainty.
verdicts.correction: Lantmäteriet (primary): 'WGS 84 och SWEREF 99 avviker för närvarande (2024) 8–9 dm ... ökar med några centimeter per år'. SWEREF 99 has internal epoch 1999.5 and plate-tectonic epoch 1989.0. SWEN17_RH2000 is the current official geoid (NKG2015 fitted to SWEREF 99/RH 2000), with 8-10 mm uncertainty on the mainland and 2-4 cm in the mountains. The PROJ grid se_lantmateriet_SWEN17_RH2000.tif is CC0 and links EPSG:5613 and EPSG:4377. The NovAtel source could not be fetched (403), but the Lantmäteriet page supersedes it.

verdicts.claim: COLMAP 4.2.1 (Sept 2026) uses GPS as pose priors (pose_prior_mapper, default std 1 m), geo-registers with model_aligner (at least 3 images, ecef/enu/plane), has no GCP term in BA, and integrated GLOMAP in 4.0, spherical cameras and Caspar in 4.1, and gravity priors from EXIF plus multi-component global mapping in 4.2.
verdicts.correction: Mostly right. 4.2.1 was released 2026-09-29. Gravity pose priors from EXIF orientation came in 4.1.0, not 4.2; 4.2.0 added multi-component global mapping and made gravity rotation averaging robust to 180-degree flips. 4.1.0 added Caspar GPU BA and the position prior in RefineGeneralizedAbsolutePose. The FAQ documents model_aligner with alignment_type ecef or ENU only ('plane' is not in the FAQ and needs checking against --help). Pose priors debuted in 3.11.0 (2024-11-28). No GCP functionality appears in the FAQ or changelog, which supports the claim that BA has no GCP term.

verdicts.claim: ODM/OpenSfM support GCPs natively in BA, geo.txt with per-image accuracy and --force-gps, and ODM has an experimental --align to a reference LAS/LAZ or DEM.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed: the gcp_list header accepts PROJ, EPSG or 'WGS84 UTM 16N'; rows are 'geo_x geo_y geo_z im_x im_y image_name [gcp_name]'; ODM recommends at least 5 GCPs, each in at least 5 images. geo.txt has optional horz/vert accuracy columns. --force-gps uses EXIF GPS even when GCPs are present. OpenSfM uses GCPs in both alignment and BA. But --align does not fit this project. The source (opendm/align.py) uses NGA's CODEM with DSM-based coarse registration plus ICP fine registration, reads the CRS of both inputs (so both must be georeferenced), and sets DSM_SOLVE_SCALE=False and ICP_SOLVE_SCALE=False. A BLK2GO local-frame LAS has no CRS, and an under-canopy LiDAR DSM does not match a drone canopy-top DSM. Neither ODM nor OpenSfM docs mention arbitrary local or topocentric GCP coordinates, so a fake projected CRS with an offset would be needed (untested).

verdicts.claim: Target sizing: at least 5-10x GSD, with Pix4D AutoGCP needing at least 5x GSD and other guidance saying 20x; at least 5 GCPs, each in at least 5 images; GCP accuracy finer than GSD/10 adds nothing.
verdicts.correction: The attribution is swapped. Pix4D's general GCP guidance says 5-10x GSD. Pix4D AutoGCP (automatic detection) says 'a minimum of 20 times the average GSD', with a target diagonal of about 20 px (e.g. 50 cm at 2.5 cm GSD). For automated detection at 1-1.5 cm GSD, plan at least a 30 cm diagonal; the proposed 40-60 cm boards are fine. 'At least 5 GCPs x 5 images' and 'no more accurate than GSD/10' are confirmed. On the LiDAR side, Routescene says vegetation has reflectivity similar to white paint and recommends retro-reflective material and raised targets. B/W contrast may therefore not show up in BLK2GO intensity against foliage. The 'intensity distortion at B/W transitions' claim comes from the ResearchGate TLS paper, which was not checked.

verdicts.claim: BLK2GO accuracy: range 0.5-25 m, range noise ±3 mm, relative 6-15 mm (SLAM), absolute about 20 mm indoors; outdoor forest drift unspecified.
verdicts.correction: The cited ATG page lists range 'Min. 0.5 - up to 25 m', range noise '+/- 3 mm' and absolute accuracy '+/- 10 mm' indoor. It has no 6-15 mm relative or 20 mm absolute figure, and no outdoor spec. Leica's own spec pages returned 403, so the 6-15 mm/20 mm figures are unverified here. 'No outdoor or forest drift spec' is confirmed.

verdicts.claim: Cyclone REGISTER 360 PLUS has Applied Control and imports BLK2GO data; it is undocumented whether control works on BLK2GO kinematic imports; Field 360 georeferencing is documented for the RTC360 only.
verdicts.correction: The BLK2GO support page covers importing walks, WayPoints, panoramas, trajectory and GeoTags, and says nothing about targets or control. The Apply Control page describes the AppliedControl object and its control-to-Bundle errors, but names no target types or scanner restrictions; the auto B&W/sphere detection claim is not shown on that page. Field 360 georeferencing needs an RTC360 with firmware 7.0. Keep this low confidence and plan a Python/CloudCompare fallback.

verdicts.claim: KHR_gaussian_splatting is a release candidate (Feb 2026, ratification targeted for Q2 2026). The first CesiumJS implementation was 1.139, and LOD splats in 3D Tiles arrived in Apr 2026.
verdicts.correction: Stale. The Khronos glTF registry README now reads 'Complete, Ratified by the Khronos Group'; the Feb 3, 2026 press release was the RC announcement. CesiumJS CHANGES.md: 1.135 (2025-11-03) 'Removed support for KHR_spz_gaussian_splats_compression in favor of ... KHR_gaussian_splatting and KHR_gaussian_splatting_compression_spz_2'. Support therefore dates from 1.135, not 1.139. The current version is 1.146 (2026-10-01). The Cesium blog of 27 Apr 2026 confirms splat tilesets in CesiumJS and splats being added to the proposed 3D Tiles 2.0, and gives no version number. The root.transform mechanism is standard 3D Tiles and fine.

verdicts.claim: A 2026 arXiv paper shows hold-out self-validation stays at confidence 1.00 while true errors vary 14x, and misses coherent distortion.
verdicts.correction: Asadi, 'Hold-Out Self-Validation Cannot Certify Photogrammetric Accuracy...', arXiv 2607.24852 (v1 25 Jul 2026, final 3 Sep 2026). It reports a 14.1x swing at confidence 1.00, and globally distorted models that were 55-106 m wrong at confidence 1.00. It is a single-author preprint, not peer reviewed. The recommendation to use independent checkpoints does not depend on it.

verdicts.claim: Leica Infinity v3.6.1+ post-processes DJI GNSS tracks, and v4.3.1 supports the DJI Mavic 4.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed: v3.6.1 (article of 14 Mar 2022) imports DJI GNSS data and images, post-processes the kinematic track and updates camera positions; the article names the Phantom 4 RTK and M300 RTK. Not verified: v4.3.1, Mavic 4 support, and Matrice 4E/Mavic 3E PPK support in Infinity. The Mavic 4 Pro is a consumer drone, so any 'support' would be image import, not RTK/PPK. Leica's imaging page confirms UAV photogrammetry with GCP measurement and QA reports. Ask Hexagon whether Infinity handles M4E MRK/PPKRAW files.

verdicts.claim: HxGN SmartNet (Hexagon) also covers Sweden.
verdicts.correction: The SmartNet services and coverage pages fetched say only 'worldwide' and offer a Swedish UI language; no country list was readable. Confirm through Hexagon or Leica Sweden. SWEPOS alone is enough.

verdicts.claim: Adding 20-35 degree obliques reduces doming by up to two orders of magnitude without control (James & Robson 2014) and improves precision and accuracy by about 50% (rs11030239).
verdicts.correction: Both publisher pages (Wiley, MDPI) returned 403, and the search budget was used up. This is consistent with the widely cited doming literature, so keep the recommendation and mark the exact numbers as unverified.

missed_developments.claim: Sweden requires a dissemination permit (spridningstillstånd) from Lantmäteriet to share, publish or sell drone imagery. The report does not mention it, and it directly affects putting drone-derived splats or clouds into a web viewer.
missed_developments.details: Lantmäteriet: 'Om du har fotograferat eller filmat från luftfartyg som till exempel drönare ... och vill dela, publicera eller sälja dina bilder behöver du ansöka om spridningstillstånd'. Spreading without a permit 'kan vara straffbart'. The requirement covers 'flygfoton, videor, laserdata, höjddata med mera', so derived 3D data is likely covered. Applying is free, but processing currently takes about 65 working days. Forest land is exempt only if the landowner ordered the material or was the photographer, and the images 'får inte innehålla fordon eller andra mänskliga aktiviteter förutom sådant som tillhör skogsbruket'. All exemptions fall away if the image shows surrounding areas sensitive for national defence. Consequences for the plan: (1) get landowner commissioning, or apply about 3 months before publishing; (2) the operator with the BLK2GO, vehicles and possibly the targets may count as human activity; (3) keep drone data private or local until cleared. Ground-only BLK2GO/Insta360 data is not aerial and is not covered.

missed_developments.claim: In the EU a C2 drone such as the Matrice 4E can fly in subcategory A3 with only the A1/A3 online training, which suits remote forest test flights. A2 rules (A2 CofC, 30 m or 5 m from people) apply only when flying near people.
missed_developments.details: Regulation (EU) 2019/947 UAS.OPEN.040(4) allows class C2 (with active remote ID and geo-awareness), C3 and C4 drones, and privately built drones under 25 kg, in A3. A3 requires at least 150 m horizontal distance from residential, commercial, industrial or recreational areas. Note that marked recreational areas or trails in a forest could count. The EASA page confirms A2 for C2: a remote pilot certificate of competency, 30 m from uninvolved people (5 m in low-speed mode), and a 120 m AGL limit, with the rules applying since 1 Jan 2024. No 2024-2026 amendment was found, but the search budget was exhausted.

missed_developments.claim: ODM's experimental --align is CODEM DSM-based coarse registration plus ICP with scale fixed at 1, and it requires georeferenced (CRS-tagged) inputs. It is not a usable drone-to-BLK2GO registration path under canopy.
missed_developments.details: opendm/align.py calls codem.coarse_registration (DSM), then codem.fine_registration (ICP), reads get_point_cloud_crs and get_raster_crs from both inputs, and sets DSM_SOLVE_SCALE=False and ICP_SOLVE_SCALE=False. A Cyclone local-frame LAS has no CRS, and a BLK2GO 'DSM' under canopy is understory or lower crown, not the canopy top that drone SfM sees. At most it could work in clearings, after the LAS has been given a fake projected CRS.

missed_developments.claim: How Horizon-GS co-registered aerial and ground views, an open question in the report: SfM in commercial ContextCapture, plus added 'transitional views'.
missed_developments.details: Horizon-GS (arXiv 2412.01745, CVPR 2025): 'we utilize a powerful commercial software, ContextCapture to enhance the performance of the structure-from-motion (SfM) technique' and 'we include transitional views to increase image overlap'. Depth scale and offset were fitted to the SfM points. No RTK or manual alignment is mentioned. This supports the report's bridging-view advice, and shows that even the best-known aerial-ground splat work used commercial SfM and extra captures, in non-forest scenes.

missed_developments.claim: KHR_gaussian_splatting is now ratified, and CesiumJS has supported it since 1.135 (Nov 2025). The current CesiumJS is 1.146 (Oct 2026).
missed_developments.details: This affects the georeferenced-delivery path. A splat in glTF/3D Tiles with root.transform = T_W->ECEF is now a stable standard path rather than a release-candidate bet.

missed_developments.claim: Target design for the BLK2GO: vegetation is as reflective as white paint at LiDAR wavelengths, so B/W checker contrast may not separate targets from foliage in intensity. Use retro-reflective material and raised targets.
missed_developments.details: Routescene: 'Background vegetation has a similar (high) reflectivity to white material so we need something better'. Retro-reflective returns stay 'more uniform regardless how far you fly'. Its 60 cm raised targets get 200-300 hits each. For dual-use drone and BLK2GO targets, use a B/W photogrammetric pattern on top (for the camera) with a retro-reflective element or a raised plane or sphere geometry (for the LiDAR), and validate detection in the first ground-only test.

verification.recommendation_assessment:
The core recommendations hold up: the LiDAR local frame as W, plus an optional T_W->ECEF with CRS and epoch, and shared physical targets in a clearing, edge or track as the primary drone-to-LiDAR tie. So do the three other placements: RTK/PPK as an aid rather than a substitute, marker-free ICP only as gated refinement, and joint aerial-ground SfM as experimental. None of the load-bearing evidence was refuted. Casseau (0.26-0.61 m, ALS-MLS), Forests 2025 (0.24 m), AerialMegaDepth (<5% -> ~56%), Štroner 2020 (0.06-0.10 m RTK-only vertical, a 0.14 m shift fixed by 1 GCP), the DJI RtkFlag codes and ellipsoidal heights, SWEPOS prices and the SWEREF 99/WGS84 offset of 0.8-0.9 m (Lantmäteriet primary source) were all confirmed. Several marker-free numbers come from LiDAR-to-LiDAR work, so they are optimistic bounds for photogrammetry, as the report says.

Changes I would make:
(1) Add the Swedish spridningstillstånd as a hard gate for publishing any drone-derived layer. It is free but takes about 65 working days. Forest is exempt only if the landowner commissioned the material and no non-forestry human activity or vehicles are visible. Until it is cleared, drone layers stay local or private. This is a schedule risk for option (b) or (c) and does not affect the first LiDAR + Insta360 test.
(2) Drop ODM --align from the toolbox for this use. It needs CRS-tagged inputs, matches DSMs with scale fixed at 1, and fails conceptually under canopy.
(3) GCP-in-local-frame is still unproven for ODM/OpenSfM. Plan to run SfM with drone priors and then a custom robust SE(3)/Sim(3) fit on triangulated target centres (pycolmap/pyceres), or use Metashape/Infinity local coordinates. Test ODM with a fake projected CRS only as an option.
(4) Target design: size boards at least 20x GSD on the diagonal if auto-detection is wanted (the Pix4D AutoGCP attribution in the report was swapped). Add retro-reflective or geometric features for the BLK2GO, because white paint does not contrast with vegetation in LiDAR intensity. Validate detection in the first ground test, which the report already recommends.
(5) Update the stale facts. KHR_gaussian_splatting is ratified; CesiumJS has supported it since 1.135 and is now at 1.146. COLMAP EXIF gravity priors came in 4.1, not 4.2. Metashape reads XMP AbsoluteAltitude, not EXIF GPSAltitude. BLK2GO absolute accuracy on the cited page is ±10 mm indoor, and the 6-15 mm/20 mm figures are unverified. The Mini 4 Pro numbers are a compilation, so treat them as indicative.
(6) Regulation: a C2 Matrice 4E may fly in A3 with only A1/A3 training at least 150 m from residential or recreational areas. Remote forest test flights therefore do not need the A2 CofC.
(7) Leica Infinity PPK support for the M4E and HxGN SmartNet coverage of Sweden are unverified; ask Hexagon internally.

The drone-to-LiDAR accuracy estimate of 2-5 cm near the targets is plausible but rests on an unverified BLK2GO target-centre accuracy and unknown forest SLAM drift, so keep it at medium-to-low confidence until the first test measures checkpoint residuals.

Note: the shared web-search budget ran out early in this check, so checking relied on direct fetches of primary URLs. The doming/oblique figures (Wiley/MDPI 403), the Forests 2025 manual-registration figure, the DJI Pilot 2 ASL option and Leica's own BLK2GO datasheet could not be checked.

research.summary:
Scope: drone capture protocol, drone class, and processing load on an RTX 3080 Ti laptop (16 GB) for a ~10x10 m forest plot (larger tropical plots later). Note: the shared WebSearch budget ran out partway through, so a few late items (Autel specs, whether BLK2FLY is still sold, EUR prices, the US FCC status of DJI) were not verified. They are flagged as low confidence.

1) What the drone can contribute to a 10x10 m plot. At 30-40 m above the canopy, one 24 mm-equivalent 4:3 frame covers about 1.44D x 1.08D (D = camera-to-canopy distance), roughly 45-58 m x 33-43 m. So the whole plot fits in one image. Grid coverage is easy. What matters is angular diversity, and most of the plot floor is hidden by canopy. Splat-oriented guidance agrees that nadir-only flights give poor splats. You need oblique crosshatch passes plus multi-altitude, variable-radius orbits (WebODM docs: "a nadir-only flight usually yields very poor results"; Pix4D; MipMap; ESRI). Overlap targets for splats are at least 80/70, with 85/80 for best quality. Forest photogrammetry needs more. Pix4D says at least 85% front and 70-85% side for dense vegetation and recommends flying higher. Frey et al. 2018 got the best forest reconstruction completeness with more than 95% overlap and GSD coarser than 5 cm. Dandois et al. 2015 tested 20-80 m above canopy: canopy-height error doubled when forward overlap dropped, and accuracy needed more than 80% overlap. Recommended protocol for a small plot (about 300-550 stills, about 15-30 min of flying, 1-2 batteries):
- Nadir crosshatch at canopy+40-60 m over a 60-100 m AOI, 85-90/75-80 overlap.
- Oblique crosshatch at -45°.
- 2-3 orbits around the plot centre at a 5° step (72 photos per ring), for example R≈20 m @ canopy+15 m with gimbal -50°, R≈35 m @ +30 m with -40°, and R≈50 m @ +45 m with -30°.
- A bridge sequence: a vertical "elevator" ascent and descent in the nearest gap or at the forest edge, with photos every 1-2 m from about 2 m up to canopy+10 m, plus slow near-horizontal passes (-10 to -20°) along the edge facing in. This copies heliguy's M4E + XGRIDS fusion workflow, which used images every 1 m during the ascent plus takeoff/landing shots for ground-to-aerial registration.

Under-canopy flight is not advisable. DJI vision sensing does not reliably detect branches thinner than about 2-3 cm, and the pilot has to keep visual line of sight from a clearing.

2) Stills versus video, and camera settings. Prefer stills in 12 MP mode on Mini and Air models:
- faster readout (Air 3S under 16 ms at 12 MP versus 20-30 ms at 50 MP; Mini 3 Pro 26 ms versus 60 ms)
- the 2 s minimum interval applies only at 12 MP; at 48/50 MP the minimum is 5 s
- smaller files.

Use DJI Fly waypoints with hover-and-shoot (up to 200 waypoints, hover 0-30 s) or a slow interval-timer flight (1-3 m/s), which makes rolling shutter irrelevant. The M4E's mechanical shutter (up to 1/2000 s) and 0.5 s interval matter only for fast, large-area grids, for example the later tropical plots.

Video (4K at 130-150 Mbps, about 1 GB/min, 8.3 MP frames, H.265 compression, no per-frame EXIF GPS, only SRT telemetry) is acceptable for a quick first test with frames extracted at 1-2 fps, but stills are better.

Settings:
- Manual exposure, ISO 100-400, shutter at least 1/1000 s when moving (at least 1/500 s when hovering).
- White balance fixed in Kelvin; focus locked; HDR/SmartPhoto modes off; 4:3 aspect, uncropped.
- JPEG is enough. JPEG+DNG is useful if you want to match colour with the Insta360.
- Distortion correction OFF (DewarpFlag=0), so the SfM lens model sees unaltered optics. Never mix corrected and uncorrected images.

Fly within the same overcast window as the ground walk, directly before or after it (within 30-60 min), with wind at the canopy below about 3-4 m/s. Dandois found clear sky gives slightly deeper canopy penetration (18% vs 16%), but diffuse light is better for matching appearance with under-canopy 360 video (the under-canopy NeRF paper, WACV-W 2026). Sequence the drone and ground captures so the ground operator does not appear in the aerial frames.

3) Drone class. What matters, in order:
(1) Automated missions: MSDK support, or DJI Fly waypoints/KMZ.
(2) A sensor of about 1 inch with fast readout, or a mechanical shutter.
(3) C0/C1 class for easy paperwork.
(4) RAW and manual exposure.
(5) RTK is optional. The BLK2GO has no GNSS, so RTK only georeferences the aerial layer. GCPs/targets in canopy gaps or the LiDAR geometry still tie it to the LiDAR frame.

Candidates:
- Budget: DJI Mini 4 Pro (C0, under 249 g). It is the only current Mini on MSDK v5, so Dronelink (full virtual-stick grids and orbits) and Litchi Pilot work. Alternatively the DJI Mini 5 Pro (C0 with the standard 249.9 g battery, C1 with the Plus battery; 1-inch 50 MP; forward LiDAR). It has no MSDK, so you use DJI Fly waypoints plus KMZ through Pixpro (about €5/month) or Litchi Hub.
- Mid: DJI Air 3S (C1, 724 g, 1-inch 50 MP plus 70 mm tele, 45 min). Dronelink supports it in onboard-waypoint mode only.
- Pro and tropical: DJI Matrice 4E (C2, 1219 g, 4/3 20 MP mechanical shutter, 0.5 s interval, integrated RTK, Smart 3D/oblique, MSDK, 49 min, about $5,000-5,400).
- Overkill for this: Mavic 4 Pro (C2, 1063 g, 100 MP). The Mavic 3E is being phased out.
- Non-DJI: Autel EVO II Pro V3 / RTK V3 (C2 by firmware, about $3k with RTK). Parrot ANAFI Ai is ageing and Pix4Dcapture has been terminated. Leica BLK2FLY is no longer listed on Leica's autonomous-capture page; check internally at Hexagon.

Regulations: Swedish operator registration and A1/A3 online training apply. A3 rules require 150 m from residential areas and a 120 m ceiling. Publishing aerial images or 3D models of Swedish land on the web needs a Lantmäteriet spridningstillstånd (dissemination permit). It is free, and there is a forest exemption when the landowner commissioned or took the imagery. Derived 3D models of approved material need no separate review.

4) Data and compute.
- File sizes (estimates): about 4-8 MB per JPEG at 12 MP, 7-12 MB at 20 MP, 15-25 MB at 48-50 MP. DNG is about 24 MB (12 MP), 40 MB (20 MP) and 70-100 MB (48-50 MP). So a plot is about 2-4 GB as JPEG, 12-50 GB with DNG, and about 1 GB per minute of 4K video.
- SfM: COLMAP downsizes to 3200 px for SIFT by default.
- Training: INRIA 3DGS auto-rescales images wider than 1.6K. Train aerial images at 1600-2000 px.
- VRAM: INRIA keeps every image on the GPU as float32 by default (about 23 MB per 1600x1200 image, so 300 aerial images ≈ 6.9 GB). Use --data_device cpu, or gsplat, which loads from disk or host RAM. On 16 GB, Gaussian count dominates: gsplat measured 5.6 GB for 3.24M Gaussians (default) and 2.0/5.0 GB for 1M/3M with MCMC; OpenSplat states about 2 GB per million. A ground plus aerial merged model should be capped at about 4-6M Gaussians (MCMC cap). Under a fixed cap, aerial context takes budget away from ground detail, and the much larger scene extent changes densification scaling. This is a compute argument for option (c): separate models, each with its own budget.
- Training time: roughly 30-60 min per 30k iterations on the laptop GPU (inferred from A100 and RTX 3060/4070 figures).
- ODM/ODX: OpenDroneMap is AGPL-3.0, runs natively on Windows or in Docker, and uses the GPU only for SIFT (about 2x faster). GPU on Windows effectively needs the Docker/WSL2 image. RAM scales with image count: about 16 GB for 250 images and 32 GB for 500. Since April 2026, WebODM (AGPL-3.0, free installer v3.3.0) has split off to its own ODX engine and exports splat training data for OpenSplat (AGPL-3.0). Use it as an external process for aerial ortho, DSM, CHM and splat layers.

Overall: keep the first test as LiDAR + Insta360. Add the drone later as option (c), a separate aerial layer, and capture the bridge images so a merge can be tried later if wanted.

findings.claim: Nadir-only drone imagery gives poor Gaussian splats. Splat capture needs oblique crosshatch passes plus multi-altitude, variable-radius orbits.
findings.details: WebODM docs: 'Gaussian splatting requires oblique and/or orbit shots... A nadir-only flight, usually yields very poor results.' PIX4Dmatic: a nadir-only reconstruction 'can degrade significantly moving away from this viewing direction'. It recommends double grids, orbits at varying altitudes and angles, and helix patterns, and says to minimise sky. MipMap (Jun 2026) recommends multi-tier variable-radius orbits plus 'crosshatch oblique grids combined with targeted orbital fill-shots'. 3dgsviewers and aerocartwright (Apr 2026) say the same.

findings.claim: Overlap targets: at least 80/70 for splats and 85/80 for best quality. Forests need more: Pix4D says at least 85% front and 70-85% side; Frey 2018 found more than 95% best for completeness.
findings.details: MipMap: minimum 80% front, 70% side. thefuture3d M4E workflow (Apr 2026): 80/70 minimum, 85/80 for highest quality, GSD ≤3 cm. Pix4D dense vegetation: at least 85% frontal and side overlap, and fly higher so vegetation features match. Frey et al. 2018 (Remote Sensing 10:912): best forest reconstruction completeness with overlap >95% and GSD >5 cm, so higher overlap and coarser GSD both helped. Dandois et al. 2015 tested 20/40/60/80 m above canopy: canopy-height error doubled when forward overlap decreased, and accurate canopy height (RMSE about 3 m against LiDAR) needed >80% overlap.

findings.claim: For a 10x10 m plot a single frame covers the whole plot from canopy+30-40 m. Coverage is trivial; the hard parts are angular diversity and bridging to ground images.
findings.details: Computed for a 24 mm-equivalent 4:3 camera: HFOV ≈71.6°, VFOV ≈56.8°. Footprint ≈1.44D x 1.08D, where D is camera-to-canopy distance. At D=40 m that is about 58 x 43 m. GSD (computed from sensor specs): M4E/M3E 20 MP ≈ D/37 cm (0.8 cm at 30 m); Mini 5 Pro or Air 3S in 12.5 MP mode ≈ D/27 cm; Mini 4 Pro 12 MP ≈ D/28 cm. Altitude AGL = canopy height + D. Swedish canopy is about 15-30 m, so a nadir grid flies at about 60-90 m AGL. Tropical canopy is 30-50 m with emergents above that, so 80-110 m. Both stay under the 120 m limit. Heights are background knowledge.

findings.claim: Bridge images (vertical ascent at the forest edge or in a gap, plus takeoff/landing shots) are what working aerial-ground splat fusions use. Direct aerial-to-ground matching with off-the-shelf methods mostly fails.
findings.details: heliguy (Jul 2025): M4E plus XGRIDS Lixel K1 fusion used an ortho flight at 30 m (two perpendicular flights), Smart Oblique at 70 m, manual triggers every 1 m during ascent to 70 m at building corners, and takeoff/landing shots for ground-to-aerial registration. Both devices needed an RTK fix. Processing took 5 h on an RTX 5090 with 128 GB RAM. AerialMegaDepth (CVPR 2025): aerial-ground registration success (rotation error <5°) was about 5% for off-the-shelf DUSt3R/MASt3R and about 56% after fine-tuning. arXiv 2509.19898 needs rendered intermediate views to get aerial-ground matches. Sky2Ground (2026): large altitude gaps degrade pose estimation.

findings.claim: Stills in 12 MP mode beat 48/50 MP mode on consumer DJI drones for photogrammetry or splats: faster readout, shorter minimum interval, smaller files.
findings.details: Air 3S readout: <16 ms at 12 MP, 20-30 ms at 50 MP (Pixpro, Nov 2024). Mini 3 Pro: 25-26 ms at 12 MP, 60-61 ms at 48 MP (ODM community, Feb 2024). Pixpro on the Mavic 4 Pro: avoid high-resolution modes for moving capture. Minimum interval: Mini 4 Pro, Mini 5 Pro and Air 3S are 2 s at 12 MP and 5 s at 48/50 MP. Pixpro: shoot full-resolution uncropped 4:3; 16:9 does not work. Pixpro Mini 5 Pro test: '12 megapixels is the practical choice for consistent grid capture'. Example: 25 ms readout at 3 m/s gives 7.5 cm of skew, so fly slowly or hover-and-shoot.

findings.claim: Video is usable for splats but worse than stills. COLMAP does not model rolling shutter, and video adds H.265 compression, about 8 MP frames and no per-frame EXIF GPS.
findings.details: Mini 4 Pro records 4K at up to 150 Mbps and the Mini 5 Pro up to 130 Mbps, about 1 GB per minute. 'Gaussian Splatting on the Move' (ECCV 2024) notes COLMAP does not handle rolling shutter efficiently. Their deblur/rolling-shutter compensation needs VIO velocities. Postshot-style guidance: 4K 30/60 fps, slow steady motion. aerocartwright: standard drone JPEG is fine and RAW is not needed. ODM parses DJI video telemetry (SRT); fixed in ODM 3.6.x.

findings.claim: Turn DJI in-camera distortion correction OFF so SfM gets the raw optics (DewarpFlag=0). Never mix corrected and uncorrected images.
findings.details: Pix4D says photogrammetry software works better with original images without correction algorithms applied. Its camera database parameters are for the raw lens, and DJI-dewarped images can cause processing problems and inaccuracy. With correction off, the EXIF DewarpFlag is 0. For COLMAP this means an OPENCV/RADIAL model estimates the distortion. A dewarped image only approximately fits a pinhole model, and a mixed set breaks shared intrinsics (inferred).

findings.claim: Camera settings for drone splat capture: manual exposure, ISO 100-400, shutter at least 1/1000 s when moving, fixed white balance; mechanical shutter on the M4E/M3E.
findings.details: thefuture3d M4E workflow: mechanical shutter, ISO 100-400, shutter 1/1000 or faster, fixed daylight white balance. MipMap troubleshooting: for blur, increase shutter speed or reduce flight speed. Mini and Air models have a fixed f/1.8 aperture, so 1/1000 s at ISO 100-400 is easy under overcast. Do not use ND filters, because they force slower shutters. Lock focus and disable HDR/SmartPhoto modes so frames stay consistent (background knowledge).

findings.claim: Lighting: use diffuse or overcast light, fly the drone back-to-back with the ground walk, keep wind low. Clear sky gives slightly deeper SfM canopy penetration but hurts appearance consistency with the under-canopy capture.
findings.details: Dandois 2015: canopy penetration was significantly lower on cloudy days (16% vs 18%). Wind was a major factor that made overlap uneven. Under-canopy NeRF paper (arXiv 2601.22861, WACV-W 2026): 'performs best under diffuse light (overcast or twilight)'. Direct sun forces a trade-off between overexposed foliage and underexposed ground, and they suggest a GSD of about 1-2 cm. 3dgsviewers: avoid wind that moves trees. Insta360 under-canopy video also needs diffuse light, which is why the two captures should share the same overcast window.

findings.claim: Mission-planning support varies by model. The Mini 4 Pro is the only current consumer DJI on MSDK v5, which gives full third-party automation. Mini 5 Pro, Air 3S and Mavic 4 Pro rely on DJI Fly waypoints and KMZ workarounds.
findings.details: MSDK v5 supported products: Matrice 4E/4T/4D/4TD, M300/M350, M30, Mavic 3E/3M, Mini 4 Pro, Mini 3/3 Pro. Not supported: Mini 5 Pro, Air 3S, Mavic 4 Pro. Dronelink: Mini 4 Pro has full virtual-stick support (mapping, orbits, facades) with RC-N2 and Android since Mar 2025. Air 3/3S and Mavic 4 Pro are onboard-only. Mini 5 Pro needs an unofficial APK. Litchi Pilot supports Mini 4 Pro and M4E; Mini 5 Pro, Air 3S and Mavic 4 Pro go through Litchi Hub with DJI Fly. DJI Fly Waypoint Flight: up to 200 waypoints, Take Photo action, hover 0-30 s, gimbal tilt per waypoint, no grid/mapping tool, no KML import on Mavic 4 Pro, Mavic 3 or Air 3/3S. Pixpro Waypoints (from €5/month) builds grids, multi-grids and orbits as KMZ that replace a placeholder DJI Fly mission. It shoots with the interval timer and supports Mini 4 Pro, Mini 5 Pro, Air 3/3S and Mavic 3/4 Pro.

findings.claim: Current EU drone specs and class labels relevant to this choice.
findings.details: Mini 4 Pro: <249 g, C0, 1/1.3-inch 48 MP, 34 min (45 min Plus), omnidirectional vision plus 3D infrared. Mini 5 Pro: 249.9 g, C0 with standard battery and C1 with Plus battery, 1-inch 50 MP, up to 52 min (Plus), omnidirectional vision plus forward LiDAR, 12 m/s wind, 42 GB storage. Air 3S: 724 g, C1, 1-inch 50 MP wide plus 1/1.3-inch 48 MP 70 mm, 45 min, forward LiDAR. Mavic 4 Pro: about 1063 g, C2, 4/3 100 MP, 51 min, no mechanical shutter. Mavic 3E: 1050 g, C2, 4/3 20 MP, mechanical shutter 8-1/2000 s, 0.7 s interval, 45 min, optional RTK. Matrice 4E: 1219 g, C2, 4/3 20 MP with mechanical shutter 2-1/2000 s (electronic to 1/8000), 0.5 s interval, JPEG/DNG 5280x3956, 49 min, RTK 1 cm+1 ppm H / 1.5 cm+1 ppm V. Multiple dealers say M4E RTK is integrated and non-removable; DJI's spec page is ambiguous. M4E is about $5,000-5,400 and is called the new standard; the Mavic 3E is being superseded.

findings.claim: Non-DJI options exist but are weaker fits: Autel EVO II Pro (RTK) V3, Parrot ANAFI Ai, Skydio. Leica BLK2FLY no longer appears on Leica's autonomous-capture product page.
findings.details: Autel EVO II V3 gained the C2 label by firmware (Open A2/A3 from 1 Jan 2024). The RTK V3 supports RTK and PPK, uses Autel Explorer mapping, costs about $2,999 with RTK, and has a 1-inch 20 MP sensor. Dronelink support for Autel EVO II is unofficial. Parrot ANAFI Ai: 48 MP, 4G, about $4-5k. Pix4Dcapture has been terminated, and Dronelink does not support Parrot. ANAFI UKR is a defence product at $16-22k. Leica's 'autonomous reality capture' page lists RTC360, BLK360, BLK2GO, BLK2GO PULSE and BLK ARC, but not BLK2FLY (fetched Oct 2026). It is probably discontinued; not verified. Skydio X10 is not assessed because of the search limit.

findings.claim: EU/Swedish rules for test flights: register as operator, do A1/A3 training for C1/C2, fly A3 away from people and below 120 m with visual line of sight. Publishing aerial images or 3D models of Swedish land needs a Lantmäteriet dissemination permit (free; forest exemption possible).
findings.details: EASA Open category: A3 means 150 m horizontal from uninvolved people and urban areas and below 120 m AGL. C0/C1 can fly in A1, C2 in A2 with an A2 certificate of competency, and any class in A3 with A1/A3 training. Sweden: Transportstyrelsen operator registration is about 150 SEK for 3 years (secondary source). The spridningstillstånd covers all airborne images and data over Swedish land, and 3D models and orthomosaics count as geographic information. Applying is free. Forest exemption: material ordered or photographed by the landowner with no vehicles or non-forestry human activity (power lines void the exemption). Follow-up products such as 3D models of approved material need no separate review unless the decision says so. Tropical countries need their own permits.

findings.claim: On 16 GB VRAM the number of Gaussians is the main limit, not the number of images, provided images are not stored on the GPU. INRIA 3DGS stores every image on the GPU as float32 by default.
findings.details: INRIA README: data_device defaults to cuda; use cpu for large or high-resolution datasets. Images wider than 1.6K are auto-rescaled. Paper-quality training needs 24 GB VRAM. cameras.py: original_image = gt_image.clamp(0,1).to(data_device), float32. Computed: 1600x1200x3x4 B ≈ 23 MB per image, so 300 aerial images ≈ 6.9 GB VRAM. gsplat's COLMAP dataset loads from disk per item or preloads into host RAM, and caches downscaled images. gsplat on A100 at 30k steps (Mip-NeRF360): default 3.24M Gaussians in 5.62 GB and 19.4 min. MCMC: 1M in 1.98 GB and 15.4 min, 2M in 3.43 GB, 3M in 4.99 GB and 27.6 min. OpenSplat: about 2 GB per million Gaussians.

findings.claim: Merging aerial images into the ground splat (option b) forces the ground plot and a 60-100 m aerial context into one Gaussian budget and one scene extent. Separate models (option c) handle this better on a 16 GB laptop.
findings.details: Inferred from the memory figures above plus knowledge of how 3DGS scales densification and learning rate with camera extent. With an MCMC cap of 4-6M Gaussians (about 7-12 GB), aerial context competes with ground detail. Without a cap, densification grows the Gaussian count with area. The extent grows about 10x (10 m to 100 m), which changes spatial thresholds. Separate models each get the full budget and can be streamed or LOD-ed separately in the viewer.

findings.claim: Data volume per plot: about 2-4 GB as 12 MP JPEG, 12-50 GB with DNG, about 1 GB per minute of 4K video. Downscale to about 3200 px for SfM and 1600-2000 px for training.
findings.details: Per-image sizes are estimates (no primary spec found): JPEG about 4-8 MB at 12 MP, 7-12 MB at 20 MP, 15-25 MB at 48-50 MP. DNG about 24 MB at 12 MP, about 40 MB at 20 MP, about 70-100 MB at 48-50 MP; one search snippet reported about 71 MB for a Mini 4 Pro DNG and about 20 MB for its JPEG. COLMAP SiftExtraction/FeatureExtraction max_image_size defaults to 3200, so 8192 px images are downscaled anyway. INRIA auto-rescales to 1.6K. gsplat has a data_factor option with a cached downscale.

findings.claim: Training-time expectation on an RTX 3080 Ti laptop: about 30-60 min per 30k iterations for 200-600 images at about 1.6-2K px with 1-4M Gaussians.
findings.details: Inferred from published figures, not measured on this GPU. gsplat on A100: 15-28 min. aerocartwright: RTX 3060 12 GB takes 25-40 min for 200-500 images; RTX 4090 8-12 min. arXiv 2602.20342: INRIA 3DGS at 30k iterations on RTX 4070 12 GB took 27-41 min. Per-iteration cost scales with rendered pixels and Gaussian count, not image count. Larger image sets may need more iterations so each view is seen enough.

findings.claim: OpenDroneMap is AGPL-3.0 with GPU only for SIFT extraction (about 2x faster); GPU on Windows effectively means Docker. Since April 2026, WebODM is a separate AGPL project on its own ODX engine that exports splat training data for OpenSplat.
findings.details: ODM: AGPL-3.0, native Windows setup or Docker. GPU uses the opendronemap/odm:gpu image with --gpus all, CUDA SIFT, GTX 9xx or newer. Native Windows users have reported 'Cannot initialize CUDA'. ODM 3.6.x added Mini 3 rolling-shutter support and DJI video telemetry fixes; the dates on the releases page looked inconsistent. --rolling-shutter correction is available. WebODM split from OpenDroneMap on 6 Apr 2026. It is AGPL-3.0, has a free installer (v3.3.0, dated 09/05/26), and supports the ODX, MicMac and LGT engines. ODX is AGPL-3.0, has a native Windows setup, a webodm/odx:gpu Docker image, OpenSfM 1.0 and GPU feature matching, and processes aerial and ground images. WebODM splats workflow: download training data, train in OpenSplat or another tool, upload the result for display; .RAD format preferred. OpenSplat (AGPL-3.0) reads ODX, OpenSfM, COLMAP, OpenMVG and nerfstudio projects and runs on CUDA, ROCm, Metal or CPU. RAM needs about 4 GB for 40 images, 16 GB for 250, 32 GB for 500 and 192 GB for 3500 (search summary of the WebODM hardware docs; the page itself returned 404).

findings.claim: Commercial drone splat tools such as DJI Terra GS do not fit the open-source, no-licence-limits requirement.
findings.details: DJI Terra V5 Gaussian splatting needs the Flagship tier: $3,700 per year or $10,580 perpetual. The Standard tier ($1,850 per year) has no GS. It targets Smart 3D Capture data with ≥80% overlap and exports .ply/.gsplat. Pix4Dmatic splats are also commercial; they need ≥10 GB VRAM and do not support fisheye or 360 input.

findings.claim: Near trees, do not rely on obstacle sensing. Thin branches of about 2-3 cm or less are not reliably detected, so low bridge passes must be flown manually and kept within sight of a clearing.
findings.details: Several secondary sources summarise DJI manual warnings: vision systems cannot reliably detect power lines, thin branches or thin wires, especially against foliage. Forward LiDAR on Mini 5 Pro, Air 3S and Mavic 4 Pro (0.5-25 m at night) helps but does not solve this. Under-canopy flying is out of scope for a consumer drone. Background knowledge: set return-to-home altitude above the tallest trees and keep the plot visible from the takeoff clearing.

recommendations.recommendation: Keep Phase 1 as LiDAR + Insta360 only. Add the drone as a later, optional option (c): a separate aerial model (splat plus optional ortho, DSM and canopy-height model) registered into the LiDAR frame and shown as its own viewer layer.
recommendations.rationale: Over a 10x10 m plot the drone mainly sees canopy tops and surroundings. Merging into the ground splat (option b) needs aerial-to-ground SfM matching, which mostly fails off the shelf (AerialMegaDepth: about 5% registration success). It also splits a 16 GB VRAM Gaussian budget and stretches scene extent about 10x. Option (c) gives each model its own budget, can be processed with a separate pipeline (COLMAP/GLOMAP+gsplat or ODX/WebODM), and suits a modular source design.
recommendations.alternatives: (b) merged single splat: only if the bridge images register reliably. Treat it as an experiment after (c) works. (a) alone is enough for the forest-floor product.

recommendations.recommendation: Aerial capture protocol for the first drone test (about 300-550 stills, 15-30 min, 1-2 batteries): nadir crosshatch at canopy+40-60 m with 85-90/75-80 overlap; oblique crosshatch at -45°; 2-3 orbits at 5° steps (R≈20/35/50 m at canopy+15/30/45 m, gimbal -50/-40/-30°); and a bridge sequence (vertical ascent in a gap or at the forest edge with photos every 1-2 m from 2 m to canopy+10 m, plus near-horizontal edge passes).
recommendations.rationale: Combines the splat guidance (orbits and obliques; 80/70 minimum), the forest guidance (85%+ overlap; Frey >95%), and the proven fusion practice of vertical-ascent and takeoff/landing bridge images (heliguy M4E workflow). Orbits give the angular diversity splats need. The bridge images are the only views that overlap the ground capture, and they keep option (b) possible later.
recommendations.alternatives: Reduced set for a quick feasibility test: 3 orbits, one oblique pass and the bridge (about 250-300 images in one battery). Video: 4K at 1-2 m/s on orbits with 1-2 fps extraction, acceptable for a test only.

recommendations.recommendation: Camera settings: stills in 12 MP mode (not 48/50 MP), 4:3 uncropped, manual exposure, ISO 100-400, shutter at least 1/1000 s while moving (at least 1/500 s when hovering), fixed Kelvin white balance, focus locked, distortion correction OFF, HDR/SmartPhoto off, JPEG (+DNG optional). Use hover-and-shoot waypoints or flight at 1-3 m/s.
recommendations.rationale: 12 MP mode has 2-4x faster readout and a 2 s minimum interval (48/50 MP is limited to 5 s). Hover-and-shoot removes rolling-shutter and blur effects, which COLMAP does not model. Raw lens geometry keeps SfM intrinsics consistent. Fixed exposure and white balance avoid appearance flicker that splats turn into floaters or colour seams.
recommendations.alternatives: Matrice 4E: use the mechanical shutter at 1/1000-1/2000 s with a 0.5 s interval and fly at normal mapping speed.

recommendations.recommendation: Timing: fly the drone directly before or after the ground walk, within the same 30-60 min of uniform overcast, with canopy wind below about 3-4 m/s, and keep the ground operator out of the aerial frames.
recommendations.rationale: Diffuse light suits both under-canopy 360 video and appearance matching between sources. Moving foliage breaks SfM and causes splat ghosting. Dandois found clear sky gives slightly deeper SfM canopy penetration (18% vs 16%), but appearance consistency matters more for this viewer.
recommendations.alternatives: If it is sunny, fly near solar noon and keep the gap under about 30 min. Expect shadow mismatch and use per-image appearance embeddings in training.

recommendations.recommendation: Drone choice. Budget: DJI Mini 4 Pro (C0; MSDK, so Dronelink/Litchi Pilot can automate grids and orbits and you could write your own Android app) or DJI Mini 5 Pro (C0 with standard battery; better 1-inch sensor; DJI Fly waypoints + Pixpro/Litchi Hub KMZ). Mid: DJI Air 3S (C1). Pro or tropical scale: DJI Matrice 4E (C2, mechanical shutter, 0.5 s interval, integrated RTK, Smart 3D, MSDK; about $5-5.4k).
recommendations.rationale: For a 10x10 m plot, a sub-250 g drone with waypoint hover-and-shoot is enough and needs the least paperwork. A mechanical shutter and RTK pay off only for large, fast grids and georeferencing, as on later tropical plots. Without GNSS on the BLK2GO, RTK does not by itself tie the aerial model to the LiDAR frame.
recommendations.alternatives: Autel EVO II Pro (RTK) V3 (C2) if company policy excludes DJI. Mavic 4 Pro (C2, 100 MP) is overkill. Check internally whether Hexagon still offers BLK2FLY or any aerial capture hardware.

recommendations.recommendation: Place 4-6 high-contrast targets in canopy gaps or at the forest edge that are visible both from the air and to the BLK2GO and Insta360, and take drone takeoff/landing shots near them.
recommendations.rationale: A handheld LiDAR scanning from below and a drone viewing from above share little surface. Targets in gaps, plus stems at the plot edge seen in the low obliques, are the most reliable ties for registering the aerial model to the LiDAR frame. Drone GPS or RTK only gives a georeferenced frame and approximate scale.
recommendations.alternatives: Register the aerial model's DSM to LiDAR stems and gap edges with ICP and use GPS priors as an initial guess. This is less reliable under closed canopy.

recommendations.recommendation: Compute settings: never keep images on the GPU (gsplat, or INRIA with --data_device cpu); train aerial images at 1600-2000 px; let COLMAP downsize to 3200 px for SIFT; cap Gaussians with MCMC (about 1-3M for the aerial layer, and 4-6M total if merged); use COLMAP's spatial matcher with EXIF GPS for the drone set.
recommendations.rationale: 300 aerial images at 1600x1200 stored as float32 on the GPU take about 6.9 GB. Gaussian memory is about 1.7-2 GB per million. A 16 GB laptop GPU with Windows overhead realistically allows about 4-6M Gaussians.
recommendations.alternatives: ODX/WebODM (AGPL, run as an external process) for the aerial ortho, DSM and point cloud and for OpenSfM poses fed to OpenSplat or gsplat.

recommendations.recommendation: Before publishing any aerial layer of a Swedish site, get a Lantmäteriet spridningstillstånd (free), or confirm the forest/landowner exemption. Register as operator with Transportstyrelsen and do A1/A3 training, and fly in A3 conditions. Plan tropical permits per country.
recommendations.rationale: Aerial images and derived 3D models of Swedish land are covered by Lag 2016:319. A web-delivered splat counts as dissemination.
recommendations.alternatives: Keep the aerial layer private or internal until the permit is granted.

risks: Aerial and ground images may not register in one SfM run, because of the large viewpoint, scale and appearance gap (AerialMegaDepth shows about 5% registration success for off-the-shelf methods). Option (b) may fail outright, and even option (c) needs targets or LiDAR-geometry ties.
Under a closed canopy the drone sees almost none of the 10x10 m forest floor, so it adds little to the main product while adding cost, permits and processing.
Wind-driven foliage motion between frames, and between the aerial and ground captures, causes SfM failures and splat ghosting or floaters at the canopy.
Changing sun and shadows between the drone flight and the ground walk cause visible seams. Uniform overcast or a back-to-back schedule is required.
Consumer DJI rolling shutter (16-60 ms readout) plus interval shooting while moving distorts geometry. Mitigate with 12 MP mode, slow flight or hover-and-shoot.

DJI Fly limits: 200 waypoints per mission, no grid tool, no KML import on several models. Mini 5 Pro, Air 3S and Mavic 4 Pro lack MSDK, so they depend on KMZ-replacement workarounds (Pixpro, Litchi Hub) that firmware updates can break.
VRAM: a merged model can exceed 16 GB because of the larger extent and more Gaussians. INRIA's default of keeping images on the GPU alone can use 7+ GB with 300 aerial images.

Flight safety: obstacle sensing does not see thin branches, keeping visual line of sight from inside a forest is hard, GNSS is degraded near the canopy, and tropical emergent trees (60 m+) require a high return-to-home altitude.

Legal: a Swedish spridningstillstånd is needed before publishing aerial data on the web; nature reserves may have local drone bans (not verified); tropical countries need separate permits and import paperwork.

Corporate or vendor risk: company policy or future regulation may restrict DJI. US FCC actions against foreign drones in 2025-26 come from background knowledge and were not verified. Non-DJI options are weaker or costlier.
AGPL-3.0 (ODM, ODX, WebODM, OpenSplat): fine as separately invoked tools, but modifying them or embedding them in a distributed or networked product triggers source-sharing obligations.
Several numbers were not verified because the shared web-search budget ran out: per-image file sizes, training times on the 3080 Ti laptop, Autel/Skydio details, BLK2FLY status, EUR prices.
open_questions: Is there a canopy gap or clearing within visual line of sight of the 10x10 m Swedish test plot, for takeoff and the vertical bridge sequence?
Will bridge images from 2-10 m height at the forest edge actually register with the Insta360 under-canopy frames in COLMAP/GLOMAP, or will learned matchers (MASt3R/VGGT-class) be needed?
How many Gaussians does a 10x10 m ground plot need for good quality (for example 1-3M) before deciding the budget for an aerial layer or a merged model?
Measured training time and peak VRAM for gsplat on the RTX 3080 Ti laptop at 1600-2000 px. This needs a benchmark run.
Is Leica BLK2FLY (or any Hexagon aerial capture product) still available internally? It was not on Leica's product page in Oct 2026.
Is the Matrice 4E RTK module standard and non-removable in all EU bundles? Dealers say yes; DJI's spec page wording is ambiguous.
Exact JPEG/DNG file sizes for the chosen drone (estimated, not sourced).
Does the Swedish forest exemption from the dissemination permit apply if the user is not the landowner? If not, how long does Lantmäteriet take to process a permit?
questions_for_user: Does Hexagon have a policy that restricts DJI drones, or a preferred supplier, for example Autel or an internal Hexagon/Leica aerial product?
How much RAM does your laptop have? ODM/ODX needs about 16 GB for 250 images and 32 GB for 500, and this decides whether the aerial pipeline runs locally.
Who owns the Swedish test forest, and do you plan to publish the aerial layer publicly? This decides whether you need a Lantmäteriet dissemination permit or can use the landowner forest exemption.

Do you need absolute georeferencing (national grid, for example SWEREF 99, or LuciadRIA map placement) for the aerial layer? If so, RTK (Matrice 4E) or surveyed GCPs are needed; if relative alignment to the LiDAR is enough, a Mini-class drone suffices.
Is the drone layer for visual context (canopy, terrain, surroundings) or must it improve the forest-floor splat? The second is unlikely to be achievable under closed canopy.
Is there a clearing or forest road next to the test plot from which a pilot can keep the drone in sight?
