verdicts.claim: Nadir-only drone imagery gives poor Gaussian splats. Splat capture needs oblique crosshatch passes plus multi-altitude, variable-radius orbits.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed as quoted. WebODM: 'Gaussian splatting requires oblique and/or orbit shots... A nadir-only flight, usually yields very poor results.' PIX4Dmatic recommends double grids, multi-altitude circular orbits and helix patterns, and says to avoid sky. Its splat overlap guidance is lower than the report implies: 70-80% longitudinal and 60-70% transverse. MipMap (23 Jun 2026) recommends multi-tier orbits and 'crosshatch oblique grids combined with targeted orbital fill-shots'.

verdicts.claim: Overlap targets: at least 80/70 for splats, 85/80 for best quality; forests need more (Frey 2018: >95% overlap and GSD >5 cm best for completeness).
verdicts.correction: The figures check out source by source. MipMap gives 80/70 minimum. thefuture3d gives 80/70 minimum and 85/80 for highest quality. The ≤3 cm GSD figure comes from MipMap, not thefuture3d. The Frey 2018 abstract confirms 'best results are achieved with an image overlap of > 95% and a resolution of > 5 cm', with wind and terrain elevation the main environmental factors. Two corrections. First, splat guidance is not uniform: Pix4D GS recommends only 70-80/60-70. Second, the Dandois 2015 abstract says height error was explained mostly by CHM-to-DTM alignment (R²=0.81). Once that is accounted for, it found 'no significant differences... in height error at different levels of lighting, altitude, and side overlap'. The 'error doubled when forward overlap decreased' detail could not be read in the primary text (MDPI returns 403) and is unverified. The Pix4D dense-vegetation article could not be fetched (redirect loop). The 85-90/75-80 forest recommendation is still reasonable.

verdicts.claim: Dandois 2015: canopy penetration 18% (clear) vs 16% (cloudy); accurate canopy height needed >80% overlap.
verdicts.correction: The visible abstract does not contain these numbers, and the MDPI full text returned 403. The study was in temperate deciduous forest, not boreal or tropical. Do not use 18% vs 16% as a design driver.

verdicts.claim: The under-canopy NeRF paper (arXiv 2601.22861, WACV-W 2026) supports diffuse light for matching appearance with under-canopy 360 video.
verdicts.correction: The quote is real: 'Our method performs best under diffuse light (overcast or twilight), which balances canopy and ground exposure.' The paper also hypothesises 'a GSD of approximately 1–2 cm offers a good trade-off'. The context is wrong, though. The paper (Sheffer et al., WACV 2026 CV4EO workshop) reconstructs understory terrain from drone RGB imagery taken from above (AOS dataset). It is not about ground-level 360 video. It is therefore direct evidence on the addendum question of how much forest floor a drone sees: partial recovery through gaps under diffuse light, and 'not all persons were uncovered' in scenes with 'broadleaf or mixed canopies, which create dense occlusions'. The paper gives no coverage percentages.

verdicts.claim: Bridge images (vertical ascent at the edge or in a gap, plus takeoff/landing shots) are what working aerial-ground splat fusions use; the protocol 'copies heliguy's M4E + XGRIDS workflow'.
verdicts.correction: The heliguy details are confirmed (11 Jul 2025): two perpendicular ortho flights at 30 m, two perpendicular Smart Oblique flights at 70 m, manual triggers every 1 m during ascents to 70 m at building corners, plus takeoff/landing shots. Processing took 5 h on a Ryzen 9 9950X3D with an RTX 5090 and 128 GB RAM. But heliguy also states 'the K1 and M4E required an RTK fix' for Aerial Ground Map Fusion. The site was an open building, and processing used commercial Lixel CyberColor. The BLK2GO has no GNSS and the plot is under canopy, so the shared frame that made that fusion work is missing. For this project the bridge sequence is an untested hypothesis, not a copy of proven practice. Targets/GCPs are the primary tie.

verdicts.claim: AerialMegaDepth (CVPR 2025): off-the-shelf aerial-ground registration about 5%, about 56% after fine-tuning (rotation error <5°).
verdicts.correction: Abstract: 'baseline DUSt3R localizes fewer than 5% of aerial-ground pairs within 5 degrees of camera rotation error, while fine-tuning with our data raises accuracy to nearly 56%'. The baseline is DUSt3R specifically, and the test data is urban and building-centric, not forest. Sky2Ground (CVPR 2026) benchmarks MASt3R, DUSt3R, MapAnything and VGGT. Its headline finding is that adding satellite imagery degrades performance under large altitude gaps. arXiv 2509.19898 does rely on rendered intermediate views.

verdicts.claim: Rolling-shutter readout: Air 3S <16 ms at 12 MP and 20-30 ms at 50 MP; Mini 3 Pro about 25 ms (12 MP) and 60 ms (48 MP).
verdicts.correction: Pixpro (28 Nov 2024): 'sub 16-millisecond readout' at 12 MP and '20 - 30 millisecond' at 50 MP. ODM community (5 Feb 2024): 48 MP '60 or 61 ms', 12 MP 'looks like 25ms'. Both are community measurements, not manufacturer specs.

verdicts.claim: Minimum photo interval: Mini 4 Pro, Mini 5 Pro and Air 3S are 2 s at 12 MP and 5 s at 48/50 MP; Mavic 3E 0.7 s; Matrice 4E 0.5 s.
verdicts.correction: All figures match the DJI spec pages. Mavic 4 Pro timed shots go down to 1 s (512 GB version) or 2 s, depending on resolution.

verdicts.claim: The Mini 4 Pro is the only current consumer Mini on MSDK v5; Mini 5 Pro, Air 3S and Mavic 4 Pro are not supported.
verdicts.correction: The MSDK v5 list (fetched Oct 2026) is: Matrice 4D/4TD, 4E/4T, M300, M350, M30, Mavic 3E series, Mavic 3M, Mini 4 Pro, Mini 3 and Mini 3 Pro. Mini 5 Pro, Air 3S and Mavic 4 Pro are absent, as the report says. Correction: Mini 3 and Mini 3 Pro are also supported, and DJI still lists the Mini 3 as a current product, so 'only' is wrong. Practical caveat the report leaves out of its recommendation: Mini 4 Pro MSDK works only with the RC-N2 phone-holder controller. 'DJI has not released MSDK support for the DJI RC 2 controller' (DroneDJ, 21 Mar 2025). Buy the RC-N2 bundle.

verdicts.claim: Dronelink: Mini 4 Pro full support; Air 3/3S and Mavic 4 Pro onboard only; Mini 5 Pro via unofficial APK; Autel unofficial; Parrot not supported. Litchi Pilot supports Mini 4 Pro and M4E; Litchi Hub covers Mini 5 Pro, Air 3S and Mavic 4 Pro.
verdicts.correction: Dronelink lists Air 3/3S and Mavic 4 Pro as 'onboard only', Autel EVO II as '(unofficial)', and Parrot Anafi and Anafi Ai as '(not supported)'. Mini 5 Pro is not on the page at all, so the 'unofficial APK' route is unverified. Litchi supports Mini 4 Pro and Matrice 4 in Litchi Pilot BETA, and Mini 5 Pro, Air 3/3S and Mavic 4 Pro through Litchi Hub.

verdicts.claim: DJI Fly Waypoint Flight: up to 200 waypoints, Take Photo action, hover 0-30 s, per-waypoint gimbal tilt, no grid tool, no KML import on Mavic 4 Pro / Mavic 3 / Air 3 / Air 3S.
verdicts.correction: DJI support quotes: 'You can pin up to 200 waypoints'; hover 'from 0s to 30s'; 'Mavic 4 Pro, DJI Mavic 3 Series/DJI Air 3/DJI Air 3S does not support the import of KML flight routes'. Speeds are 0.1-15 m/s. The supported list also includes the new DJI Lito X1.

verdicts.claim: Pixpro Waypoints (from €5/month) builds grids, multi-grids (4 oblique headings) and orbits as KMZ, shooting by interval timer.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed: from about €5/month, interval-timer capture, the 200-waypoint DJI Fly limit, the placeholder-file workflow, and '16:9 photos will not work'. Supported drones include Mini 4 Pro, Mini 5 Pro, Air 3/3S, Mavic 3 and 4 Pro, and Lito X1. Correction: the FAQ says it 'currently offers automated single grids and orbitals', with a third type 'coming soon'. Oblique multi-grids may not be available yet. Planned photo positions are 'just for visualization purposes'. Pixpro itself recommends shutter priority at 1/400 s or faster with RAW preferred, which differs from the report's 'JPEG is enough'.

verdicts.claim: Mini 5 Pro: 249.9 g, C0 with standard battery and C1 with Plus, 1-inch 50 MP, up to 52 min (Plus), forward LiDAR, 130 Mbps, 42 GB.
verdicts.correction: Matches the DJI specs. Standard-battery flight time is 36 min. DJI states 'if the C0-certified drone is fitted with the Intelligent Flight Battery Plus, it exceeds the C0 MTOM threshold'. 12 MP and 50 MP single-shot modes; minimum interval 2 s / 5 s. There is no mechanical shutter. Pixpro (9 Oct 2025) recommends 12 MP for grids and notes that Mini 5 Pro has no RTK, so GCPs are needed.

verdicts.claim: Mini 4 Pro: <249 g, C0, 1/1.3-inch 48 MP, 34 min (45 min Plus), omnidirectional vision + 3D infrared, 150 Mbps.
verdicts.correction: DJI states 'The Intelligent Flight Battery Plus is not sold in Europe'. In the EU the Mini 4 Pro is therefore a 34-minute, C0-only drone. Everything else is confirmed.

verdicts.claim: Air 3S: 724 g, C1, 1-inch 50 MP + 70 mm tele, 45 min, forward LiDAR, 12 m/s wind; Mavic 4 Pro about 1063 g, C2, 4/3 100 MP, 51 min, no mechanical shutter.
verdicts.correction: The Air 3S figures and the 'C1 (EU)' label are confirmed. Mavic 4 Pro 'Approx. 1063 g', 'C2 (EU)', 4/3 100 MP and 51 min are confirmed. Single-shot modes are 25 MP and 100 MP. No mechanical shutter is listed.

verdicts.claim: Matrice 4E: 1219 g, C2, 4/3 20 MP, mechanical shutter 2-1/2000 s, 0.5 s interval, 49 min, RTK 1 cm+1 ppm H / 1.5 cm+1 ppm V; RTK integration ambiguous on DJI's page; about $5,000-5,400.
verdicts.correction: All specs are confirmed. The open question is answered by DJI's own FAQ: 'Is the RTK module of the DJI Matrice 4 series removable? No.' and 'DJI Matrice 4 Series is C2 certified by EASA'. MSDK and DJI Pilot 2 are supported. Flight time with low-noise propellers is 46 min. The price was not verified.

verdicts.claim: Mavic 3E: 1050 g, C2, mechanical shutter 8-1/2000 s, 0.7 s interval, 45 min, optional RTK; being phased out.
verdicts.correction: The specs and the 'C2 (EU)' label are confirmed. The RTK module is an optional accessory. The phase-out was not verified: DJI's spec page shows no discontinuation notice.

verdicts.claim: Leica BLK2FLY is no longer listed on Leica's autonomous reality capture page.
verdicts.correction: The page lists RTC series, BLK360, BLK360 SE, BLK2GO, BLK2GO PULSE and BLK ARC, with no BLK2FLY. The BLK2FLY product URL returns 404 or redirects to the general scanner page. It looks discontinued, but there is no explicit notice. Check internally at Hexagon.

verdicts.claim: Autel EVO II V3 gained C2 by firmware (Open A2/A3 from 1 Jan 2024).
verdicts.correction: An authorised dealer (autelpilot.com, 12 Mar 2024) states the 'EVO II V3 series' obtained C2. It does not say this came by firmware. Autel's own product page returned 403, so whether the RTK V3 is still sold, its price, and Autel's 2026 market status are unverified.

verdicts.claim: EASA Open category: A3 means 150 m from uninvolved people and urban areas, 120 m AGL; C0/C1 fly in A1, C2 in A2 with an A2 CofC, any class in A3 with A1/A3 training.
verdicts.correction: EASA: A3 'Maintain a horizontal distance of 150 m from uninvolved people and urban areas'; A2 30 m (5 m in low-speed mode); 'below 120m above ground level'. C0 requires only reading the manual. Camera drones under 250 g still need operator registration.

verdicts.claim: Sweden: Transportstyrelsen operator registration is about 150 SEK for 3 years.
verdicts.correction: Transportstyrelsen's fee page (updated 1 Jan 2026) gives a 190 SEK application fee plus a 250 SEK annual register-keeping fee. The drönarkort (A1/A3, A2) is valid 5 years and is required for drones of 250 g or more. Since 1 January 2026, flying without one is a criminal offence ('Det är nu straffbart att flyga drönare utan drönarkort').

verdicts.claim: Lantmäteriet spridningstillstånd: needed to publish aerial images or 3D models of Swedish land; free; forest exemption when the landowner commissioned or took the imagery (power lines void it); derived products of approved material need no separate review; keep the layer 'private or internal' until granted.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed: 'Att ansöka om spridningstillstånd är kostnadsfritt'. The forest exemption wording is confirmed: the landowner must have ordered the material or been the photographer, there must be no vehicles or human activity other than forestry, and a power line voids it. Derived products are allowed: 'Du får enbart sprida materialet som vi skickat tillbaka samt skapa följdprodukter utifrån det'. Corrections: (1) Current processing time is about 65 working days, roughly 3 months of lead time. (2) Dissemination is defined broadly: 'skickar det med e-post, publicerar det på en webbplats... lagrar det i molntjänster eller på servrar som du inte själv har fullständig kontroll över'. Emailing colleagues or storing the data on corporate cloud or a hosted viewer therefore already counts. 'Internal' is safe only if the data stays on the user's own machine. (3) Lantmäteriet cannot retouch 3D models or video, so submit the source JPG/TIF images and train from the returned, approved set.

verdicts.claim: INRIA 3DGS stores every image on the GPU as float32 by default (data_device=cuda), auto-rescales images wider than 1.6K, and needs 24 GB for paper quality; licence is non-commercial.
verdicts.correction: README and cameras.py confirm: gt_image.clamp(0.0,1.0).to(self.data_device). The 300 × 23 MB ≈ 6.9 GB arithmetic is correct. LICENSE.md Section 5 says 'THE USER CANNOT USE, EXPLOIT OR DISTRIBUTE THE SOFTWARE FOR COMMERCIAL PURPOSES WITHOUT PRIOR AND EXPLICIT CONSENT'. This matters for a Hexagon project: use gsplat (Apache-2.0) as the default trainer, not INRIA.

verdicts.claim: gsplat on A100 at 30k steps (Mip-NeRF360): default 3.24M Gaussians in 5.62 GB and 19.4 min; MCMC 1M 1.98 GB 15.4 min, 2M 3.43 GB, 3M 4.99 GB 27.6 min. OpenSplat about 2 GB per million.
verdicts.correction: Exact match to the gsplat eval page (7-scene Mip-NeRF360 average on an A100). OpenSplat: 'you need ~2GB of GPU memory for each million gaussians'. gsplat is Apache-2.0 and at v1.6.0 (repo activity Aug 2026). Extrapolating to 4-6M Gaussians on a 16 GB laptop is reasonable, but it is not a measurement on that GPU.

verdicts.claim: OpenDroneMap is AGPL-3.0, GPU only for SIFT (about 2x), GPU via the opendronemap/odm:gpu Docker image; RAM 4/16/32/192 GB for 40/250/500/3500 images.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed in the ODM README and installation docs. The full table is 40→4, 250→16, 500→32, 1500→64, 2500→128, 3500→192 and 5000→256 GB. The installation docs also say 'a graphics card (GPU) currently has no impact on performance', which is inconsistent with the README's 2x SIFT claim. Expect at most a minor GPU benefit.

verdicts.claim: WebODM split from OpenDroneMap on 6 Apr 2026, is AGPL-3.0 with a free installer (v3.3.0), uses its own ODX engine, and exports splat training data for OpenSplat.
verdicts.correction: Decoupling is confirmed: 'WebODM has officially decoupled from OpenDroneMap'. It is AGPL-3.0 and the installer is '100% Free'. The date is slightly off: the decoupling shipped in release v3.2.0 on 9 Apr (2026), and v3.3.0 (5 Sep 2026) added 'Feat: Gaussian Splatting'. ODX is confirmed: AGPL-3.0, 'Forked from, faster than ODM', a Windows setup, the webodm/odx:gpu image, OpenSfM 1.0, and support for aerial and ground imagery. WebODM docs also list Brush (WebGPU, multi-vendor) alongside OpenSplat as trainers. OpenSplat Windows binaries are paid; building from source needs VS2022 and CUDA 11.8.

verdicts.claim: COLMAP downsizes to 3200 px for SIFT by default.
verdicts.correction: The CLI docs list --FeatureExtraction.max_image_size (=3200), and max_num_features defaults to 8192. COLMAP also has pose_prior_mapper and model_aligner, which matter for GPS-prior drone sets.

verdicts.claim: DJI Terra GS needs the Flagship tier ($3,700/yr or $10,580 perpetual); Pix4Dmatic splats need ≥10 GB VRAM and do not support fisheye/360.
verdicts.correction: Advexure (1 Aug 2025) confirms Flagship-only GS at those prices. Pix4D: 'at least 10 GB of VRAM (can work with less)', a PIX4Dmatic Pro licence, and 'Fisheye cameras, 360º and thermal images are not supported'.

verdicts.claim: Training time on an RTX 3080 Ti laptop is about 30-60 min per 30k iterations (inferred).
verdicts.correction: The cited inputs check out. arXiv 2602.20342 measured INRIA 3DGS at 30k iterations on an RTX 4070 12 GB at about 41 min (Mip-NeRF360), 26-27 min (Tanks and Temples) and 36 min (Deep Blending). gsplat on an A100 took 15-28 min. The 30-60 min range is a reasonable inference but has not been measured on this GPU.

verdicts.claim: Gaussian Splatting on the Move (ECCV 2024): COLMAP does not model rolling shutter; the compensation needs VIO velocities.
verdicts.correction: The abstract confirms blur and rolling-shutter compensation using VIO velocities. Code is at SpectacularAI/3dgs-deblur. The ECCV venue is not stated on the arXiv abstract page.

verdicts.claim: Per-image file sizes: JPEG 4-8 MB (12 MP), 7-12 MB (20 MP), 15-25 MB (48-50 MP); DNG about 24/40/70-100 MB.
verdicts.correction: No primary source was found, and the search budget was exhausted. The report itself marks these as estimates. Measure them on the chosen drone.

verdicts.claim: DJI obstacle sensing does not reliably detect branches thinner than about 2-3 cm.
verdicts.correction: The specific 2-3 cm threshold has no primary DJI source. The qualitative warning (thin branches and wires are not reliably detected) is standard and the advice still holds.

verdicts.claim: US FCC actions against foreign drones (DJI) in 2025-26.
verdicts.correction: The FCC Covered List page returned 403. In any case this is US-specific, not an EU legal constraint. It is relevant only as a Hexagon corporate-policy question.

missed_developments.claim: Horizon-GS shows that joint aerial+street splat training underperforms separate training. This is direct evidence for option (c).
missed_developments.details: Horizon-GS (arXiv 2412.01745, Dec 2024): 'joint training across both domains consistently underperformed separate training, even with extensive iterations'. It names two causes: 'conflicting gradient accumulation' and 'disparity in view information coverage'. The fix is a two-stage coarse-to-fine scheme: aerial-only gradients first, then street-view refinement with frozen MLP weights. Real-data poses came from commercial ContextCapture, not COLMAP. If option (b) is ever tried, plan staged training, not a naive merged run. The planner should cite this alongside AerialMegaDepth. The venue (likely CVPR 2025) was not confirmed on the arXiv page.

missed_developments.claim: Swedish operational rules the report omits: criminal sanctions since 1 Jan 2026, mandatory insurance for non-recreational flights, nature-reserve and national-park take-off/landing bans, and the LFV drone map.
missed_developments.details: Transportstyrelsen: 'Den 1 januari 2026 infördes nya och utökade straffsanktioner'. It is now criminal to fly a drone of 250 g or more without a drönarkort. Insurance is waived only 'för fritidsändamål, uppvisnings- eller rekreationsverksamhet' under 20 kg; 'Övriga drönaroperationer omfattas av försäkringskrav enligt Förordning (EU) 785/2004'. Hexagon work flights therefore need liability insurance. 'Start- och landningsförbud kan råda i Naturreservat och nationalparker'; Länsstyrelsen grants exemptions. Always check LFV Drönarkartan (dronechart.lfv.se) for geographic zones. Direct and network remote ID requirements apply to class-labelled drones.

missed_developments.claim: The Lantmäteriet permit has about 65 working days of lead time, and its definition of dissemination covers email and cloud storage. This affects the web-delivery architecture.
missed_developments.details: Current processing time is about 65 working days ('Vi handlägger just nu ärenden från vecka 29'). Dissemination includes emailing, web publication, and storing 'i molntjänster eller på servrar som du inte själv har fullständig kontroll över'. Any drone-derived layer of a Swedish site must therefore stay on the local laptop until approval or the forest/landowner exemption is confirmed. That includes sharing with Hexagon colleagues, OneDrive/SharePoint, GitHub, or a hosted web or LuciadRIA viewer. Lantmäteriet cannot retouch 3D models, so submit the images and build the splat from the returned set. Capture itself needs no permit, only dissemination does.

missed_developments.claim: 360-camera drones now exist and could provide low-altitude bridge imagery with the same equirectangular camera model as the Insta360.
missed_developments.details: DJI Avata 360: about 455 g, C1 (EU), two 1/1.1-inch 64 MP sensors, 360 photos up to 120 MP (15520×7760), 8K 2:1 360 video, about 23 min flight, omnidirectional vision plus forward LiDAR. Antigravity (Insta360's drone brand) sells the A1, billed as 'The World's First 360 Drone' with 8K 360 video. Its weight and class label were not verified. Both are FPV/cinematic platforms with no mapping missions; flying with goggles needs a visual observer in the Open category, and they are untested for SfM bridging. They are worth one experiment in the later drone phase: slow 360 passes along the forest edge or in a gap could share the camera model and viewpoints with the Insta360 ground walk, which addresses the aerial-ground matching gap better than nadir stills.

missed_developments.claim: DJI Lito X1 is a new sub-250 g option supported by DJI Fly waypoints and Pixpro.
missed_developments.details: Lito X1: about 249 g standard (340 g max), C0/C1 (EU), 1/1.3-inch 48 MP (12/48 MP modes), forward LiDAR 0.5-36 m, 36 min max. It is listed in DJI Fly Waypoint Flight support and Pixpro Waypoints support. It is not on MSDK v5 and its sensor is smaller than the Mini 5 Pro's, so it is not better for this project. It belongs in the candidate comparison for completeness.

missed_developments.claim: Drone-based under-canopy terrain reconstruction (AOS dataset, WACV-W 2026) is the relevant evidence for 'how much forest floor can a drone see'.
missed_developments.details: Sheffer et al. reconstruct understory terrain from drone RGB imagery with NeRF, low-light losses and vegetation removal. It works best under diffuse light with a GSD of about 1-2 cm. Hidden persons were not all recovered under broadleaf or mixed canopies. This supports the report's conclusion that a drone is mainly a canopy, terrain and context layer. Some floor visibility through gaps is achievable in sparse boreal stands, much less in dense tropical forest.

verification.recommendation_assessment:
The core recommendations hold up and are strengthened. Phase 1 stays LiDAR + Insta360. Drone comes later as option (c), a separately trained aerial model registered to the LiDAR frame by targets or GCPs, with bridge images captured so (b) can be tried later. Horizon-GS, which the report missed, reports that joint aerial+street training 'consistently underperformed separate training'. AerialMegaDepth confirms that off-the-shelf DUSt3R registers fewer than 5% of aerial-ground pairs within 5°. The protocol (obliques plus multi-radius orbits, 85-90/75-80 overlap for forest, 12 MP stills, hover-and-shoot or slow flight, distortion correction off, same overcast window) is consistent with the primary sources checked. Specs, class labels, intervals, MSDK and third-party app support, gsplat and OpenSplat memory figures, the INRIA data_device default, and ODM/ODX/WebODM licences are verified.

Changes I would make:
(1) Drop the claim that the bridge sequence 'copies' a proven workflow. heliguy's fusion depended on an RTK fix on both the K1 and the M4E at an open building site, and the BLK2GO has no GNSS. Under canopy, 4-6 targets in gaps or at the edge, visible to drone, BLK2GO and Insta360, are the primary tie. Bridge images are an experiment.
(2) Mini 4 Pro: say explicitly to buy the RC-N2 bundle, because MSDK does not work with the RC 2. In the EU it is 34 min only, since the Plus battery is not sold there. Mini 3 and Mini 3 Pro are also MSDK models, so 'only' should go.
(3) Matrice 4E: RTK is integrated and non-removable, and it is C2 (DJI FAQ). Remove the open question.
(4) Pixpro currently offers only single grids and orbits. Oblique multi-grids may not exist yet, so the budget-drone oblique crosshatch may need manual DJI Fly waypoints or Dronelink on the Mini 4 Pro.
(5) Fix the Swedish compliance section. Fees are 190 SEK plus 250 SEK per year. Flying a drone of 250 g or more without a drönarkort has been criminal since 1 Jan 2026. Work flights need liability insurance under EU 785/2004. Check nature-reserve and national-park take-off/landing bans with Länsstyrelsen and check LFV Drönarkartan.
(6) Fix the spridningstillstånd guidance. Allow about 65 working days and apply as soon as a site is chosen. 'Internal' sharing by email, corporate cloud or a hosted viewer already counts as dissemination, so the aerial layer must stay on the local laptop until approval or a confirmed landowner exemption. Submit images, not 3D models, which Lantmäteriet cannot retouch. This constrains the web-delivery and LuciadRIA plan for drone layers.
(7) Re-cite the WACV-W 2026 paper as drone-from-above understory evidence, not as evidence about 360 video.
(8) Use gsplat (Apache-2.0) as the default trainer. INRIA 3DGS is non-commercial only (LICENSE Section 5), which matters for a Hexagon project.
(9) Optionally add a 360-drone experiment (DJI Avata 360, Antigravity A1) to the later phase for edge and gap bridge passes that share the Insta360 camera model.

Still unverified: per-image file sizes, the Dandois 18%/16% figures, the M4E price, Autel's 2026 status, and the FCC status. The shared WebSearch budget was exhausted, so verification used direct fetches of primary pages only.

research.summary:
REGULATORY PICTURE (as of 2026-10-06). The legal side changes the drone decision. A ground-only capture (option a: BLK2GO + Insta360 carried on foot) is outside Sweden's law on protection of geographical information. Lag 2016:319 §9 bans spreading compilations of geographic information about Swedish land only when "informationen har inhämtats från luftfartyg", and a drone counts as an aircraft. So option (a) can be published on the web without a Lantmäteriet permit; only GDPR applies (blur faces and number plates). Any drone-derived product needs a dissemination permit (spridningstillstånd) before it is put on the web, emailed to others, or stored on cloud servers or other servers you do not fully control. That covers photos, video, orthophotos, laser and height data and 3D models, and a Gaussian splat almost certainly counts as a 3D model. The permit is free. Lantmäteriet's estimate is now about 65 working days (about 3 months). Lantmäteriet cannot retouch 3D models, so a model is approved or refused as a whole. The rule still stands: the only 2026 amendment (SFS 2026:1378, in force 1 Aug 2026) changed §6, which covers exemptions for authorities and photography during heightened readiness, not the §9 permit duty. Riksdag motion 2025/26:2626, which asked for a review, was rejected. Lantmäteriet's exemptions include forest land, but only if the landowner ordered or took the material, it shows no vehicles or human activity other than forestry, it shows no power lines, and no wider surroundings are visible. A drone grid over a test plot will often show roads or buildings, so plan to apply. The architecture consequence is direct. Option (b), a merged splat, puts the whole splat under the permit duty, and the ground layer cannot be published on its own. Option (c), a separate aerial layer, lets the ground model be published right away while the drone layer waits for or fails the permit. The source-module design should therefore carry a per-source 'dissemination clearance' flag, and the public build should leave out uncleared aerial layers.

EU AVIATION FRAMEWORK. Regulations (EU) 2019/947 (operations) and 2019/945 (product classes C0–C6) apply. Open category: VLOS, at most 120 m above the closest point of the terrain, MTOM under 25 kg.
- A1: C0 drones (<250 g) may fly over uninvolved people but never over assemblies; C1 (<900 g) must not overfly uninvolved people.
- A2: C2 (<4 kg), at least 30 m from uninvolved people, or 5 m in low-speed mode; needs the A2 certificate of competency (CofC).
- A3: C2/C3/C4 and legacy drones; no uninvolved person may be endangered, and the drone must stay at least 150 m from residential, commercial, industrial or recreational areas. The regulation does not define a recreational area, so the operator has to judge forest trails and recreation areas.
- Legacy drones (no class label, placed on the market before 1 Jan 2024) may still fly: under 250 g in A1, otherwise only in A3.
- Direct Remote ID has been mandatory since 1 Jan 2024 for C1, C2, C3, C5 and C6, and for the Specific category. C0, C4 and legacy drones are exempt. The operator registration number must be uploaded to the drone.
- Insurance: Regulation 785/2004 exempts model aircraft under 20 kg.
- Specific category: STS-01/02 with C5/C6 drones, PDRA, or SORA 2.5 (ED Decision 2025/018/R). It is needed only for BVLOS, flights above 120 m, flights over assemblies or drones over 25 kg; a small forest grid fits in Open.

Coming change: EASA Opinion 06/2026 (18 Sep 2026, sent to the Commission, not yet adopted) would lower registration, Remote ID and training thresholds from 250 g to 100 g and require identity checks of operators. Drones under 900 g placed on the market before entry into force + 12 months would not need a Remote ID add-on. Press reports expect the first effects around mid-2028. Buy a class-labelled drone with Remote ID.

SWEDEN (Transportstyrelsen):
- Operator registration is required if the drone is 250 g or more, or carries a camera or sensor (so any camera drone). It costs 190 SEK to apply and 250 SEK per year, billed to anyone registered on 1 January. Display the operator ID on the drone.
- A1/A3 card: online test, 40 questions, 75% to pass, 600 SEK, valid 5 years. It is mandatory for drones of 250 g or more. Flying without it has been a crime since 1 Jan 2026 (30–150 day-fines, up to 6 months' prison in the worst cases).
- A2 card: an extra 30-question exam, which per Transportstyrelsen must now be taken under supervision at an authorised drone school (ADS; a secondary source dates this to 23 Oct 2025), plus a declared practical self-training. 850 SEK, or 600 SEK if the A1/A3 fee is already paid.
- Insurance is not required for leisure drones under 20 kg. For work flights, check that Hexagon's liability insurance covers drones.
- Airspace: check the LFV drone map (dronechart.lfv.se) and NOTAM/AIP SUP. Within 5 km of a runway, ATC permission is always needed. Elsewhere in a control zone (CTR), the limit is 50 m AGL, or 10 m at military airports, at speeds of 25 m/s or less. Coordinate with any heliport within 1,000 m, such as hospital helipads. Never fly over or next to a designated protected site (skyddsobjekt) or in R-areas.
- Protected nature: landing is banned in all national parks without a Länsstyrelsen permit, and some parks also have Transportstyrelsen flight restrictions. Nature reserves may ban take-off and landing, so check the reserve's rules with the Länsstyrelsen. Bird protection areas often have a seasonal access ban, typically 1 Apr–15 Jul. Deliberately disturbing breeding birds is banned under artskyddsförordningen 4 §.
- Landowner: allemansrätten does not cover drone operations. Take-off or landing that causes appreciable damage or nuisance needs the landowner's consent. Get written consent anyway, because it also enables the forest exemption.
- Privacy: GDPR and the camera surveillance act apply only if people or number plates can be identified. A drone flown on site for a mapping session is generally not 'camera surveillance', which means ongoing or regularly repeated monitoring of people. Since 1 Aug 2026 (SFS 2026:1373) no one needs a camera surveillance permit.

TROPICS. Rules depend on the country and are often much stricter for foreigners. An EU A1/A3 certificate is generally not recognised.
- Brazil: RBAC 100 has been in force since 16 Jun 2026. Drones over 250 g must be registered in SISANT, which needs a CPF. Every flight needs DECEA SARPAS authorisation, the drone needs ANATEL homologation, the ANAC exam is enforced from 1 Jan 2027, and third-party insurance is mandatory.
- Malaysia: CAAM Authorisation to Fly (ATF), applied for at least 14 working days ahead. JUPEM approval is needed for aerial photo, mapping or LiDAR. Sabah and Sarawak require extra authorisation.
- Costa Rica: DGAC registration and authorisation. SINAC protected areas also need an environmental permit (MINAE).
- Indonesia: foreigners cannot register a drone and must work through a local company; national parks need a BKSDA permit.
Budget months, and use a local licensed operator.

NET RECOMMENDATION FROM A REGULATORY VIEW. Keep phase 1 ground-only. If a drone is added, use a C0 or C1 drone in A1, or a C2 in A3 over the forest. Process the images locally, not in cloud photogrammetry. Show the drone data as a separate layer (option c), and apply for the permit about 3 months before publishing.

Limitations: the WebSearch budget ran out near the end. The Lantmäteriet LMFS exemption PDF, the Naturvårdsverket guidance PDF and the official ANAC, Costa Rica DGAC and Indonesian regulator pages could not be read (unparseable PDFs, CAPTCHA, HTTP 403), so the tropical details rest on secondary sources.

findings.claim: In Sweden, spreading anything derived from drone imagery over land (photos, video, orthophotos, laser and height data, 3D models, so very likely a Gaussian splat) requires a dissemination permit (spridningstillstånd) from Lantmäteriet. This is still in force in Oct 2026.
findings.details: Lag 2016:319 §9 bans spreading compilations of geographic information about Swedish land 'om informationen har inhämtats från luftfartyg genom fotografering eller liknande registrering'. The penalty is fines or up to 1 year in prison (§12). The law has been amended up to SFS 2026:1378 (published 2026-06-25, in force 2026-08-01), but that amendment changed §6, which covers exemptions for authorities and photography during heightened readiness, not §9. Riksdag motion 2025/26:2626 (6 Oct 2025), which asked for a review, was rejected (avslag). Lantmäteriet's application form lists 3D models, laser data and height data as material types, and a secondary guide says material compiled into a 3D model or orthophoto is covered.

findings.claim: Ground-captured data (handheld BLK2GO LiDAR and an Insta360 carried on foot) is not covered by the dissemination-permit duty. Option (a) can be published on the web without Lantmäteriet's approval.
findings.details: §9 covers information about land only when it was gathered from aircraft (and it covers sea areas in general). Lantmäteriet's FAQ says 'Spridningstillstånd krävs bara när du filmar från luftfartyg' and that pictures taken from high points with ground contact need no permit. GDPR still applies to identifiable people in the 360 video.

findings.claim: 'Dissemination' includes emailing, publishing on a website or social media, and storing on cloud services or servers you do not fully control. Uploading raw drone images to cloud photogrammetry, or hosting a drone-derived splat publicly, is dissemination.
findings.details: Lantmäteriet FAQ: 'Spridning är när du tillgängliggör materialet för andra, till exempel skickar det med e-post, publicerar det på en webbplats eller sociala medier, lagrar det i molntjänster eller på servrar som du inte själv har fullständig kontroll över'. It also covers print and exhibitions. Purely internal use on systems you control appears not to count (the summary model's reading; not quoted verbatim). Implication: process drone data locally on the RTX laptop.

findings.claim: The permit is free but slow: Lantmäteriet's current estimate is about 65 working days. Lantmäteriet cannot retouch 3D models or video, so a 3D model or splat is approved or refused as a whole.
findings.details: Application page: 'Vi handlägger just nu ärenden från vecka 29. Den uppskattade handläggningstiden är ca 65 arbetsdagar'. Uploads are limited to 5 GB per file, 5,000 files and 250 GB in total; larger sets go by post. You must mark the area on a map. FAQ: 'Vi kan retuschera bildmaterial ... JPG, JPEG, PNG och TIF' but 'Vi har inte möjlighet att retuschera i videofilmer, 3-D modeller, radardata'. The pages read did not say whether you can apply before capturing. Several SVT reports describe record-long waiting times.

findings.claim: A forest exemption from the permit exists but is narrow. The landowner must have ordered the material or taken it, it may show no vehicles or human activity other than forestry, it may show no power lines, and no zoomed-out surroundings may be visible.
findings.details: Lantmäteriet exemptions page: 'Skogsmark är undantagen ... Det ska vara markägaren som har beställt materialet eller varit fotograf. Bilderna får inte innehålla fordon eller andra mänskliga aktiviteter förutom sådant som tillhör skogsbruket. Om materialet exempelvis innehåller kraftledning gäller inte undantaget.' The general caveat reads 'undantaget inte gäller för en mer utzoomad vy där omgivningarna syns' and 'Om du är osäker ska du ansöka'. Other exemptions cover single homes, public places, public events, farmland, building sites, golf courses, quarries, landfills, pre-1950 photos and satellite images. A drone grid over a forest plot with a road, parked car, power line or buildings in view falls outside the exemption. Researchers walking under the canopy may also count as non-forestry human activity (interpretation).

findings.claim: Consequence for the a/b/c options: in option (b), the merged splat as a whole becomes permit-bound drone-derived material, so the ground model cannot go public alone. In option (c), the ground layer can be published at once and the aerial layer added only after a permit.
findings.details: Inference from the findings above: §9 scope, 3D models covered, no retouching of 3D models. Architecture: give each source module a 'dissemination_clearance' attribute (ground = cleared; drone = pending/approved/denied, with the Lantmäteriet case number). The public viewer build should leave out uncleared layers and any splat trained on drone images.

findings.claim: EU Open category rules: VLOS; at most 120 m above the closest point of the terrain; A1, A2 and A3 subcategories set by class label; legacy drones without a class label are limited to A1 (<250 g) or A3.
findings.details: EASA: A1 'fly over people but not over assemblies of people' (C0; C1 must not overfly uninvolved persons). A2 (C2): at least 30 m horizontal from uninvolved persons, 5 m with low-speed mode. A3 (C2, C3, C4, legacy): 'reasonably expects that no uninvolved person will be endangered' and 'at least 150 metres from residential, commercial, industrial or recreational areas'. Class weights: C0 <250 g, C1 <900 g, C2 <4 kg, C3/C4 <25 kg. Legacy UAS placed on the market before 1 Jan 2024 may fly 'without the need to apply any retrofit/sticker' in A1 (<250 g) or A3 (<25 kg). Hilly terrain: stay within 120 m of the closest point of the terrain. The regulation does not define 'recreational area'; it may vary by season and the operator must assess it. This matters in Swedish forests open to the public.

findings.claim: Direct Remote ID has been mandatory since 1 Jan 2024 for drones labelled C1, C2, C3, C5 and C6, and for Specific-category operations. C0, C4 and legacy drones are exempt. The operator must upload the operator registration number to the drone.
findings.details: EASA: drones with C1, C2, C3, C5 and C6 labels 'are already equipped with a remote identification system'. The broadcast includes serial number, operator registration number, pilot position or take-off point, and drone position. The 'same UAS operator registration number must be uploaded onto all drones'. Legacy drones are only 'recommended' to carry Remote ID. The C0/C4 exemption comes from the Irish IAA guidance as summarised (PDF only partly parsed).

findings.claim: Coming EU change: EASA Opinion 06/2026 (18 Sep 2026) proposes lowering the registration, Remote ID and training threshold from 250 g to 100 g, checking operators' identity before registration, and tightening the geographical-zone framework. It is not yet adopted.
findings.details: Sent to the European Commission for adoption; it follows NPA 2026-103 and the Commission's Drone and Counter-Drone Security Action Plan of 11 Feb 2026. Transition: drones under 900 g placed on the market before [entry into force + 12 months] would not need a Remote ID add-on, and all legacy UAS would be exempt from the take-off-prevention function. Dronewatch expects the first changes around mid-2028 and the full framework not 'before 2031 at the earliest'. No effect on a 2026–27 test, but it argues for buying a class-labelled drone with Remote ID and for getting the A1/A3 card even for a sub-250 g drone.

findings.claim: In Sweden, operator registration with Transportstyrelsen is required for any camera drone, including those under 250 g. It costs a 190 SEK application fee plus 250 SEK per year, and the operator ID must be displayed on the drone.
findings.details: An operator ID is required outdoors if the drone weighs at least 250 g, can transfer more than 80 J, has a camera, microphone or sensor, or flies in the Specific category. Registration is through the 'Drönarsidan' e-service, for private persons or company signatories. The annual fee is billed to anyone registered on 1 January, and deregistering mid-year does not refund it. Fees have been unchanged since 1 Jan 2025. ID shown on the drone: 'readable at least when the UAS is on the ground'; QR codes are allowed. Specific-category fees: declaration verification 1,500 SEK; annual supervision base fee 6,500 SEK, plus 2,800 SEK per STS declaration; LUC 65,000 SEK per year.

findings.claim: Pilot competency in Sweden: the A1/A3 online test (600 SEK, valid 5 years) is mandatory for drones of 250 g or more, and flying without it has been a crime since 1 Jan 2026. The A2 certificate costs 850 SEK (600 SEK if the A1/A3 fee is already paid) and must now be taken under supervision at an authorised drone school.
findings.details: A1/A3: 40 multiple-choice questions, 75% to pass, renewable from three months before expiry; retake 600 SEK, renewal 550 SEK. A2: an extra 30-question exam, which per Transportstyrelsen must now be taken under supervision at an ADS (a secondary source dates this to 23 Oct 2025), plus a declared practical self-training. C0 needs only the manual to be read. Transportstyrelsen press release (4 Dec 2025): from 1 Jan 2026, flying a drone of 250 g or more without a card is punishable with 30–150 day-fines, and up to 6 months' prison in the worst cases. Flying without a card in other ways can also break luftfartslagen (2010:500).

findings.claim: Insurance: the EU's 785/2004 exempts model aircraft under 20 kg, and Transportstyrelsen says insurance is not required for drones under 20 kg used for leisure. For work flights it points to 785/2004 without a clear answer, so check Hexagon's liability cover.
findings.details: 785/2004 Art. 2(2)(b) exempts 'model aircraft with an MTOM of less than 20 kg'. The minimum third-party cover for aircraft under 500 kg is 0.75 million SDR. Transportstyrelsen: 'För drönaroperatörer som endast använder drönare under 20 kg för fritidsändamål ... krävs inte försäkring', while other operations are referred to 785/2004. The EASA FAQ notes that most member states require third-party insurance even for lighter drones. Sweden does not appear to (medium confidence).

findings.claim: Swedish airspace: check the LFV drone map before each flight. Within 5 km of a runway, ATC permission is always needed. Elsewhere in a control zone the limit is 50 m AGL (10 m at military airports) at speeds of 25 m/s or less. Coordinate with any heliport within 1,000 m. R-areas and protected sites (skyddsobjekt) are off limits.
findings.details: Transportstyrelsen: 'Closer than 5km to any runway, you need permission from air traffic control regardless of the altitude'. 'Flygning närmare än 1 000 m från helikopterflygplats får endast ske i samråd med berörd helikopterflygplats'. Permanent R-areas cover nuclear plants, prisons, protected nature areas and military sites. Temporary restrictions are published in AIP SUP and NOTAM (AROWeb). Since April 2025 the LFV map can generate an ATC permission request PDF for Göteborg-Landvetter's CTR (pilot programme). Flying over or near a designated skyddsobjekt is banned (skyddslag 2010:305). At night, a green flashing light is required.

findings.claim: Protected nature in Sweden: landing aircraft, drones included, is banned in all national parks without a Länsstyrelsen permit, and some parks also have Transportstyrelsen flight restrictions. Nature reserves may ban take-off and landing. Bird protection areas often have a seasonal access ban (typically 1 Apr–15 Jul). Disturbing breeding birds is banned.
findings.details: Länsstyrelsen Gävleborg: 'Det är förbjudet i samtliga nationalparker att landa med luftfartyg eller luftfarkost. Dit räknas bland annat drönare.' Färnebofjärden needs permits from both the Länsstyrelsen and Transportstyrelsen, and processing times are long. Transportstyrelsen: 'Start- och landningsförbud kan råda i Naturreservat', so contact the Länsstyrelsen. Naturvårdsverket recommends handling protected areas through UAS geographical zones, which then appear on the LFV map. Artskyddsförordningen 4 § bans deliberately disturbing wild birds, especially during breeding. A police report followed a drone flight in Fulufjället in 2021. The typical 1 Apr–15 Jul period comes from a search summary only; check each area's rules.

findings.claim: Landowner permission: allemansrätten does not give a right to run drone operations. Overflight is not prohibited by aviation rules, but take-off or landing on another's land that causes appreciable damage or nuisance needs the owner's consent. Getting written consent is also the practical route to the forest exemption.
findings.details: Lawline: no Transportstyrelsen rule prohibits overflying another's plot. Secondary and academic sources describe Swedish aviation law: take-off and landing outside airports must not cause appreciable damage or nuisance, otherwise the owner's consent is required. The exact provision (likely in TSFS rules on landing sites) was not confirmed from the primary text; the Luftfartsförordning (2010:770) fetch found only 6 kap. 2 § (a Transportstyrelsen mandate). Inference: get a written agreement with the landowner that covers the drone flights, the ground capture and that the landowner 'orders' the material (for the forest exemption).

findings.claim: Privacy: GDPR and the camera surveillance act (kamerabevakningslagen) apply only if people or number plates can be identified. A drone flown on site for a mapping session is generally not 'camera surveillance', and since 1 Aug 2026 no actor needs a camera surveillance permit. GDPR still applies to the Insta360 and drone footage, so blur before publishing.
findings.details: IMY: 'Om ingen person eller någon annan uppgift som kan härledas till en viss person kommer med i bild, gäller inte dataskyddsförordningen eller kamerabevakningslagen'. Filming outside your private sphere makes you the data controller. Kamerabevakningslag 2018:1200 §3 defines camera surveillance as equipment that 'utan att manövreras på platsen' is used for 'varaktig eller regelbundet upprepad personbevakning'. IMY reportedly notes that automation alone does not make equipment 'manoeuvred on site' (via a secondary source), so a pre-programmed grid over people would be a grey zone. SFS 2026:1373 (in force 1 Aug 2026) removed the permit requirement for all actors; the signage duty (§15) remains where the law applies. For a forest plot with no people in view, neither law applies.

findings.claim: How common mapping-capable drones map onto subcategories: DJI Mini 5 Pro is C0 (EASA confirmed C0 despite about 252 g), so A1 with the minimum paperwork. DJI Mavic 4 Pro and Matrice 4E (mechanical shutter, mapping) are C2: A3 in a forest with A1/A3, or A2 near people with the A2 certificate.
findings.details: Mini 5 Pro: declaration of conformity for C0, with a weight tolerance under prEN 4709-001 that EASA accepts. Matrice 4 series: C2-certified, 4/3-inch 20 MP wide camera with mechanical shutter. Mavic 4 Pro: EASA C2. Drone choice is another agent's topic; this only gives the regulatory mapping.

findings.claim: The Specific category is needed only when leaving Open limits: BVLOS (for example, long transects over tropical canopy), flights above 120 m, flights over assemblies, or drones over 25 kg. It works through an STS declaration (C5/C6 drone plus an STS certificate), a PDRA authorisation, or SORA 2.5.
findings.details: Transportstyrelsen offers PDRA-S01/S02 and STS-01/02 declarations. ED Decision 2025/018/R (29 Sep 2025) brought in SORA 2.5 AMC/GM, consolidated in the June 2026 Easy Access Rules. Swedish STS certificate: 800 SEK to issue, 500 SEK per year. A VLOS grid or orbit over a 10x10 m to 1 ha forest plot fits in Open.

findings.claim: In tropical countries the rules depend on the country and are usually harder for foreign operators. EU A1/A3 certificates are generally not recognised. Expect per-flight airspace approval, local registration (often closed to foreigners), radio homologation, and mapping or security approvals.
findings.details: Brazil (secondary sources; the ANAC site was behind a CAPTCHA): RBAC 100 (ANAC Resolution 805) has been in force since 16 Jun 2026, replacing RBAC-E 94. SISANT registration for drones over 250 g needs a gov.br account and CPF. Every flight needs DECEA SARPAS authorisation, the drone needs ANATEL homologation, the ANAC theory exam is enforced from 1 Jan 2027, third-party insurance is mandatory (§100.37), and foreign certificates are not validated. Malaysia (CAAM primary page): Standard ATF applied for at least 14 working days ahead. Camera drones may not fly within 150 m of designated areas, within 50 m of people, vehicles or structures, or over assemblies of more than 1,000 people without authorisation. JUPEM approval is needed for 'aerial photo, aerial mapping, Lidar'. CGSO governs protected places. Sabah and Sarawak (Borneo rainforest) need extra authorisation. Costa Rica (secondary): DGAC directive DO-002-OPS-RPAS (Jul 2022); registration and commercial authorisation; SINAC protected areas need special authorisation plus a MINAE environmental permit. Indonesia (secondary): PM 37/2020 and PM 63/2021 (CASR Part 107); foreigners cannot register a drone and must partner with a local company; national parks need a BKSDA permit.

recommendations.recommendation: Keep phase 1 (Swedish forest test) ground-only, with BLK2GO and Insta360 on foot. Regulation is one more reason not to bring the drone earlier.
recommendations.rationale: Ground-captured data is outside lag 2016:319, so no aviation paperwork, Lantmäteriet permit or 3-month wait is needed, and the result can go on the web right away (after blurring faces and plates). Adding a drone brings registration, competency, a site and zone check, landowner consent and, before publishing, a permit taking about 65 working days that can be refused with no retouching option.
recommendations.alternatives: If a drone must be tested early, fly it for internal R&D only. Keep the data on systems you control, and publish only after a permit is granted.

recommendations.recommendation: If drone imagery is added in Sweden, show it as a separate aerial layer (option c) rather than merging it into the ground splat (option b), at least for anything that will be published.
recommendations.rationale: A merged splat is drone-derived as a whole and needs a permit before any web sharing, and Lantmäteriet cannot retouch 3D models. A separate layer keeps the ground model publishable and confines permit risk to the aerial layer.
recommendations.alternatives: Train both a merged splat (internal and evaluation use) and a ground-only splat (public build), and publish the merged one only after approval.

recommendations.recommendation: Add a per-source 'dissemination_clearance' attribute to the common source-module interface. For example: ground sources = cleared; drone = pending/approved/denied, with the Lantmäteriet case number. The public viewer build should leave out uncleared layers and any model trained on uncleared data.
recommendations.rationale: This turns the legal rule into a build-time gate, so drone-derived content is not published or uploaded by mistake. Uploading to cloud or third-party servers already counts as dissemination.
recommendations.alternatives: A manual release checklist only (more error-prone).

recommendations.recommendation: Process drone imagery locally on the RTX 3080 Ti laptop (COLMAP/GLOMAP and an open-source splat trainer). Do not use cloud photogrammetry or cloud splat services for Swedish drone data until a permit is granted.
recommendations.rationale: Lantmäteriet counts storage on 'molntjänster eller på servrar som du inte själv har fullständig kontroll över' as dissemination.
recommendations.alternatives: A Hexagon-controlled on-prem server may count as internal, but confirm with Lantmäteriet or Hexagon legal.

recommendations.recommendation: For the first drone flights, use a class-labelled drone with Remote ID. C0 (for example, Mini 5 Pro class) or C1 allows A1 with the least friction. Choose C2 (for example, Matrice 4E with mechanical shutter) only if image quality needs it, and fly it in A3 away from people. Get the A1/A3 card (600 SEK) even for a C0 drone.
recommendations.rationale: C0/C1 in A1 avoids A3's rule of 150 m from recreational areas, which is unclear in public-access forests. Legacy non-class drones over 250 g are limited to A3. EASA Opinion 06/2026 will push training and registration down to 100 g, and flying a drone of 250 g or more without a card has been a crime since 1 Jan 2026.
recommendations.alternatives: C2 with the A2 certificate (850 SEK, supervised exam at a drone school) to fly within 30 m (5 m in low-speed mode) of uninvolved people.

recommendations.recommendation: Register the operator as the legal entity that runs the flights (likely the Hexagon unit, through a company signatory) and confirm that drones are covered by its liability insurance and internal drone and data policies.
recommendations.rationale: These are work flights, not leisure. Transportstyrelsen's insurance exemption is worded for leisure, and the operator is also the GDPR controller.
recommendations.alternatives: The user registers as a private operator (190 + 250 SEK per year) for a pure personal test, but then the data's ownership and use for Hexagon get complicated.

recommendations.recommendation: Include in the plan's drone phase a step-by-step pre-flight checklist: (1) choose the drone class and subcategory; (2) register the operator, label the drone with the operator ID and enter it into Remote ID; (3) get the A1/A3 card, plus A2 if a C2 will fly near people; (4) check insurance; (5) check the LFV drone map, NOTAM and AIP SUP for control zones (5 km rule, 50 m or 10 m limits), R-areas, UAS zones, heliports within 1,000 m and protected sites; (6) check the site's protection status (national park, nature reserve rules, bird protection season, breeding birds) and get a Länsstyrelsen permit if needed; (7) get written landowner consent that covers 'ordering' the material; (8) plan the flight within Open limits (VLOS from a clearing, possibly with an observer, at most 120 m AGL, daylight, distances to uninvolved people); (9) avoid capturing identifiable people and plan blurring; (10) keep data local; (11) apply for the permit about 3 months before any publication, marking the area on a map; (12) keep flight logs and certificates.
recommendations.rationale: This covers every requirement found and the order in which each one blocks the next.
recommendations.alternatives: Hire a Swedish licensed drone service company that handles operator duties. The dissemination permit is still needed for publication.

recommendations.recommendation: For tropical campaigns, budget a country-specific legal review months ahead and plan to partner with a locally licensed operator. Check the aviation authority's registration (often closed to foreigners), per-flight airspace approval, radio homologation and customs, mapping or survey and security approvals (for example, Malaysia JUPEM for aerial photo, mapping and LiDAR), protected-area permits, research or fieldwork permits for foreigners, and any limits on exporting or publishing geodata.
recommendations.rationale: Brazil, Malaysia, Costa Rica and Indonesia all impose extra approvals, and EU certificates are generally not recognised.
recommendations.alternatives: Run tropical tests ground-only (LiDAR + 360 camera) to avoid aviation permits. Protected-area and research permits may still apply.
