risks: The dissemination permit for drone-derived models can be refused or delayed (about 65 working days now, with record backlogs reported). Lantmäteriet cannot retouch 3D models, so a merged splat (option b) could become unpublishable as a whole.

Uploading drone images or models to any cloud or third-party server (cloud photogrammetry, CDN hosting, sharing links) counts as dissemination before a permit. This affects pipeline and hosting choices.
Relying on the forest exemption is legally fragile. A visible road, vehicle, power line, building or wide view of the surroundings voids it, and the person disseminating carries the risk.
A3 operations (C2/C3/legacy drones) need 150 m from 'recreational areas', which the regulation does not define, and Swedish forests are open to the public. C0/C1 in A1 avoids this.
VLOS is hard to keep in a forest. Launching from clearings and staying above the canopy is required in the Open category; flying under the canopy quickly loses VLOS.
The test site may lie in a control zone, near a hospital heliport, in a nature reserve or national park, or in a bird protection area with a seasonal ban. This is unknown until the location is fixed.
EU rule change (Opinion 06/2026: 100 g threshold, operator identity checks, geo-zone framework) may change requirements during the project, probably from about 2028.
Corporate constraints: Hexagon may have internal policies on drone brands (for example, DJI), data security, insurance or a flight-operations manual. Not researched; background knowledge only.

Tropical campaigns: foreigners are often barred from registering drones (Indonesia, Brazil without a CPF). Expect multi-agency approvals (aviation, mapping or survey, defence, environment), customs and radio-homologation hurdles, and long lead times. Researching only in-country partners may be the only legal route.
GDPR exposure from identifiable people in the Insta360 or drone footage published in the browser viewer. A face and plate blurring step is needed in the pipeline.
open_questions: Whether Lantmäteriet treats a Gaussian splat file (.ply/.spz/.sog) exactly like a 3D model, which file it wants submitted (the model itself or renders), and whether a permit covers later re-trained versions of the same area.

Whether sharing inside Hexagon (company-controlled servers, internal web viewer) counts as dissemination. The FAQ wording points to 'servers you do not fully control'; confirm with Lantmäteriet or Hexagon legal.
Whether you can apply before capturing (pre-approval for an area) or only with the finished material. The pages read did not say.
The exact Swedish provision on landowner consent for drone take-off and landing (likely in TSFS); the primary text was not found.
Whether the test plot lies in any CTR, UAS geographical zone, nature reserve with a take-off/landing ban, Natura 2000 site or bird protection area.

The exact LMFS exemption text and the Naturvårdsverket guidance on flight restrictions in protected areas: the PDFs could not be parsed, so details rest on Lantmäteriet's web pages and secondary sources.
Primary-source confirmation of the tropical rules (the ANAC, Costa Rica DGAC and Indonesian regulator pages were blocked or not reached; the WebSearch budget ran out).
questions_for_user: Where exactly is the Swedish test plot (municipality or coordinates), and who owns the land? This decides control zones, protected-area status and landowner consent.
Will the drone be flown privately or on behalf of Hexagon (operator registration, insurance, GDPR controller), and does Hexagon have an internal drone policy, for example on DJI hardware?
Is the goal to publish drone-derived content publicly in the browser? If so, by when? Applying for the Lantmäteriet permit needs about 3 months of lead time.
Will any processing or hosting happen on cloud or third-party servers? For Swedish drone data that counts as dissemination.
Which tropical countries are planned, and will you work with a local partner organisation that can hold the drone permits?

tools_and_licenses.notes: Shows control zones, R-areas, UAS geographical zones and temporary restrictions; can generate ATC request PDFs for Landvetter's CTR (pilot programme since Apr 2025). Check before every flight.

tools_and_licenses.tool: Transportstyrelsen Drönarsidan e-service (operator registration, A1/A3 test)
tools_and_licenses.license: Government service; fees 190 SEK + 250 SEK/yr (registration), 600 SEK (A1/A3)
tools_and_licenses.notes: Private persons or company signatories can register.
About 65 working days; file transfer up to 5 GB per file, 250 GB in total; 3D models cannot be retouched.
Temporary airspace restrictions.

verdicts.claim: Lag 2016:319 §9 still requires a Lantmäteriet dissemination permit (spridningstillstånd) before spreading drone-derived material of Swedish land, including 3D models, as of Oct 2026. The only 2026 amendment, SFS 2026:1378, changed §6 and not §9.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed. The §9 wording is unchanged and the drone material is covered: Lantmäteriet names drones, and its form lists 3D-modeller, laserdata and höjddata. The lagen.nu change register for SFS 2026:1378 reads 'ändr. 6 §', in force 2026-08-01. The preparatory work is Prop. 2025/26:256 (a tachograph bill) and Bet. 2025/26:TU22, so the §6 change looks like a consequential edit. The report says §6 covers 'exemptions for authorities'. That description does not match the current text. §6 now bans aerial photography in or of military restricted areas 'när det råder höjd beredskap, eller under annan tid som regeringen beslutar med hänsyn till Sveriges försvarsberedskap'. The project is not affected, because R-areas are already closed to drones. SFS 2024:880 (in force 2024-11-08) repealed §13, which is also irrelevant here.

verdicts.claim: Ground-captured data (handheld BLK2GO plus an Insta360 carried on foot) is outside the permit duty, so option (a) can be published without Lantmäteriet. Only GDPR applies.
verdicts.correction: The permit part is confirmed. Lag 2016:319 regulates only hydrographic survey (§§3-5), aerial photography (§§6-8) and the spread of hydrographic or aerially captured information (§9). It has no provision on land surveying, terrestrial LiDAR or databases. The Lantmäteriet FAQ says a permit is needed only for filming from luftfartyg, and that photos from high points with ground contact need none. 'Only GDPR applies' is too strong, though. Under skyddslag (2010:305) §7, the access ban for a designated skyddsobjekt can carry a ban on 'avbildningar, beskrivningar eller mätningar' (photographing, describing or measuring). Breaking it is punished under §30a with fines or up to 1 year in prison, and this applies to ground capture too. Check for signposted protected sites, such as substations or military land, near the plot.

verdicts.claim: 'Dissemination' includes emailing, publishing on a website or social media, and storing on cloud services or servers you do not fully control.
verdicts.correction: The FAQ wording quoted in the report is verbatim. Note that the FAQ lists 'lagrar det i molntjänster' as its own example. Corporate OneDrive or SharePoint sync therefore probably counts, as do GitHub or Git LFS and any CDN or artifact host. This matters because the project folder is under the Windows Desktop, which is often synced to OneDrive. The FAQ says nothing about internal use within an organisation.

verdicts.claim: The permit is free, takes about 65 working days (cases from week 29 are being handled now), and Lantmäteriet cannot retouch 3D models or video.
verdicts.correction: All confirmed: 'Att ansöka om spridningstillstånd är kostnadsfritt'; 'ca 65 arbetsdagar'; retouching only for JPG/JPEG/PNG/TIF, and not for video, 3D models, radar or RAW files. The upload limits of 5 GB per file, 5,000 files and 250 GB per delivery are also confirmed. The report left one point open, and it is now answered: you cannot apply in advance ('Du kan inte heller söka spridningstillstånd i förväg'). The application must include the finished material.

verdicts.claim: The forest exemption is narrow: the landowner must have ordered or taken the material, there may be no vehicles or non-forestry human activity, no power lines, and no zoomed-out views of the surroundings.
verdicts.correction: The quotes match the Lantmäteriet exemptions page word for word, including 'Om du är osäker ska du ansöka'. That page does not name the LMFS regulation number.

verdicts.claim: Riksdag motion 2025/26:2626, which asked for a review of the permit legislation, was rejected.
verdicts.correction: Rickard Nordin (C) filed it on 6 Oct 2025. It was rejected (avslag) through Bet. 2025/26:FöU9. None of the pages fetched shows a pending government bill that would change §9.

verdicts.claim: Since 1 Aug 2026 (SFS 2026:1373), no one needs a camera surveillance permit. GDPR and kamerabevakningslagen apply only if people or number plates can be identified.
verdicts.correction: The date and the act are wrong. The permit requirement was removed by SFS 2025:220 (published 18 Mar 2025, in force 1 Apr 2025). SFS 2026:1373 (in force 1 Aug 2026) changed only §11 (exemptions for certain surveillance) and §16 (exemptions from the duty to inform). The IMY points are confirmed: the laws apply only when people or other personal data can be identified, and number plates count as personal data. IMY also says 'För kamerabevakning med drönare gäller samma regler som när du filmar med en vanlig bevakningskamera'. The report's reading, that a drone piloted on site is usually not 'kamerabevakning' under the §3 'utan att manövreras på platsen' test, is plausible but not stated by IMY.

verdicts.claim: Insurance: not required for leisure drones under 20 kg. Sweden does not appear to require third-party insurance for lighter drones (medium confidence); for work flights, check Hexagon's cover.
verdicts.correction: Transportstyrelsen exempts only operators who use drones under 20 kg 'för fritidsändamål, uppvisnings- eller rekreationsverksamhet'. Other drone operations fall under Regulation (EC) 785/2004. In practice this means work flights for Hexagon need third-party liability insurance, with a minimum of 0.75 million SDR per accident for MTOM under 500 kg (785/2004 Art. 7). Treat insurance as mandatory for Hexagon flights, not as something to check.

verdicts.claim: Swedish operator registration is required for any camera drone, including under 250 g. It costs 190 SEK to apply plus 250 SEK per year, and the ID must be shown on the drone.
verdicts.correction: The fees are confirmed (fee page last updated 2026-01-01). The camera rule is confirmed by Transportstyrelsen and by 2019/947 Art. 14(5). The EASA FAQ adds a toy exception: drones under 250 g that comply with Toy Directive 2009/48/EC. Display rule confirmed: readable on the ground without aids other than glasses. Specific-category fees: declaration 1,500 SEK, STS add-on 2,800 SEK, operational authorisation base fee 6,500 SEK, LUC 65,000 SEK per year.

verdicts.claim: The A1/A3 test costs 600 SEK, has 40 questions, needs 75% to pass and is valid 5 years. Since 1 Jan 2026, flying a drone of 250 g or more without the card is a crime (30–150 day-fines, up to 6 months' prison).
verdicts.correction: Confirmed by the Transportstyrelsen card page, the fee table (retake 600 SEK, renewal 550 SEK) and the 4 Dec 2025 press release. Transportstyrelsen calls the 1 Jan 2026 package 'nya och utökade straffsanktioner', so it covers more than the card offence. A C0 pilot only has to be familiar with the manufacturer's instructions (UAS.OPEN.020(4)).

verdicts.claim: The A2 CofC costs 850 SEK (600 SEK if the A1/A3 fee is already paid), has 30 extra questions, and must be taken under supervision at an authorised drone school (ADS), plus a declared practical self-training.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed: 'måste ske övervakat hos en auktoriserad drönarskola (ADS)'. The start date of 23 Oct 2025 is not on the Transportstyrelsen page and could not be checked against a primary source. The STS remote pilot certificate costs 800 SEK to issue, 500 SEK per year and 200 SEK to renew.

verdicts.claim: Swedish airspace: ATC permission within 5 km of a runway; elsewhere in a control zone, at most 50 m AGL (10 m at military airports) at speeds of 25 m/s or less; coordinate with heliports within 1,000 m; check the LFV drone map and AROWeb.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed (Transportstyrelsen page updated 2025-09-17). The LFV map at dronechart.lfv.se has, since 7 Apr 2025, generated ATC request PDFs for Göteborg-Landvetter, with more airports planned. New since the report: the temporary central-Malmö restriction ESR644 is now permanent as ESR130.

verdicts.claim: National parks ban landing drones without a Länsstyrelsen permit, and some (Färnebofjärden) also need Transportstyrelsen permission. Nature reserves may ban take-off and landing.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed verbatim by Länsstyrelsen Gävleborg and Transportstyrelsen ('Start- och landningsförbud kan råda i Naturreservat och nationalparker'). The typical bird-sanctuary period of 1 Apr–15 Jul could not be checked; a Länsstyrelsen page returned 404 and no searches were left. Treat it as unverified and check each site's own regulations.

verdicts.claim: EU Open category: VLOS; within 120 m of the closest point of the earth's surface; A1 (C0 may overfly uninvolved people but not assemblies; C1 must not overfly uninvolved people), A2 (C2, 30 m or 5 m in low-speed mode), A3 (150 m from residential, commercial, industrial or recreational areas); legacy drones in A1 if under 250 g, otherwise A3 if under 25 kg.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed by EASA pages and the consolidated text of 2019/947 (UAS.OPEN.010(2), .020, .030, .040). None of the pages read defines 'recreational area', so that remains the operator's judgement.

verdicts.claim: Direct Remote ID has been mandatory since 1 Jan 2024 for C1, C2, C3, C5 and C6 drones and for the Specific category; C0, C4 and legacy drones are exempt; the operator number must be uploaded.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed for C1, C2, C3, C5, C6, the Specific category, the upload duty and the broadcast contents. Legacy drones are 'recommended' to carry Remote ID. The EASA page does not mention the C0/C4 exemption explicitly; it rests on the 2019/945 class annexes (background knowledge, medium confidence).

verdicts.claim: EASA Opinion 06/2026 (18 Sep 2026, not yet adopted) would lower registration, Remote ID and training thresholds to 100 g and add identity checks. Drones of 900 g or less already on the market would not need a Remote ID add-on. First effects around mid-2028.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed. The EASA status is 'Pending Official Publication'. The Opinion follows the Commission's Drone and Counter-Drone Security Action Plan of Feb 2026. It also exempts all existing UAS from the take-off-prevention function and brings in national conditions for geographical zones. Dronewatch's 'mid-2028 / 2031 at the earliest' comes from its 23 Jun 2026 article on NPA 2026-103, not on the Opinion itself.

verdicts.claim: The DJI Mini 5 Pro is C0 (EASA confirmed despite about 252 g); the Matrice 4E is C2.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed for the Mini 5 Pro: EASA cites the ±3% tolerance in prEN 4709-001, the declared mass is 249.9 g, and real units weigh 252–253 g. This applies only to the certified configuration. It probably does not hold with a heavier 'Plus' battery (background knowledge, unverified). The Matrice 4 series is C2 per DJI, with a 4/3-inch 20 MP wide camera on the 4E. The DJI FAQ page read does not mention the mechanical shutter.

verdicts.claim: In the Specific category, SORA 2.5 was introduced by ED Decision 2025/018/R and consolidated in the June 2026 Easy Access Rules. Sweden offers STS-01/02 and PDRA declarations.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed: the Easy Access Rules revision of 30 Jun 2026 includes ED Decision 2025/018/R. Transportstyrelsen news says SORA 2.5 applied in Sweden immediately from 30 Sep 2025, and SORA 2.0 applications need not be resubmitted. Transportstyrelsen also lists PDRA-G01..G03 in addition to S01/S02.

verdicts.claim: Malaysia: the CAAM Authorisation to Fly (ATF) must be applied for at least 14 working days ahead; JUPEM approval is needed for aerial photo, mapping or LiDAR; Sabah and Sarawak need extra authorisation.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed on the CAAM primary page. Other limits there: 150 m from residential, commercial, industrial or recreational areas; 50 m from people, vehicles or structures (30 m at take-off and landing); 400 ft AGL; assemblies over 1,000 people need authorisation. Sabah needs Jabatan Tanah dan Ukur Sabah, and Sarawak needs the Premier's Office. The framework is Civil Aviation Directive 6011.

verdicts.claim: Brazil: RBAC 100 in force since 16 Jun 2026; SISANT registration for drones over 250 g; DECEA SARPAS authorisation for every flight; ANATEL homologation; ANAC exam enforced from 1 Jan 2027; mandatory insurance.
verdicts.correction: The ANAC primary site (gov.br/anac) returned a CAPTCHA. A secondary source (aerocopilot) agrees on every point and adds Resolution 806/2026 for drones of 250 g or less, and that recreational flights in designated areas are exempt from SARPAS. Keep at low confidence until checked against ANAC or DECEA.

verdicts.claim: Indonesia: foreigners cannot register drones and need a local company; national parks need a BKSDA permit. Costa Rica: DGAC authorisation plus a SINAC/MINAE permit for protected areas.
verdicts.correction: Only secondary sources were reachable. Drone-traveller (updated 1 Oct 2026) cites PM 63/2021 section 107.89: only Indonesian citizens and companies may register. It mentions park fees (Komodo) but not BKSDA by name in the extract. The Costa Rica secondary source (5 May 2026) confirms dual DGAC plus SINAC/MINAE authorisation and mentions 8 km airport coordination zones and mandatory liability insurance. No primary regulator page was confirmed.

verdicts.claim: Landowner: take-off or landing on another's land that causes appreciable damage or nuisance needs the owner's consent (Swedish aviation law).
verdicts.correction: The cited Lawline answer dates from 31 Dec 2018 (pre-EU rules). It says only that flying over another's land requires meeting the safety rules; it does not state the consent rule. Luftfartsförordning (2010:770) 6 kap. 2 § only empowers Transportstyrelsen to issue rules on landing sites. 'Avsevärt men för markägarna' appears in 6 kap. 23 §, which concerns obstacle marking and has nothing to do with drones. The advice to get written landowner consent remains sound, but the legal basis was not confirmed.

verdicts.claim: 'Several SVT reports describe record-long waiting times' for permits.
verdicts.correction: The cited SVT article dates from 7 Aug 2022. At that time the handling time was 40 working days, and applications had grown from about 700 to over 23,000 in five years, with about 30,000 expected in 2022. It is stale context. The current figure of about 65 working days comes from Lantmäteriet itself.

missed_developments.claim: You cannot apply for a dissemination permit in advance. You can apply only with the finished material.
missed_developments.details: Lantmäteriet FAQ: 'Du kan inte heller söka spridningstillstånd i förväg', because protected objects change and each case needs a total-defence assessment. This settles the report's open question. Plan consequence: the order is capture, local processing, final model, application with the model and a map of the area, about 65 working days (roughly 13 weeks) of waiting, then publication. Each newly trained version, or a re-export that changes content, will probably need a new application (inference). Since 3D models cannot be retouched, edit the model yourself before applying, for example by cropping out a road or power line.

missed_developments.claim: Elevated capture from a mast or pole with ground contact needs no Lantmäteriet permit and falls under no aviation rules.
missed_developments.details: The FAQ says images from high points with ground contact (mountains, buildings, cranes) need no permit; only luftfartyg trigger §9. A telescopic mast with the Insta360 (a few metres up) is therefore a cheap, permit-free way to get oblique views from above under the canopy. Drones (tethered ones too, background knowledge) remain aircraft. The drone-vs-ground comparison should consider this as an alternative.

missed_developments.claim: Drone work flights for Hexagon need mandatory third-party liability insurance. The report treated this as optional.
missed_developments.details: Transportstyrelsen exempts only drones under 20 kg used for leisure, display or recreation. Other operations fall under Regulation 785/2004, with a minimum of 0.75 M SDR per accident for MTOM under 500 kg. Hexagon must confirm its cover before the first drone flight.

missed_developments.claim: Skyddslag (2010:305) can ban photographing, describing or measuring a designated protected site (skyddsobjekt). This applies to ground LiDAR and 360 capture too, not only drones.
missed_developments.details: Skyddslag §7, second paragraph: the access ban can be combined with a 'förbud mot att göra avbildningar, beskrivningar eller mätningar av eller inom skyddsobjektet'. Under §30a, unlawful depiction is punished with fines or up to 1 year in prison. Guards may intervene against drones near such sites (§11). Add a skyddsobjekt check (look for signs; substations and military land) to the site checklist for every source module, not just the drone.

missed_developments.claim: Syncing drone imagery to cloud storage, including the Windows Desktop folder synced to OneDrive, probably already counts as dissemination before a permit.
missed_developments.details: Lantmäteriet lists storing material 'i molntjänster' as dissemination. The project lives under C:\Users\...\Desktop\Code, which Windows 11 often syncs to OneDrive. Keep raw drone data and drone-derived models in a non-synced local folder. Keep them out of Git remotes, LFS and artifact or CDN hosting until a permit is granted.

missed_developments.claim: The camera surveillance permit requirement was removed on 1 Apr 2025 (SFS 2025:220), not on 1 Aug 2026.
missed_developments.details: SFS 2026:1373 (in force 1 Aug 2026) amended only kamerabevakningslag §11 and §16. The project is not affected, but the date in the report is wrong.

missed_developments.claim: In Sweden, SORA 2.5 applied immediately from 30 Sep 2025. On 1 Jan 2026 Sweden also brought in a broader package of drone sanctions ('nya och utökade straffsanktioner').
missed_developments.details: The Transportstyrelsen drone page (updated 2026-10-06) also notes that the Malmö restriction is now permanent as ESR130. This is relevant only if a later tropical-style long BVLOS transect is ever tested in Sweden under the Specific category.

verification.recommendation_assessment:
The recommendations hold up. All of the load-bearing legal claims were confirmed against primary sources: §9 of lag 2016:319 is unchanged (SFS 2026:1378 changed only §6), a permit is needed for drone-derived 3D models, ground capture is outside the law, the cloud and email definition of dissemination, the free permit with about 65 working days of handling, no retouching of 3D models, and the narrow forest exemption. Keeping phase 1 ground-only and choosing option (c), a separate aerial layer, over (b) for anything public is well supported by the law.

Changes I would make:
1. Lantmäteriet cannot pre-approve. Applications are accepted only with the finished material, so the permit is a gate after processing. Plan about 13 weeks between the final drone-derived model and publication, and expect to reapply for each substantively new model version (inference).
2. Insurance is mandatory for Hexagon work flights under 785/2004, according to Transportstyrelsen, not just something to check.
3. Fix the camera surveillance date: the permit was removed by SFS 2025:220 on 1 Apr 2025. The project is not affected.
4. The 'keep data local' rule must explicitly exclude OneDrive-synced folders (the project sits under Desktop), Git remotes, LFS and CDNs, because Lantmäteriet names 'molntjänster' as dissemination.
5. Add a skyddsobjekt check (skyddslag §7 ban on depicting and measuring) for all sources, ground capture included. Option (a) is therefore not 'GDPR only'.
6. Track lineage, not just a flag, in the source-module interface. Any model trained on drone pixels inherits the drone's clearance status. A ground-only splat whose poses were only co-registered using drone SfM is a grey zone: treat it as uncleared or ask Lantmäteriet.
7. Consider a permit-free mast or pole elevated 360 capture (ground contact, so outside §9 and aviation rules) as a cheaper middle option before committing to a drone.

The drone-class advice (C0 or C1 in A1 to avoid the undefined 'recreational area' rule in A3; buy a class-labelled drone with Remote ID because of Opinion 06/2026) stands. Note that the Mini 5 Pro's C0 status depends on its certified configuration.

Several items could not be checked against primary sources: the tropical details for Brazil, Indonesia and Costa Rica, the landowner-consent provision, the bird-season dates and the 23 Oct 2025 start date of the supervised A2 exam. Keep these at low or medium confidence.

The web search budget was used up before this check began, so it relied only on direct fetches of known primary URLs. A follow-up search could look for pending §9 reforms not shown on Lantmäteriet's pages and for Hexagon's own drone policy.

research.summary:
Proposed architecture for a single-developer local app on Windows 11 with an RTX 3080 Ti (16 GB): a Python backend that plans and runs the processing pipeline, a Vite/TypeScript web UI, and one Three.js viewer package. The same viewer serves both the local preview and the public static export.

1) SOURCE MODULES. Each capture source is a plugin with a small interface:
- probe() runs a fast validation and returns a metadata report plus refined capabilities.
- stages() declares the source's part of the pipeline graph, with typed inputs and outputs, a parameter model, resource needs (GPU yes/no, estimated VRAM) and whether the stage can resume.
- layers() lists what the source contributes to the viewer.

Capabilities are explicit fields:
- metric_scale: exact / approx / none
- georef: none / gnss / rtk / gcp, with its accuracy
- gravity_aligned
- imagery_for_splat
- geometry
- time_base

For the current sources:
- BLK2GO LAS: exact metric scale, gravity-aligned, no georeference.
- Insta360 video: imagery only. No scale, no georeference.
- Drone images: approximate scale and georeference from GNSS. Accuracy depends on RTK status read from the DJI XMP tags. Barometric altitude is unreliable.

This mirrors established tools:
- nerfstudio DataParsers turn any dataset into one common output (image filenames, cameras, dataparser_transform, dataparser_scale) and are registered through Python entry points.
- ODM runs a fixed list of named stages (dataset ... odm_postprocess) and supports rerun / rerun-from.
- Meshroom gives every node a hash of its output-affecting attributes and caches results in MeshroomCache/<NodeType>/<uid>.

Work that combines sources lives in project-level stages, not inside the modules:
- reconstruction groups: one SfM run per group of imagery sources
- registration
- splat training per group
- export

The reconstruction group is what makes drone options (b) and (c) a configuration choice rather than a code fork:
- (b) = Insta360 and drone in one SfM/splat group.
- (c) = separate groups that produce separate layers.
So the drone decision can be postponed and tested empirically.

2) FRAMES. A frame graph with Sim(3) edges (s, R, t as 4x4 doubles), each carrying:
- an optional 7x7 tangent-space covariance and scalar quality metrics (RMSE, inlier fraction, correspondence count)
- provenance: method, parameters, input hashes, tool versions, time, and a user-accepted flag
- a status: prior / estimated / manual / verified

Rules for picking the project (anchor) frame automatically:
- LiDAR present: use the LiDAR frame, re-centred to a local origin with the offset stored.
- Otherwise, a drone with GNSS: use a local ENU tangent frame at a chosen latitude/longitude/height origin. This is the OpenSfM reference_lla pattern.
- Otherwise: the SfM frame of the first imagery group, with gravity from COLMAP orientation alignment. Scale is marked arbitrary until the user enters a known distance.

A separate double-precision project-to-world transform (ECEF plus EPSG metadata, e.g. SWEREF 99 TM EPSG:3006 + RH 2000 EPSG:5613) exists only when a connected source provides a georeference. The LiDAR scale is never changed by the drone GNSS. A drone-to-LiDAR scale that differs from 1 is reported as a QA signal.

Never store or render real-world coordinates in float32. At Swedish northings around 6.5e6 m the float32 step is 0.5 m. 3D Tiles solves the same problem with relative-to-centre storage and root transforms.

Consistency check: where two paths exist between frames (e.g. Insta360→LiDAR directly versus Insta360→drone→LiDAR), report the discrepancy.

Implementation:
- Hand-rolled frame graph of about 100 lines; pytransform3d's TransformManager is an optional reference.
- pycolmap Sim3d, align_reconstructions_via_points and Reconstruction.transform for the SfM-side operations.
- COLMAP model_aligner (ENU/ECEF, needs at least 3 images with known positions) for GNSS georeferencing.

3) CRITICAL SPLAT-FRAME FINDING. gsplat's simple_trainer defaults to normalize_world_space=True. Its parser applies a similarity transform plus a principal-axes rotation (and possibly a 180° flip), stores it as parser.transform, and exports the PLY in that normalized frame without inverting it. Undoing this afterwards means rotating the SH coefficients as well. Recommendation:
- Register the sparse SfM to the LiDAR first. This is cheap and can be repeated.
- Apply the Sim(3) to the COLMAP model.
- Train in the project frame with normalization off, or invert the transform with proper SH rotation.
- Apply only small later corrections as viewer node transforms.

Spark's SplatMesh supports position/quaternion transforms but only uniform scale. Whether SH is evaluated correctly under object rotation is not documented and must be tested.

4) PROJECT FILES AND CACHING. Pydantic v2 models, saved as JSON:
- project.json: user intent, i.e. sources, parameters, groups, anchor policy.
- frames.json: the transform graph.
- state/<stage>.json: status, PID, input fingerprint, output hashes.
- export/scene.json: the viewer manifest, generated from the rest.

The JSON Schema is exported to TypeScript types for the UI and viewer. Writes are atomic (temp file + os.replace).

Stage cache key = hash of:
- stage id and implementation version
- canonical parameters
- input artefact content IDs
- external tool versions

Outputs live in cache/<stage>/<key>/ (Meshroom style). The stage record works like DVC's dvc.lock. Large raw inputs (multi-GB LAS or video) stay where they are and are fingerprinted with size, mtime and BLAKE3.

Proportionate tooling is a hand-rolled DAG of a few hundred lines. The alternatives fit worse:
- doit is the closest off-the-shelf fit (file_dep, config_changed, works on Windows).
- Snakemake runs on Windows only through WSL.
- Dagster and Prefect bring a server/UI and are overkill.
- Hamilton caches in-process Python objects (pickle), not subprocess GPU jobs producing gigabytes of files.
- Luigi checks whether target files exist, with no content hashing.

5) BACKEND AND UI. Option (a): FastAPI + uvicorn on localhost, serving the built Vite app and the project files. Range requests work from Starlette 0.39. Native SSE exists from FastAPI 0.135, with Last-Event-ID resume and a 15 s keep-alive. Commands go over REST.

Each stage runs as its own Python or native subprocess:
- Started with subprocess.Popen in a worker thread, not asyncio subprocesses. uvicorn --reload or workers>1 on Windows switches to the Selector event loop, which raises NotImplementedError for subprocesses.
- Placed in a Windows Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE plus CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP, so cancelling kills the whole process tree.
- Writes events.jsonl for progress and metrics, plus a log. stdout is parsed only as a fallback (COLMAP "Processed file [i/n]", "Matching block", gsplat tqdm).
- A process per stage also frees VRAM reliably. PyTorch's caching allocator keeps memory, and empty_cache() cannot free memory held by live tensors.
- One GPU job at a time.
- On startup, records still marked RUNNING whose PID is dead become INTERRUPTED, with resume offered for stages that checkpoint. Meshroom has the same stale-RUNNING problem.

Option (b): pywebview (WebView2) can wrap the same UI later to get native file dialogs. Browsers cannot hand over absolute paths, and uploading gigabytes to localhost is wasteful. Tauri/Electron add a Rust/Node layer and sidecar packaging with no benefit here.

Option (c) loses on reuse:
- Gradio, Streamlit and NiceGUI cannot reuse the TypeScript viewer. NiceGUI also has the Windows asyncio subprocess issue.
- PySide6 cannot reuse it either.
- viser (Apache-2.0) is still worth using as a developer tool for checking registration, thanks to its transform gizmos.

Packaging:
- A pixi workspace with a lockfile: conda-forge for PDAL/GDAL/PROJ (PDAL's PyPI bindings need a separate libpdal), PyTorch CUDA from conda-forge or the PyTorch index.
- External binaries pinned with version probes: COLMAP CUDA build (pycolmap Windows wheels are CPU-only), ODM native if used.
- No PyInstaller.
- Avoid spaces in paths. The user profile "C:\Users\Leonard Lind" has one, and both ODM and torch cpp_extension JIT builds have failed on spaces. Set TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR and use a short project root.

6) VIEWER. scene.json lists layers:
- id, kind (pointcloud, splat, mesh, ortho/dsm, ground/navmesh), source, format and URI
- a 4x4 transform to the project frame, bounds, LoD information
- toggle group and default visibility

It also holds presets (LiDAR / Splat / Combined / Aerial), each shown only when all the layers it needs exist, the project-to-world block, and navigation (ground, start pose).

The static export is the viewer dist folder plus export/ copied as-is. For 3D Tiles:
- Each layer becomes its own tileset.
- A root tileset references them, with root.transform = project→ECEF.
- Point clouds via py3dtiles; splats as glTF with KHR_gaussian_splatting (ratified Sept 2026) plus spz_2 compression.
- LuciadRIA 2026.1 reads these. In Three.js they load through 3DTilesRendererJS plus a 3DGS plugin.
- A project with no georeference has to be placed at a pseudo-georeference, flagged as such.

findings.claim: Model the pipeline on ODM's named stages with rerun-from, but key each stage's cache on content (Meshroom/DVC style) rather than on whether output files exist.
findings.details: ODM stages: dataset, split, merge, opensfm, openmvs, odm_filterpoints, odm_meshing, mvs_texturing, odm_georeferencing, odm_dem, odm_orthophoto, odm_report, odm_postprocess. Stages are chained with connect(). A stage reruns if --rerun names it, --rerun-all is set, or it falls in --rerun-from. Progress is split into per-stage windows; e.g. update_progress(50) in a stage spanning 40–80 % reports 60 % overall. Meshroom: every node has a hash of its attributes, attributes flagged uid/invalidate feed that hash, and outputs go to MeshroomCache/<nodeType>/<uid>/, so only downstream nodes are invalidated. DVC records content hashes of deps/outs/params in dvc.lock and re-runs only stages whose hashes changed.

findings.claim: nerfstudio's DataParser is the right precedent for the common source interface: each source is normalized into one lightweight output contract and registered as a plugin.
findings.details: DataparserOutputs holds image_filenames, cameras, alpha_color, scene_box, mask_filenames, metadata, dataparser_transform (3x4) and dataparser_scale. Implementations override _generate_dataparser_outputs(split). Plugins register through the entry-point groups nerfstudio.dataparser_configs / nerfstudio.method_configs, or through the env vars NERFSTUDIO_DATAPARSER_CONFIGS / NERFSTUDIO_METHOD_CONFIGS. Keeping dataparser_transform/scale is the precedent for recording how each source frame relates to the training frame. For a single developer a plain registry dict is enough; entry points can come later.

findings.claim: gsplat's simple_trainer exports splats in a normalized frame, not the input COLMAP frame. The registration/export pipeline must account for this.
findings.details: normalize_world_space defaults to True. The Parser applies T1 = similarity_from_cameras (rotation + scale) and T2 = align_principal_axes (rotation), with an optional 180° X flip, and stores the combined matrix as parser.transform. export_splats writes means/scales/quats straight from the normalized splats with no inverse. Undoing a rotation also requires rotating the SH coefficients (degrees 1–3); simple_trainer has no SH-rotation code. Mitigations: (1) transform the COLMAP model into the project frame (pycolmap Reconstruction.transform) and train with normalize_world_space=False; or (2) invert parser.transform with a proper SH (Wigner-D) rotation. Option 1 is simplest for the 10x10 m test. Brush and LichtFeld were not checked for the same behaviour; run a bbox test.

findings.claim: Viewer-time transforms for splats are limited: Spark SplatMesh supports position/quaternion but only uniform scale, and does not document whether SH is evaluated correctly in a rotated object space.
findings.details: Spark docs: 'scale only allows uniform scaling and averages the x/y/z scales'. Sim(3) fits, since it has uniform scale. SH correctness under rotation is not stated. PlayCanvas splat-transform (MIT) supports translate, Euler rotate and uniform scale, can output GLB with KHR_gaussian_splatting, SOG and LOD chunks, but SH rotation was not confirmed in its docs. Treat viewer-side transforms as fine for small corrections, and either bake transforms by training in the project frame or verify SH rotation in the tool.

findings.claim: Real-world coordinates must never reach float32 buffers. The project frame has to be local, with a double-precision offset or ECEF transform kept separately.
findings.details: Own computation: at a SWEREF 99 TM northing of ~6.5e6 m (between 2^22 and 2^23) the float32 spacing is 0.5 m; ECEF values of 3–6e6 m give 0.25–0.5 m. 3D Tiles and Cesium handle this with RTC (relative-to-centre) storage and tile/root transforms. OpenSfM uses a topocentric ENU frame with its origin in reference_lla.json, explicitly 'to keep coordinates small and prevent numerical issues'. ODM likewise stores UTM with offsets. Splat trainers also work in float32.

findings.claim: COLMAP and pycolmap already provide the georeferencing and Sim(3) primitives the registration and anchor logic needs.
findings.details: model_aligner takes --ref_images_path or --database_path (pose priors from EXIF GPS), --ref_is_gps, --alignment_type {ecef, enu, plane, custom}, --alignment_max_error (RANSAC), and needs at least 3 images with known positions. pose_prior_mapper is the incremental mapper with position priors, and --overwrite_priors_covariance sets the prior uncertainty. pycolmap has Sim3d (scale, rotation, translation), align_reconstructions_via_points / _via_reprojections / _via_proj_centers, and Reconstruction.transform. The COLMAP database now includes rigs and frames tables, which suit Insta360 multi-view rigs and mixed ground/aerial image sets.

findings.claim: pycolmap's Windows wheels are CPU-only. GPU SIFT on Windows needs the COLMAP CUDA executable run as a subprocess; pycolmap stays useful for model I/O and alignment.
findings.details: The pycolmap docs say CUDA wheels (pycolmap-cuda12) exist only for Linux and that the standard PyPI wheels have no GPU support. The docs are built from COLMAP 4.3.0.dev0 (2026-10-01). Release notes: 4.1.0 added a spherical (equirectangular) camera model for 360 panoramas and Caspar GPU bundle adjustment ('1–2 orders of magnitude faster than Ceres CUDA'). 4.2.0 added multi-component reconstruction, LoMa ONNX features and a browser-based sparse viewer. The release-page fetch gave month and day; the year (2026) is inferred.

findings.claim: On Windows, run GPU stages as separate subprocesses started with Popen in worker threads, not asyncio subprocesses inside uvicorn.
findings.details: uvicorn with --reload, or with workers>1, installs WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy. SelectorEventLoop cannot create subprocesses, so asyncio.create_subprocess_exec raises NotImplementedError, whose message is empty. NiceGUI has the same issue. Use a Windows Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE (pywin32 win32job) plus CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP, so cancelling or a backend crash kills the whole COLMAP/trainer tree; taskkill /T can miss detached children. A process per stage also guarantees VRAM is released: PyTorch's caching allocator keeps memory reserved, shows it as used in nvidia-smi, and empty_cache() cannot free memory held by live tensors.

findings.claim: FastAPI now has native SSE and Starlette serves HTTP Range requests, so a plain FastAPI app can stream status events and serve streaming 3D formats to the same viewer used in the public export.
findings.details: FastAPI 0.135.0 added fastapi.sse (EventSourceResponse, ServerSentEvent), with Last-Event-ID resume, an automatic 15 s keep-alive comment and Cache-Control: no-cache / X-Accel-Buffering: no. Starlette 0.39.0 (2024-09-23) added Range support to FileResponse, which StaticFiles uses. COPC, RAD and 3D Tiles byte-range loading therefore works from localhost exactly as from a static host.

findings.claim: The off-the-shelf pipeline libraries either fit poorly or are overkill for a single-user Windows desktop tool. A small hand-rolled DAG is proportionate; doit is the best ready-made alternative.
findings.details: Snakemake (docs v9.27.0) documents Windows only through WSL; the full install and per-rule conda envs are not native. Dagster supports Windows (Python ≥3.10) but brings a webserver, its own UI and asset framework, duplicating our UI. Prefect 3 caching hashes task inputs plus source code, stores results in ~/.prefect/storage and needs PREFECT_RESULTS_PERSIST_BY_DEFAULT; path arguments are hashed as strings, not by file content. Hamilton caching hashes node name, code version and dependency data versions, stores pickles in ./.hamilton_cache, warns cache keys can be unstable across versions, and is still incubating at Apache. It suits in-process dataframes, not subprocess GPU jobs that write gigabytes. doit offers file_dep change detection, targets, config_changed/result_dep uptodate checks and persistent saved values.

findings.claim: Meshroom shows the crash-recovery pitfall to design for: stage status files left as RUNNING after a crash block recomputation.
findings.details: Each Meshroom node has log, status and statistics files in its cache folder, organized by type, hash and chunk. meshroom_compute has --forceStatus because nodes get stuck as RUNNING/SUBMITTED ('Graph is being computed externally'). Design: the stage record stores PID, start time and heartbeat; on startup, a RUNNING record with a dead PID becomes INTERRUPTED, and stages that checkpoint (trainers) offer resume.

findings.claim: WebODM/NodeODM/pyodm is the reference design for separating the UI and orchestrator from the processing engine through a task REST API, but that topology is heavier than this project needs.
findings.details: NodeODM REST endpoints: /task/new, /task/new/init → /task/new/upload/{uuid} → /task/new/commit/{uuid}, /task/{uuid}/info (progress 0–100, processing time, image count), /task/{uuid}/output?line=N (incremental console log), /task/cancel, /task/remove, /task/restart, /task/{uuid}/download/{asset}. Status codes: 10 QUEUED, 20 RUNNING, 30 FAILED, 40 COMPLETED, 50 CANCELED. Our backend can expose the same task/status/log semantics in-process, without Celery/Redis/Postgres. WebODM's server stack (Django/Celery/Redis/Postgres) is from background knowledge.

findings.claim: For drone-only or drone-aerial-model cases, ODM can be wrapped as an optional external engine. It is AGPL-3.0, has a native Windows installer, produces 3D Tiles, and fails on paths containing spaces.
findings.details: ODM: AGPL-3.0; native Windows setup from its releases page; GPU SIFT through Docker (opendronemap/odm:gpu); outputs orthophoto GeoTIFF, DSM/DTM, textured OBJ mesh, LAZ point cloud; --3d-tiles flag (docs 3.6.0). GCP file gcp_list.txt: first line is a PROJ string, an EPSG code or 'WGS84 UTM 16N'; rows are 'geo_x geo_y geo_z im_x im_y image_name [gcp_name]'; at least 5 GCPs × 3 images recommended. Known Windows bug: the OpenSfM stage fails on project paths with spaces (issue #1006, community threads). Running ODM as a separate process avoids AGPL linking concerns for a local tool (licensing interpretation is background knowledge, low confidence).

findings.claim: The user's Windows profile path contains a space ('C:\Users\Leonard Lind'), and the current project path contains a space and a '+'. Both are known to break parts of this toolchain.
findings.details: torch.utils.cpp_extension (used by gsplat JIT builds) fails when the build directory or include paths contain spaces (pytorch #38781, #122476). ODM's OpenSfM fails on spaces. Also, Windows JIT CUDA extensions fail with CUDA 13.2+ because CCCL needs /Zc:preprocessor (pytorch #197574). Mitigations: a project/data root such as C:\gsl or D:\gsl; TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR and TEMP/TMP pointed at paths without spaces for subprocesses; prefer gsplat's prebuilt Windows wheels; pin CUDA 12.8.

findings.claim: Package with a locked pixi (conda-forge + PyPI) environment and pinned external binaries, not PyInstaller or a Tauri/Electron sidecar.
findings.details: pixi documents PyTorch CUDA through conda-forge (pytorch-gpu, cuda-version) or the PyTorch PyPI indexes, with system-requirements cuda declared. uv also supports CUDA PyTorch on Windows through an explicit index (pytorch-cu126/cu128/cu130) and --torch-backend=auto (uv pip only). PDAL's PyPI bindings do not bundle libpdal (need PDAL ≥2.7 installed); conda-forge python-pdal 3.5.5 is the practical Windows route, which favours pixi. gsplat needs PyTorch 2.7+ and ships prebuilt Linux and Windows wheels for some torch/CUDA combinations. Tauri sidecars need target-triple-named single binaries (externalBin) and shell permissions. Freezing CUDA torch with PyInstaller produces multi-GB bundles and still needs MSVC/CUDA for JIT (background knowledge).

findings.claim: Exporting to 3D Tiles for LuciadRIA and Cesium is now standards-based for both splats and point clouds.
findings.details: KHR_gaussian_splatting status: 'Complete, Ratified by the Khronos Group'. The ratification date of 2026-09-03 comes from a third-party GitHub issue. Release candidate was February 2026. Attributes: POSITION, KHR_gaussian_splatting:ROTATION/SCALE/OPACITY, SH degree 0 required and 1–3 optional; kernel 'ellipse'; colorSpace srgb_rec709_display or lin_rec709_display. LuciadRIA 2026.1 decodes splats from OGC 3D Tiles with glTF payloads using KHR_gaussian_splatting or KHR_gaussian_splatting_compression_spz_2, via TileSet3DLayer + OGC3DTilesModel, styled with gaussianSplatsStyle. Cesium added hierarchical LoD splats in 3D Tiles (April 2026). Three.js path: 3DTilesRendererJS + the Apache-2.0 3D-Tiles-RendererJS-3DGS-Plugin. Only spz_2-compressed payloads are supported, it needs WASM and workers, and WebGPU needs a secure context or localhost. Splat tilesets can be made with npx 3dgs-ply-3dtiles-converter <ply> <out> --coordinate "[lat, lon, h]". Point-cloud tilesets: py3dtiles v12.1.1 (2026-03-20, Apache-2.0), LAS/XYZ to pnts.

findings.claim: Spark 2.0 (Three.js) is a suitable splat renderer for both the local preview and the public export. It streams LoD and reads the formats the trainers produce.
findings.details: Spark 2.0 was released 2026-04-15. It adds streaming LoD with a per-frame splat budget (platform default 500K–2.5M) and the .RAD format, chunked in 64K-splat spatial pieces for progressive loading. SplatMesh reads .ply (including compressed), .splat, .ksplat, .spz, .sog, .zip and .rad, and sits in a normal Three.js scene graph, so point-cloud and nav layers share one scene. How depth and occlusion combine with other Three.js objects is not documented; test it.

findings.claim: Python-native UI frameworks cannot reuse the TypeScript/Three.js viewer for the public web export. viser is useful only as a developer/QA tool.
findings.details: viser (Apache-2.0) runs a Python server and a React/three.js client over WebSocket, with point clouds, add_gaussian_splats, transform gizmos, GUI widgets and get_scene_serializer() for static embedding. That makes it ideal for interactive registration checks, but its scene graph is driven from Python, not by our scene.json. pywebview uses EdgeChromium (WebView2, Chromium-based) on Windows, falling back to mshtml, so it can wrap the same Vite UI and add native file dialogs.

findings.claim: The drone module's georeference capability must carry an accuracy class taken from metadata. Its altitude is not trustworthy without RTK or GCPs.
findings.details: DJI XMP (drone-dji namespace) carries GpsLatitude/GpsLongitude, AbsoluteAltitude, RelativeAltitude, Gimbal{Roll,Pitch,Yaw}Degree, RtkFlag and RtkStdLat/Lon/Hgt (e.g. RtkFlag=16 with Std ≈1–2.5 on a P1). The community Metashape manual says DJI EXIF GPSAltitude is barometric and gives 5–50 m vertical errors without GCPs; RTK per-image sigmas are typically 0.01–0.05 m horizontally. So the anchor logic should use drone GNSS as the project frame only when no LiDAR is present, and treat non-RTK georeference as approximate (metre level). RtkFlag value meanings were not confirmed.

findings.claim: Swedish georeferencing targets for the project-to-world block are SWEREF 99 TM (EPSG:3006) for horizontal and RH 2000 (EPSG:5613) for heights via the SWEN17_RH2000 geoid. The internal world frame stays ECEF/WGS84.
findings.details: SWEREF 99 is the Swedish realisation of ETRS89. SWEN17_RH2000 converts RH 2000 heights to SWEREF 99 ellipsoidal heights (EPSG:4377) with 8–10 mm standard uncertainty. pyproj/PROJ grids exist for Lantmäteriet (cdn.proj.org).

findings.claim: The splat trainers consume COLMAP models, so 'COLMAP sparse model + undistorted images + masks' should be the internal contract for imagery-for-splat. Trainer-specific caveats remain.
findings.details: Brush (Apache-2.0, Rust/Burn, WebGPU, no CUDA needed; web build needs Chrome 134+ on Windows/macOS) reads COLMAP and nerfstudio datasets and offers --with-viewer. LichtFeld Studio (GPLv3) needs compute capability 7.5+ and driver 570+ (CUDA 12.8+); it trains from COLMAP, exports PLY/SOG/SPZ/HTML, and has a Python plugin system since v0.5.0. Its README says prebuilt Windows binaries come through the 'LichtFeld Portal', yet the GitHub releases page lists Windows assets for v0.4.2–v0.5.3; this conflict is unresolved (2026 dates inferred). gsplat (Apache-2.0) simple_trainer reports progress with tqdm, writes ckpt_*.pt at save_steps and PLY at ply_steps.

findings.claim: A browser-only UI cannot get absolute local file paths. Importing multi-GB LAS, video and drone folders needs a backend-side file browser or a native dialog.
findings.details: Background knowledge: <input type=file> and the File System Access API return handles, not paths, and uploading gigabytes to localhost duplicates data. Options: a backend /fs/list endpoint scoped to user-chosen roots; pywebview's native file/folder dialog; or a Tauri dialog plugin. This is the main concrete reason to add the pywebview wrapper (option b) later.

recommendations.recommendation: Architecture: (1) a Python backend package 'core' (Pydantic models, source registry, DAG planner, stage runner, frame graph, cache); (2) 'stages/' as standalone CLI entry points (python -m app.stages.<name> --record <state.json>), each writing events.jsonl and a log; (3) FastAPI ≥0.135 on 127.0.0.1 serving REST commands, an SSE event stream, the built UI and project files with Range support; (4) a Vite/TS monorepo with packages/viewer (Three.js + Spark 2 + point-cloud loader, driven only by scene.json), packages/app-ui (wizard, status, logs, embeds the viewer) and packages/schema (TS types generated from the Pydantic JSON Schema); (5) export = viewer dist + export/ folder, plus an optional 3D Tiles bundle.
recommendations.rationale: One viewer codebase serves the local preview, the public web and the Luciad/Cesium paths. Running stages as subprocesses gives cancellation, VRAM release and crash isolation on Windows. Everything fits a single developer's TypeScript and Python skills.
recommendations.alternatives: Tauri/Electron shell: extra layer, no gain. PySide6/NiceGUI/Gradio/Streamlit: cannot reuse the web viewer. Add pywebview later only for native dialogs and an app window.

recommendations.recommendation: Source module interface (Python Protocol): kind, version, capabilities {metric_scale: exact|approx|none, georef: none|gnss|rtk|gcp with sigma_m, gravity_aligned, imagery_for_splat, geometry, time_base}; probe(inputs) -> ProbeReport (metadata, warnings, refined capabilities); stages(cfg) -> list[StageSpec{id, inputs: typed artefact ports, outputs, params model, resources{gpu, vram_gb_est}, resumable}]; layers(artefacts) -> list[LayerSpec]. Artefact types: PointCloud, GroundModel, ImageSet (frames, masks, intrinsics prior, timestamps), SfMModel (COLMAP), Splat, Mesh, Ortho/DSM, TransformEdge. Project-level stages (not owned by modules): ReconstructionGroup SfM, Register, TrainSplat (per group), BuildNav, Export.
recommendations.rationale: Mirrors nerfstudio DataParser normalization and ODM's stage list. Reconstruction groups turn drone options (b) merged and (c) separate into a config switch, so the drone decision can be made from data later. The UI enables only the steps and toggles the declared capabilities allow.
recommendations.alternatives: Per-combination hard-coded pipelines: simpler for the first test, but the number of combinations explodes once the drone source arrives.

recommendations.recommendation: Anchor-frame policy and frame graph: project frame = re-centred LiDAR frame if LiDAR present; else ENU at the drone GNSS origin (lat/lon/h stored as in OpenSfM reference_lla) if drone present; else the SfM frame with gravity-up and scale 'arbitrary' until the user enters a known distance. Store every source→project edge as Sim(3) (4x4 float64 + s,R,t) with {method, status: prior|estimated|manual|verified, rmse, inlier_ratio, n_corr, optional 7x7 covariance, input hashes, tool versions, accepted_by_user}. Keep project→world (ECEF 4x4 float64 + EPSG:3006/5613 metadata) separate, and fill it only when a connected source is georeferenced. Never let drone GNSS rescale LiDAR; report the drone↔LiDAR scale deviation as QA. Check cycle consistency when several paths exist.
recommendations.rationale: Keeps all GPU buffers in small local coordinates (float32 step ≈0.5 m at Swedish northings otherwise). Makes georeferencing optional and auditable. The user-measured device offset becomes a 'prior' edge that the software estimate checks.
recommendations.alternatives: pytransform3d TransformManager for graph path-finding (BSD-3; Sim(3) support unverified); ROS tf2-style tree (no uncertainty).

recommendations.recommendation: Splat-frame handling: register the COLMAP sparse model to LiDAR before training (pycolmap align/Sim3d + ICP refine), apply the Sim(3) to the COLMAP model, then train with gsplat normalize_world_space=False, or invert parser.transform including SH rotation. Apply only small post-training corrections as viewer node transforms. Add an automated check that compares the exported splat-means bbox with the sparse-points bbox in the project frame.
recommendations.rationale: gsplat exports in a normalized, rotated frame by default, and undoing a rotation requires rotating SH. Spark supports only uniform scale and does not document SH correctness under rotation. For a 10x10 m test, re-training after a registration change is acceptable.
recommendations.alternatives: Train in the SfM frame and bake the transform at export with an SH-rotation utility (implement Wigner-D rotation, or verify that splat-transform rotates SH).

recommendations.recommendation: Project files and cache: project.json (intent), frames.json (transform graph), state/<stage>.json (status, PID, heartbeat, cache_key, outputs), export/scene.json (generated), all Pydantic v2 with schema_version and atomic writes (temp + os.replace). Stage cache key = BLAKE3(stage id + impl version + canonical params JSON + input artefact IDs + external tool version strings). Outputs go to cache/<stage>/<key16>/. Raw inputs are referenced in place and fingerprinted by size + mtime_ns + BLAKE3 (fast partial hash at import, full hash in the background). Provide 'rerun from stage' and 'force' like ODM.
recommendations.rationale: Content-addressed and proportionate. Changing registration or export parameters does not redo SfM, and the cache records double as provenance. Avoids the heavy orchestration frameworks.
recommendations.alternatives: doit (file_dep + config_changed) as the engine under the same records; DVC only if the user wants git-tracked data lineage.

recommendations.recommendation: Runner on Windows: one GPU queue (one GPU job at a time on 16 GB) plus a CPU pool. Start subprocess.Popen in threads with CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP and attach each child to a Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE. Cancel = CTRL_BREAK, then job terminate. Never run uvicorn with --reload or workers>1 for the job host. Progress comes from stage-emitted JSONL (step, total, loss, n_gaussians, vram); stdout regex parsing (COLMAP 'Processed file [i/n]', 'Matching block [a/b, c/d]', mapper registration lines, tqdm) is the fallback. Poll GPU memory via NVML. On restart, mark stale RUNNING records INTERRUPTED and offer resume from checkpoints.
recommendations.rationale: Avoids the SelectorEventLoop NotImplementedError, process-tree leaks and VRAM held by PyTorch's caching allocator. Avoids the stale-RUNNING lockups Meshroom users hit.
recommendations.alternatives: Wrap ODM through NodeODM's REST semantics for the drone-only aerial model.

recommendations.recommendation: UI flow: Home (new/open) → Sources (checkboxes for LiDAR / 360 video / drone images, with a live 'you will get' panel derived from capabilities: layers, anchor frame, scale and georef status) → Import (per-source path pickers through a backend file browser or a native dialog; probe reports with warnings) → Alignment setup (shown only with ≥2 sources: proposed anchor with override, device offset and time-offset priors, optional GCPs, imagery grouping joint vs separate) → Process (graph view of stages, status chips, progress/ETA, live logs over SSE, GPU memory, cancel/rerun-from, QA panels: SfM stats, registration residual heatmap) → View & Export (embedded viewer with toggles from scene.json; export web bundle / 3D Tiles).
recommendations.rationale: Each step appears only when the selected sources need it. Suits single-user desktop use and matches the user's request for a clean selection → import → status flow.
recommendations.alternatives: A single-page dashboard without a wizard, once the user is familiar with the tool.

recommendations.recommendation: Viewer manifest scene.json: {schema_version, project_frame{up:'+Z', units:'m', origin_note}, world?{ecef_from_project 4x4 f64, epsg_h:3006, epsg_v:5613, pseudo:boolean}, layers[{id, kind: pointcloud|splat|mesh|ortho|dsm|ground|navmesh, source, group: 'lidar'|'ground_splat'|'aerial', format: copc|potree2|3dtiles|spz|sog|rad|glb, uri, transform 4x4 (project_from_layer, column-major), bounds, lod, default_visible}], presets[{id:'lidar'|'splat'|'combined'|'aerial', layers:[...]}] (shown only if all their layers exist), navigation{ground_uri, walkable_polygon?, start_pose, mode: walk|orbit}}. For 3D Tiles, write one tileset per layer plus a root tileset.json whose root.transform = ecef_from_project. Splats as glTF with KHR_gaussian_splatting + spz_2; point clouds via py3dtiles.
recommendations.rationale: Toggles follow the selected sources automatically. The same manifest drives the local preview and the public export, and converts directly to the 3D Tiles that LuciadRIA 2026.1 and Cesium accept.
recommendations.alternatives: Use a glTF scene graph as the manifest. Less readable, and point-cloud LoD formats do not fit inside glTF.

recommendations.recommendation: Environment: a pixi workspace with a lockfile (conda-forge pdal/python-pdal, gdal, pyproj, laspy; PyTorch CUDA 12.8; gsplat prebuilt wheel), plus tools.toml pinning external binaries (COLMAP CUDA Windows build, optional ODM) with a version probe and checksum. Data and project root without spaces (e.g. C:\gsl\projects). For subprocesses set TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR and TEMP/TMP to paths without spaces; consider a Windows Defender exclusion for the project root.
recommendations.rationale: pycolmap's Windows wheels are CPU-only. PDAL's PyPI bindings need libpdal. The user's profile path contains a space, which has broken ODM and torch JIT builds. CUDA 13.2+ breaks Windows JIT extensions.
recommendations.alternatives: uv with the PyTorch cu128 index plus laspy instead of PDAL; implement ground detection with CSF/SMRF from another library.

recommendations.recommendation: Scope for the first test (LiDAR + Insta360): build only the LiDAR-LAS and Insta360-video modules, one reconstruction group, registration with a device-offset prior plus ICP check, gsplat training in the project frame, scene.json with the LiDAR/splat/combined presets, and static export. Keep the drone module as a stub with capability declarations and a probe() for DJI EXIF/XMP so the anchor and frame logic is exercised early. Defer ODM, 3D Tiles and the pywebview wrapper.
recommendations.rationale: Proves the riskiest parts first: frames, registration and splat-frame correctness. The interface stays ready for drone options (b) and (c) without building them now.
recommendations.alternatives: Build drone support earlier only if the drone research finds aerial imagery essential for the forest splat.

risks: gsplat exports in a normalized and rotated frame by default. If this is missed, the splat and the LiDAR will be misaligned by an arbitrary similarity transform. Undoing it afterwards also requires SH rotation.

Whether SH is evaluated correctly under viewer-side rotation (Spark) and whether splat-transform rotates SH are both unverified. Late-bound transforms may give wrong view-dependent colour for SH degree >0.
Brush and LichtFeld output frames (normalized or input frame) were not checked. Add a bbox regression test for every trainer.
The spaces in 'C:\Users\Leonard Lind' and the project path ('Desktop\Code\Gsplat+Lidar') can break ODM, torch JIT and some scripts. Windows MAX_PATH (260) limits may also hit deep cache paths.
CUDA 13.2+ breaks Windows JIT CUDA extensions (pytorch #197574). Mixing toolkits between COLMAP, gsplat and torch can cause DLL conflicts.
uvicorn --reload or workers>1 on Windows silently breaks asyncio subprocesses (empty NotImplementedError).
Process-tree leaks on cancel or crash (COLMAP, trainer) without Job Objects can hold VRAM on a 16 GB laptop GPU that also drives the display.
A stale RUNNING state after a crash blocks reruns unless PID/heartbeat checks are implemented.
If raw multi-GB inputs are referenced in place, moving the files breaks the project. Fingerprints must detect this and offer relinking.
Without LiDAR or a georeferenced source, a 'splat only' project has arbitrary scale. Navigation and measurements must be disabled or flagged until a manual scale is set.
Drone GNSS without RTK has metre-level horizontal error and 5–50 m barometric vertical error. Letting it influence the LiDAR frame would corrupt metric accuracy.
3D Tiles export of non-georeferenced projects needs a pseudo-georeference, which can mislead if it is not clearly flagged.
LichtFeld's Windows binary distribution model (Portal vs GitHub releases) is unclear. The GPLv3 licence matters if it is embedded rather than called as a separate tool.
ODM is AGPL-3.0. Keep it as an optional external process.
open_questions: Web search budget ran out (200-call limit shared across agents) before these could be checked: whether Spark evaluates SH in object-local space under rotation, whether splat-transform rotates SH, and the output frames of Brush and LichtFeld. Verify each empirically or in a follow-up search.
Exact years for the COLMAP 4.x and LichtFeld v0.5.x releases are inferred (2026); the release pages showed only month and day.
Does pytransform3d's TransformManager accept Sim(3) (scaled) matrices with checks disabled, and is its uncertainty module usable for 7-DoF covariance? Otherwise hand-roll it.
Does Starlette StaticFiles handle the range-request patterns that COPC and RAD streaming loaders use (multiple ranges, If-Range)? Test locally.
Does gsplat training with normalize_world_space=False in a metric LiDAR frame (scene extent ~10–30 m) keep quality? Learning-rate scaling uses the scene scale; confirm on the first test.
Should the drone aerial model (option c) be a splat, an ODM textured mesh, or DSM + orthophoto? That decides the layer kinds and export formats; it depends on the drone research outcome.
DJI RtkFlag value meanings (e.g. 16 vs 50) for automatic accuracy classification were not confirmed.
questions_for_user: Can the project and data root be on a path without spaces (e.g. C:\gsl or D:\gsl)? Your profile path 'C:\Users\Leonard Lind' has a space, which breaks some tools.
Is a browser tab on localhost acceptable for the processing UI in phase 1, with a native window (pywebview) later? Or do you want a desktop app window from the start?
Should raw captures (multi-GB LAS, Insta360 video, drone images) be copied into the project folder, or referenced where they already are?
For georeferenced output, should SWEREF 99 TM (EPSG:3006) + RH 2000 be the default export CRS, or WGS84/ECEF only?
Will the public web export always be static hosting, or might it be served through a Hexagon/Luciad server? This affects whether 3D Tiles is the primary or a secondary export.

verdicts.claim: gsplat simple_trainer defaults to normalize_world_space=True. The Parser applies T1=similarity_from_cameras, T2=align_principal_axes and an optional 180° X flip, stores the result as parser.transform, and export_splats writes the PLY in that normalized frame without inverting it. There is no SH-rotation code.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed from source. The Config has `normalize_world_space: bool = True`. The transform is `transform = T2 @ T1`, then `T3 @ transform` when median z > mean z. `self.transform = transform`. export_splats(means, scales, quats, ...) applies no inverse. New fact that resolves an open question: parser.scene_scale is computed from the camera spread AFTER the normalize block, whatever the flag, and the else-branch sets transform = np.eye(4). The Runner uses scene_scale = parser.scene_scale*1.1*global_scale to scale the means LR and the strategy's grow/prune thresholds. So training with normalize_world_space=False in a metric LiDAR frame keeps the LR and densification scale adaptive. Since T1 contains a scale, the default exported PLY is also rescaled, not only rotated.

verdicts.claim: Spark SplatMesh supports position/quaternion but only uniform scale. Whether SH is evaluated correctly under object rotation is undocumented, and so is depth/occlusion with other Three.js objects.
verdicts.correction: Uniform scale only is confirmed ('scale only allows uniform scaling and averages the x/y/z scales'). The SH question is answered by the source: SplatMesh.ts updates context.viewToObject from the view-to-object matrix and passes viewOrigin: viewToObject.translate to fetchSplat, with the comment 'Only trigger update if we have view-dependent spherical harmonics'. So SH is evaluated in object-local space, and rotating or translating a SplatMesh gives correct view-dependent colour. This is read from code, not from docs, so verify with one test. The Spark README states it 'Integrates with THREE.js rendering pipeline to fuse splat and mesh-based objects'. The current npm version is 2.3.1 (MIT), not 2.0. The Spark 2.0 blog is dated 2026-04-14 (the report says 04-15). The 64K-splat RAD chunks and the 500K–2.5M budget are confirmed.

verdicts.claim: Whether PlayCanvas splat-transform rotates SH is unverified, so baking a transform at export needs a custom Wigner-D implementation.
verdicts.correction: splat-transform's data-table transform code builds `new RotateSH(mat3)` from the rotation and calls `rotateSH.apply(shCoeffs)` on the f_rest_* channels. SH rotation is therefore implemented, and a custom Wigner-D utility is not needed. The CLI offers -t translate, -r Euler degrees and -s uniform scale. License MIT. Outputs: PLY, compressed PLY, SOG, streamed SOG, SPZ, GLB (KHR_gaussian_splatting), HTML, LOD. The GLB is plain KHR_gaussian_splatting, so it is NOT the spz_2-compressed payload that the 3DTilesRendererJS 3DGS plugin requires.

verdicts.claim: Prefer gsplat's prebuilt Windows wheels and pin CUDA 12.8. gsplat needs PyTorch 2.7+ and ships prebuilt Linux and Windows wheels for some torch/CUDA combinations.
verdicts.correction: The two requirements conflict. The prebuilt wheel index (docs.gsplat.studio/whl/gsplat/, 110 files) only goes up to gsplat 1.5.3, with tags pt20–pt24 × cu118/cu121/cu124. The newest Windows wheel is 1.5.3+pt24cu124 (cp310), and no pt27+/cu126+/cu128 wheels exist. The latest PyPI release is 1.5.3 (2025-07-04), a py3-none-any wheel that JIT-compiles CUDA on first import. GitHub main (v1.6.0, Jul 2026) says 'PyTorch 2.7+ is now required' with 'improved CUDA 12.8 and 13.2 build compatibility', but it has no tagged release and no prebuilt wheels. The real choice on Windows: (a) gsplat 1.5.3 prebuilt on torch 2.4/cu124 (fine for an RTX 3080 Ti, sm_86), or (b) gsplat main/1.6 compiled from source or JIT with VS Build Tools (MSVC 143/142), cl.exe on PATH via vcvars64.bat and a CUDA toolkit. Option (b) is where the CUDA 13.2+ /Zc:preprocessor issue and any path problems apply.

verdicts.claim: pycolmap provides the Sim(3) and alignment primitives the SfM→LiDAR registration needs (Sim3d, align_reconstructions_via_points/_via_reprojections/_via_proj_centers, Reconstruction.transform); the recommended registration is 'pycolmap align/Sim3d + ICP refine'.
verdicts.correction: The functions exist: Sim3d(scale, rotation, translation), Reconstruction.transform(new_from_old_world: Sim3d), align_reconstructions_via_points(src_reconstruction, tgt_reconstruction, min_common_observations=3, max_error=0.005, min_inlier_ratio=0.9) -> Sim3d|None, and the reprojection and proj-centre variants. The via_* functions align one COLMAP Reconstruction to another through shared images and observations, so they cannot register SfM to a LiDAR point cloud. They fit cross-group alignment, such as an Insta360 group against a drone group that shares images. The pycolmap call that fits the LiDAR case is align_reconstruction_to_locations(src, tgt_image_names, tgt_locations, min_common_images, ransac_options) -> Sim3d|None. It takes camera centres expressed in the LiDAR frame, for example from the BLK2GO trajectory plus the measured device offset and time sync. ICP refinement needs an external library (Open3D or similar); pycolmap has none. Also confirmed: model_aligner needs ≥3 images with known positions, --ref_is_gps, --alignment_type ecef etc., and --alignment_max_error. pose_prior_mapper has --overwrite_priors_covariance with prior_position_std defaults of 1.0 m. The COLMAP database has rigs and frames tables.

verdicts.claim: pycolmap's Windows wheels are CPU-only, so GPU SIFT on Windows needs the COLMAP CUDA executable. COLMAP 4.1.0 added the spherical camera model and Caspar GPU BA (1–2 orders of magnitude faster than Ceres CUDA); 4.2.0 added multi-component reconstruction, LoMa and a browser viewer.
verdicts.correction: The docs say: 'wheels built for CUDA 12 (only for Linux - for now) are available under the package pycolmap-cuda12'. They are built from COLMAP 4.3.0.dev0, 998ff4d (2026-10-01). The 4.2.1 release assets include colmap-x64-windows-cuda.zip and colmap-x64-windows-nocuda.zip. The Caspar quote is confirmed for medium- and large-scale problems. The release notes add a caveat that matters for the Insta360 module: the spherical model 'is generally faster but less accurate than rendering perspective views'. 4.2.0's multi-component support is described as being in the global mapper. The release pages show no year; 2026 fits the docs build date.

verdicts.claim: uvicorn with --reload or workers>1 on Windows switches to SelectorEventLoop, which makes asyncio.create_subprocess_exec raise NotImplementedError. Stages should therefore be started with Popen in worker threads.
verdicts.correction: Current uvicorn source (uvicorn/loops/asyncio.py): `if sys.platform == "win32" and not use_subprocess: return asyncio.ProactorEventLoop; return asyncio.SelectorEventLoop`. The discussion cited confirms that removing --reload fixed the NotImplementedError. The report misses a practical trap: `fastapi dev` runs with reload enabled (background knowledge), so the job host should start with `fastapi run` or a plain uvicorn command without reload. Popen in threads works under either event loop, so the recommendation stands.

verdicts.claim: FastAPI 0.135.0 added native SSE (fastapi.sse EventSourceResponse/ServerSentEvent) with Last-Event-ID resume, a 15 s keep-alive and the Cache-Control/X-Accel-Buffering headers. Starlette 0.39.0 (2024-09-23) added Range support to FileResponse/StaticFiles, so COPC/RAD/3D Tiles range loading works from localhost.
verdicts.correction: The SSE details are confirmed verbatim, and Starlette 0.39.0 (2024-09-23) did add Range support. The report misses that Starlette's Range handling has since had a security advisory and several correctness fixes: GHSA-7f5h-v6xp-fcq8 (0.49.1, 2025-10-28, range-parsing DoS); 1.0.0rc1 (2026-02-23) with sort-based range merge, multipart byterange CRLF and Content-Type fixes; 1.5.1 (2026-08-08), which rejects inverted ranges and caps ranges at 100; and 1.7.0 (2026-09-23), which ignores Range on non-200 FileResponse. The latest FastAPI, 0.142.2, only requires starlette>=0.46.0, so a resolver could install a vulnerable or buggy Starlette. Pin starlette>=1.7 (or at least >=0.49.1) and bind to 127.0.0.1. Multi-range and If-Range behaviour for COPC/RAD loaders still has to be tested.

verdicts.claim: Splats can be exported to 3D Tiles as glTF with KHR_gaussian_splatting (ratified Sept 2026) plus spz_2 compression, which LuciadRIA 2026.1 reads and which load in Three.js through 3DTilesRendererJS plus a 3DGS plugin. This keeps one viewer codebase for local preview, the public web and the Luciad/Cesium paths.
verdicts.correction: KHR_gaussian_splatting is confirmed as 'Complete, Ratified by the Khronos Group'. Its PR #2490 merged 2026-01-27, and a third-party issue gives 2026-09-03 for the status change. KHR_gaussian_splatting_compression_spz_2 is NOT ratified: it is still an open glTF PR (#2531, opened 2025-09-29) and is not in the Khronos or Vendor extension folders on main. LuciadRIA 2026.1 does consume 3D Tiles with glTF payloads using KHR_gaussian_splatting or KHR_gaussian_splatting_compression_spz_2 (TileSet3DLayer + OGC3DTilesModel; release notes, no date). The release notes give no sign that standalone .ply/.spz files load. The Three.js plugin (Apache-2.0, v0.3.0) accepts ONLY spz_2-compressed payloads, needs three>=0.186 and 3d-tiles-renderer ^0.5.0, and renders through 'Gaussian Splat Lite', not Spark. The 3D Tiles path in Three.js is therefore a second splat renderer that cannot depth-sort together with Spark SplatMeshes, so it is not 'the same viewer code'. Core 3DTilesRendererJS has no splat support but does have a Potree plugin. The nianticlabs SPZ library is now at file version 4; check that spz_2 encoders and decoders agree.

verdicts.claim: Spaces in 'C:\Users\Leonard Lind' and in the project path are known to break torch cpp_extension JIT builds (pytorch #38781, #122476) and ODM/OpenSfM (#1006). CUDA 13.2+ breaks Windows JIT extensions (pytorch #197574).
verdicts.correction: #197574 is confirmed: 'Windows JIT CUDA extensions fail on CUDA 13.2+ (CCCL requires /Zc:preprocessor)', opened 2026-09-18 and still open, with proposed fix PR #188761. The space-in-path evidence is old and closed. #38781 dates from 2020 (Windows 10, ninja 'multiple outputs' error) and is closed. #122476 dates from 2024, was on macOS/Clang ('cpp_extension doesn't support include paths with spaces') and is closed. ODM #1006 dates from 2019, was in Docker and is closed. No current, open evidence was found that these still break, so the claim is overstated. A space-free root (C:\gsl) remains a cheap precaution, especially for source-building gsplat and for MAX_PATH, but present it as a precaution, not as a known current bug.

verdicts.claim: The LichtFeld Studio README says Windows binaries come through the 'LichtFeld Portal', yet the GitHub releases page lists Windows assets for v0.4.2–v0.5.3; this conflict is unresolved. GPLv3, CC≥7.5, driver ≥570.
verdicts.correction: Resolved. v0.4.2 shipped LichtFeld-Studio-Windows-v0_4_2_.zip on GitHub. v0.5.3 (2026-06-24) has only 'Source code (zip)' and 'Source code (tar.gz)', which GitHub generates automatically. The README states: 'Prebuilt Windows binaries are distributed through the LichtFeld Portal. Access is paid: you register and make a donation of your choosing... Binaries are not published on GitHub Releases.' Since v0.5.x a free Windows option means building from source (C++23, CUDA 12.8+). GPLv3, compute capability ≥7.5 and driver ≥570 (CUDA 12.8+) are confirmed.

verdicts.claim: ODM runs a fixed list of named stages with rerun/rerun-all/rerun-from and progress split into per-stage windows. Meshroom hashes output-affecting attributes into node UIDs and caches results, and has --forceStatus for stale RUNNING/SUBMITTED nodes.
verdicts.correction: ODM types.py: rerun() returns true if `args.rerun == self.name`, `args.rerun_all`, or `self.name in args.rerun_from`, and the overall progress is previous_stages_progress() + delta_progress()/100*progress. Meshroom: 'Every node has a hash based on its attributes', and dependants change hash because their input path changes. meshroom_compute has --forceStatus ('Force computation if status is RUNNING or SUBMITTED'), --forceCompute, --toNode and --cache. The exact MeshroomCache/<nodeType>/<uid> layout was not stated on the page checked.

verdicts.claim: Off-the-shelf DAG tools fit poorly: Snakemake runs on Windows only via WSL, Hamilton caches pickles in .hamilton_cache and is incubating, and Prefect caches on inputs plus task source with persistence opt-in. A hand-rolled DAG is proportionate.
verdicts.correction: Snakemake 9.27.0 docs point Windows users to WSL. Hamilton: the cache key is node_name + code_version + dependencies_data_versions; storage is ./.hamilton_cache, pickle by default; it warns that keys may be unstable across versions; the project is 'undergoing incubation' at the ASF. Prefect: the default cache key also includes the flow run ID, so results are not reused across runs without a custom policy. Results go to ~/.prefect/storage and need PREFECT_RESULTS_PERSIST_BY_DEFAULT=true. That strengthens the 'poor fit' conclusion.
