verdicts.claim: NodeODM task API semantics: /task/new, init/upload/commit, info, output, cancel, remove, restart, download; status codes 10/20/30/40/50.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed: 10 QUEUED, 20 RUNNING, 30 FAILED, 40 COMPLETED, 50 CANCELED, and all of the listed endpoints.

verdicts.claim: ODM is AGPL-3.0, has a native Windows installer, offers GPU via Docker, has --3d-tiles (docs 3.6.0), and its GCP file recommends ≥5 GCPs × 3 images.
verdicts.correction: AGPL-3.0, the native Windows setup from releases, GPU only through the opendronemap/odm:gpu Docker image, and --3d-tiles ('Generate OGC 3D Tiles outputs. Default: False', docs 3.6.0) are all confirmed. On GCPs the docs say 'a minimum of 5 GCP works for most of the jobs, and for larger projects 8–10 are sufficient', and that each GCP should be 'found in at least 5 images'. The 15-line minimum (5 points × 3 images) is the absolute floor, not the recommendation.

verdicts.claim: DJI XMP (drone-dji) carries GPS lat/lon, Absolute/RelativeAltitude, gimbal angles, RtkFlag and RtkStd*. Non-RTK altitude is barometric with 5–50 m vertical error; RTK gives 0.01–0.05 m horizontal accuracy.
verdicts.correction: ExifTool's DJI XMP table lists GPSLatitude/GPSLongitude, AbsoluteAltitude, RelativeAltitude, GimbalYawDegree, RtkFlag (string) and RtkStdLat/Lon/Hgt. The barometric 5–50 m figure and the RTK '0.01–0.05 m horizontal, 0.05–0.5 m vertical' come from a single community manual, not from DJI. That manual also advises GCPs for vertical control even with RTK. Treat it as medium confidence. RtkFlag meanings were not verified. Background knowledge only, low confidence: 0 = none, 16 = single point, 34 = float, 50 = fixed. Under that reading the report's 'RtkFlag=16 with Std ≈1–2.5' would be a non-RTK single-point fix.

verdicts.claim: pywebview (BSD-3, 6.x) uses WebView2 on Windows and gives native file and folder dialogs, which is the main reason to add a wrapper. nerfstudio DataparserOutputs are the precedent for normalized source outputs.
verdicts.correction: pywebview LICENSE is BSD 3-Clause. The latest releases are 6.2.1 and 6.2, with WebView2 updated to 1.0.3856.49. The FileDialog enum covers OPEN, FOLDER and SAVE with allow_multiple, and returns a tuple of paths. nerfstudio DataparserOutputs fields (image_filenames, cameras, alpha_color, scene_box, mask_filenames, metadata, dataparser_transform [3,4], dataparser_scale) and the _generate_dataparser_outputs(split) override are confirmed.

verdicts.claim: Float32 spacing is 0.5 m at SWEREF 99 TM northings of ~6.5e6 m. OpenSfM uses a topocentric ENU frame with its origin in reference_lla.json. py3dtiles v12.1.1 (2026-03-20, Apache-2.0) converts LAS/XYZ to pnts. SWEN17_RH2000 converts RH 2000 (EPSG:5613) to SWEREF 99 ellipsoidal heights (EPSG:4377).
verdicts.correction: The arithmetic checks out: 2^22 ≤ 6.5e6 < 2^23 gives an ulp of 0.5 m, and ECEF values of 3e6–6e6 give 0.25–0.5 m. OpenSfM's topocentric frame and reference_lla.json are confirmed, but the quote 'to keep coordinates small and prevent numerical issues' was not found on the page and should not be quoted. py3dtiles v12.1.1 (2026-03-20, Apache 2) converts LAS/XYZ to pnts. The PROJ grid se_lantmateriet_SWEN17_RH2000.tif and its EPSG codes are confirmed. The 8–10 mm uncertainty was not on the PROJ README page and is unverified here.

verdicts.claim: Package with pixi (conda-forge PDAL, PyTorch CUDA from conda-forge or the PyTorch index). PDAL's PyPI bindings need a separately installed libpdal. uv supports CUDA torch indexes, with --torch-backend=auto in uv pip only.
verdicts.correction: PDAL/python: 'The PDAL Python bindings require the PDAL base library installed' (PDAL 2.7+). pixi documents pytorch-gpu + cuda-version and the __cuda virtual package on win-64, and warns that if torch comes from PyPI, everything depending on torch must also come from PyPI ('not mix the PyPI packages with Conda packages'). This constrains mixing conda-forge PDAL with a PyPI torch plus a source-built gsplat, so plan the environment split. uv lists indexes for cu126, cu128 and cu130, and --torch-backend=auto is 'only available in the uv pip interface'.

missed_developments.claim: Spark evaluates view-dependent SH in object-local space (viewToObject), so viewer-side Sim(3) rotation and translation of a splat layer do not corrupt SH colour.
missed_developments.details: This changes the risk balance in the report. The default can be 'train in the SfM frame, then apply the registration Sim(3) as a viewer node transform', with uniform scale only. Re-training after every registration change is no longer forced. A one-scene visual test is still advised because the evidence is source code, not docs. Spark is now at 2.3.1 (MIT), and its README advertises fusing splats with meshes in the Three.js pipeline.

missed_developments.claim: PlayCanvas splat-transform (MIT) already rotates SH (RotateSH) when it bakes transforms, so it can bake the project-frame Sim(3) into exported splats.
missed_developments.details: Use it in the Export stage to bake source→project transforms into PLY/SOG/SPZ/GLB without writing a Wigner-D implementation. The CLI takes Euler degrees and a uniform scale, so convert R to Euler or use the library API. Its GLB output is KHR_gaussian_splatting without spz_2, and the Three.js 3D Tiles plugin rejects that.

missed_developments.claim: There are no prebuilt Windows gsplat wheels for PyTorch ≥2.5. The prebuilt index stops at 1.5.3+pt24cu124, while gsplat main (v1.6.0, Jul 2026) requires PyTorch 2.7+ and has no release or wheels.
missed_developments.details: Phase-1 environment decision: pin gsplat 1.5.3 + torch 2.4 cu124 prebuilt (simplest, sm_86 is fine), or install VS Build Tools + CUDA 12.8 toolkit and build main from source. The second route is exposed to pytorch #197574 if CUDA ≥13.2 and to the usual MSVC/vcvars setup. Brush (Apache-2.0, no CUDA, native Windows) is the low-friction fallback trainer.

missed_developments.claim: Starlette has had a security advisory and a series of fixes in its Range handling since 0.39 (GHSA-7f5h-v6xp-fcq8 in 0.49.1; fixes in 1.0.0rc1, 1.5.1 and 1.7.0). FastAPI 0.142.2 only requires starlette>=0.46.0.
missed_developments.details: Pin starlette>=1.7.0 in the lockfile, because the local server streams COPC/RAD/3D Tiles with byte ranges. Bind the server to 127.0.0.1 only.

missed_developments.claim: KHR_gaussian_splatting_compression_spz_2 is still an open glTF PR (#2531), not ratified, although LuciadRIA 2026.1 and the Three.js 3DGS plugin already consume it. The SPZ reference library has moved to file version 4.
missed_developments.details: Treat spz_2 as a moving target. Pin the encoder version, and validate each 3D Tiles export against LuciadRIA and the Three.js plugin before promising it as a deliverable.

missed_developments.claim: The Three.js 3D Tiles splat plugin renders through 'Gaussian Splat Lite', not Spark, and accepts only spz_2 payloads.
missed_developments.details: The scene.json-driven viewer should use either a Spark path (PLY/SPZ/SOG/RAD with LoD) or a 3D Tiles path per splat layer, never both in one scene, because two splat sorters do not composite with each other. Keep Spark plus RAD/SOG as the primary web path and 3D Tiles as the Luciad/Cesium interchange export. Core 3DTilesRendererJS also has a Potree plugin, which is an option for the LiDAR layer.

missed_developments.claim: pycolmap.align_reconstruction_to_locations (and COLMAP pose_prior_mapper) can turn the BLK2GO trajectory plus the measured device offset directly into a metric Sim(3), or into priors, in the LiDAR frame.
missed_developments.details: This is the natural implementation of the 'device-offset prior' edge in the frame graph. Interpolate the BLK2GO trajectory at the Insta360 frame timestamps, apply the lever arm, and call align_reconstruction_to_locations, then refine with ICP against the LiDAR (external library). Alternatively, feed the positions as pose priors to pose_prior_mapper (default prior std 1.0 m, overridable) so the SfM is metric and LiDAR-framed from the start. align_reconstructions_via_points only applies between two COLMAP reconstructions, for example ground and drone groups.

missed_developments.claim: Since v0.5.0, LichtFeld Studio Windows binaries come only through a paid, donation-based Portal; GitHub releases carry source archives only.
missed_developments.details: For a zero-cost, no-watermark Windows workflow, LichtFeld means building from source (C++23, CUDA 12.8+). Keep gsplat or Brush as the default trainer modules.

missed_developments.claim: COLMAP 4.1's native spherical camera model is described as 'generally faster but less accurate than rendering perspective views'.
missed_developments.details: For the Insta360 source module, keep cubemap or perspective rendering with a rig as the quality path and treat the spherical model as a quick-look option. The COLMAP Windows CUDA binary (colmap-x64-windows-cuda.zip) is available in 4.2.1.

verification.recommendation_assessment:
The core architecture holds up and is proportionate. It has five parts: a FastAPI backend on localhost; each stage run as a CLI subprocess in a Windows Job Object; a hand-rolled, content-hashed DAG with JSON records; a frame graph with Sim(3) edges and the anchor policy (LiDAR, else drone ENU, else arbitrary); and a single Vite/Three.js viewer driven by scene.json with capability-gated toggles. Its main evidence also checked out against primary sources: the gsplat normalization default, the Selector event loop under reload, FastAPI SSE, CPU-only pycolmap on Windows, and the poor fit of Snakemake, Prefect and Hamilton.

Seven changes are needed:
1. **gsplat packaging.** The packaging plan is internally inconsistent. No prebuilt Windows gsplat wheel exists for torch ≥2.5 or cu128. Choose explicitly between gsplat 1.5.3+pt24cu124 (prebuilt) and a source build of main/1.6 with VS Build Tools and CUDA 12.8 (not 13.2+). Keep Brush as a no-CUDA fallback. Pixi's 'don't mix PyPI torch with conda torch-dependents' rule affects how PDAL and torch share one environment; consider two environments, each stage running as its own subprocess.
2. **Registration call.** Replace 'pycolmap align_reconstructions_via_points + ICP' for SfM→LiDAR with align_reconstruction_to_locations, or pose_prior_mapper priors, using BLK2GO trajectory positions plus the device offset, then refine with ICP from an external library. align_reconstructions_via_* is only for aligning one imagery group to another.
3. **Splat frame.** Training in the project frame with normalize_world_space=False is still the cleanest choice; scene_scale adapts. But the claim that viewer-side transforms are unsafe was too strong. Spark evaluates SH in object space, and splat-transform rotates SH when baking. So keep training frames flexible: apply the registration as a viewer node transform during iteration, and bake it with splat-transform at export. Keep the bbox regression test.
4. **3D Tiles.** Keep it as a secondary interchange export, not as part of 'the same viewer'. The spz_2 extension is unratified (open PR #2531), and the Three.js 3DGS plugin requires spz_2 and uses a different renderer (Gaussian Splat Lite). Validate in LuciadRIA 2026.1 directly.
5. **Starlette pin.** Pin starlette ≥1.7.0 because of the Range-parsing security fixes, and never use `fastapi dev`/--reload for the job host.
6. **Paths with spaces.** Downgrade this from 'known breakage' to a precaution: the cited issues are 2019–2020 and closed. Keep the space-free root because it costs nothing.
7. **LichtFeld.** Since v0.5 its Windows binaries are paid-portal only, which matters if it was planned as a trainer module.

The phase-1 scope (only the LiDAR + Insta360 modules, plus a drone stub with capability declarations and a DJI XMP probe) should stay as is. The reconstruction-group mechanism, which makes drone options (b) and (c) a configuration switch, is well founded.

option_comparison.cost: Hardware: nothing beyond the existing BLK2GO and Insta360. Add 4-6 dual-use targets: a B/W checker on top for the cameras plus a retro-reflective or raised geometric element for the LiDAR. These are DIY or a few thousand SEK (estimate). An optional telescopic pole for 360 views at 3-5 m. Licences: EUR 0 (COLMAP BSD, gsplat Apache-2.0, Spark MIT; Cyclone is already available). Permits: no Lantmäteriet permit, because lag 2016:319 §9 covers only information captured from aircraft. GDPR blurring of faces and number plates is still needed. Do a skyddsobjekt check (skyddslag §7 can ban depicting or measuring a site, and this applies to ground capture too) and get written landowner consent as good practice. Field time: one loop walk plus about 20-30 min to place and recover targets. Compute: one SfM and one splat on the 16 GB GPU.
option_comparison.complexity: Lowest. Two source modules and one reconstruction group. One registration edge, Insta360-SfM to LiDAR: pycolmap align_reconstruction_to_locations or pose_prior_mapper using the BLK2GO trajectory plus the measured lever arm, an external ICP check, and target checkpoints. Viewer presets: LiDAR / Splat / Combined.
option_comparison.expected_quality_gain: This is the baseline. Swedish 10x10 m plot: complete ground, understory and trunk coverage at eye level, which is what the ground-walk viewer shows. The canopy appears only from below (Insta360 8K is about 12 mm/px at 15 m), with no crown tops, which a walking viewer never sees anyway. Dense tropical forest: the floor and understory are good. The canopy top at 30-50 m is missing or blurry, and handheld scanners underestimate tree height (one HMLS study: -2.34 m bias). In Sweden only, context around the plot can be added for free from Lantmäteriet open ALS (1-2 pts/m2), the 1 m DTM and 0.16 m orthophotos. That needs a coarse LiDAR-to-SWEREF placement, because the BLK2GO has no GNSS.
option_comparison.risks: The core LiDAR-splat registration is still unproven, so it is the right thing to test first. There is no aerial overview. The tropical canopy top is missing. Ground data still needs GDPR and skyddsobjekt checks.
option_comparison.verdict: Use for Phase 1, and keep it as the permanent default configuration that the drone layer is added to. Do not buy or fly a drone for the first test, but do place the targets: they are cheap checkpoints and a rehearsal for the drone phase.

option_comparison.option: (b) LiDAR + Insta360 + drone merged into ONE splat
option_comparison.cost: Hardware: the same drone as (c), plus bridging capture: elevator ascents and low obliques at a gap or edge, a 5-8 m pole, or a 360 drone such as the DJI Avata 360 (about USD 719, EU C1). The commercial fusion vendor recommends an RTX 3090/4090 with 64 GB RAM or more, which is above the 3080 Ti laptop. Licences: the reference code (Horizon-GS, UC-GS) is under the Inria non-commercial licence, MASt3R is CC BY-NC-SA, and SuperPoint is restrictive. A commercial path means reimplementing on Apache gsplat (PPISP needs gsplat 1.6, a source build on Windows). XGRIDS-style commercial fusion needs RTK on both devices, and the BLK2GO has none. Permits: everything in (c), plus the whole merged splat, ground content included, counts as drone-derived. It therefore sits behind the Lantmäteriet permit: about 65 working days, applied for only after processing, and 3D models cannot be retouched. The ground model cannot be published from this artefact. Field time: (c) plus about 30-60 min of bridging capture, and it needs a clearing or edge next to the plot.
option_comparison.complexity: Highest. Joint aerial-ground SfM is needed, but SIFT fails at about 90 deg nadir-to-horizontal. DRAGON reached 50% registration with plain COLMAP, and DUSt3R placed fewer than 5% of pairs within 5 deg, rising to 56% only after fine-tuning on urban data. It also needs learned matchers (ALIKED/DISK + LightGlue, or RoMa), separate camera ids plus PPISP, a custom staged sampling and densification trainer, antialiasing, a split Gaussian budget (about 4-6M max on 16 GB), and cm-consistent joint poses. Decimetre registration from (c) is not enough.
option_comparison.expected_quality_gain: Swedish plot: about 0 dB expected at ground level, with real risk of degradation. Horizon-GS street PSNR was 23.80 vs 23.84 for Scaffold-GS, and its balancing mechanisms change street PSNR by only -0.04/-0.06/-0.01 dB. UC-GS gained +0.4-0.7 dB on synthetic data, and naive A+G gave +0.02/-0.18 dB. In MatrixCity, fusion was worse than both single-domain models. Forest-specific problems: few co-visible surfaces, conflicting opacity at the canopy layer (inference), foliage motion, floaters and a double canopy. The only real benefit is one model with a seamless ground-to-sky fly-up. Dense tropical forest: effectively infeasible. The canopy is closed, so there are no bridging views and almost nothing both sensors see.
option_comparison.risks: SfM likely splits into two components anyway (COLMAP 4.2's multi-component mapper would return them separately). Other risks: gradient and densification conflicts; ghosting at crown edges; the VRAM and RAM budget; non-commercial licence exposure; the permit blocking publication of the ground content; an evidence base that is synthetic or urban (only one real forest LiDAR-anchored paper, validated only in open canopy); and a large schedule cost.
option_comparison.verdict: Rejected as a product path. Keep it only as an opt-in research 'merge' setting on a reconstruction group, tried after (c) works, at an open Swedish forest edge or clearing with bridging capture. Never use it in closed tropical canopy. If it is tried, a 'loose merge' (poses from (c) plus gsplat pose_opt) is enough. Porting the Horizon-GS mechanisms is not justified, because their measured benefit is in aerial views only.

option_comparison.option: (c) Drone as a SEPARATE aerial model, registered into the shared (LiDAR) frame and shown as its own layer
option_comparison.cost: Hardware, Sweden: a C0 camera drone, either a DJI Mini 5 Pro (1-inch 50 MP; C0 only with the standard battery) or a Mini 4 Pro bought with the RC-N2 controller if MSDK automation (Dronelink/Litchi) is needed. About EUR 800-1,200, 2026 price not verified. Spare batteries and 6-8 dual-use targets. A DJI Matrice 4E (C2, integrated RTK, mechanical shutter, about EUR 4,599) only for tropical multi-hectare grids or georeferenced no-LiDAR projects. Licences: EUR 0 on the open path (COLMAP + gsplat). Optional: Pixpro about EUR 5/month, SWEPOS RTK 2,000 SEK per 30 days, DJI Terra GS USD 3,700/yr, Metashape or Leica Infinity if Hexagon already licenses them. ODX/WebODM is AGPL and can be used as an external process. Admin: Transportstyrelsen operator registration (190 SEK + 250 SEK/yr), the A1/A3 card (600 SEK; flying a drone of 250 g or more without it has been a crime since 1 Jan 2026), the A2 card (850 SEK) if a C2 flies near people, and mandatory third-party liability insurance for work flights (EU 785/2004, so confirm Hexagon's cover). Also check the LFV drone map and NOTAMs, reserve and national-park rules, and get written landowner consent. Lantmäteriet dissemination permit: free, about 65 working days after the material is final, before ANY sharing, which includes email, cloud, OneDrive and hosted viewers. Field time: +15-30 min of flying (300-550 stills, 1-2 batteries), plus about 30-60 min for zone and site checks, target layout and takeoff, all in the same overcast window as the ground walk.
option_comparison.complexity: Moderate. A drone source module (EXIF/XMP probe, RtkFlag, capabilities) and its own reconstruction group (COLMAP spatial matcher plus pose_prior_mapper). A separate gsplat model: antialiased, MCMC cap about 1-3M, images on host or disk, 1600-2000 px. A new frame-graph edge from drone to LiDAR: triangulated target centres, a robust Umeyama Sim(3), and ICP as a gated refinement only. Viewer: a new 'aerial' group/preset, volume partitioning by the LiDAR canopy height model, a cross-fade on camera height above the DTM using SplatMesh.opacity inside one Spark sort and LoD budget, and a per-layer quality badge plus a dissemination-clearance flag. Estimate: about 1-2 weeks of engineering once Phase 1 works. Because Spark evaluates SH in object space, the aerial layer can be re-registered as a viewer transform without retraining.
option_comparison.expected_quality_gain: Swedish 10x10 m plot: no change at walking height, by design, because the ground splat is untouched. It adds crown tops (about 5 mm/px at 30 m range at 50 MP, about 1 cm at 12 MP), gaps, edges, terrain and the surroundings, for an overview or fly-up mode. In thinned pine, oblique views may add some stems and ground (TreeDGS). For a 10x10 m plot the marginal gain is small to moderate, and much of the context value can be had for free and with no permit from Lantmäteriet open data, at lower resolution and not photoreal. Dense tropical forest: high. It is the only practical source of canopy-top content, because the ground devices cannot see a canopy 30-50 m up. It adds nothing for the floor, since SfM rarely reaches the ground there.
option_comparison.risks: Registration is decimetre-level away from the targets (0.2-0.6 m markerless). The target tie needs a clearing, track or edge within the BLK2GO loop. Other risks: double surfaces or ghosting at the canopy boundary if the layer partition is wrong; a shared mobile splat budget of about 500K; Spark sort lag during fast fades; permit delay or refusal (whole-model, no retouching); target detectability in BLK2GO intensity; datum and height mix-ups (ETRS89 vs WGS84 about 0.9 m; ellipsoid vs RH 2000 heights tens of metres apart); and Hexagon policy on buying DJI.
option_comparison.verdict: RECOMMENDED way to support drones. It is an optional later phase on top of (a), and the default whenever the drone source is selected. It cannot degrade the ground splat, tolerates decimetre registration, keeps the ground model publishable while the aerial layer waits for its permit, and fits the modular reconstruction-group design.

option_comparison.option: (a+) Supplementary no-drone variant: (a) plus a Lantmäteriet open-data context layer and/or the Insta360 on a mast
option_comparison.cost: About EUR 0 for the data. Lantmäteriet publishes it, so no dissemination permit is needed, but check the licence string per product (CC0 vs CC BY 4.0). A telescopic mast or pole costs a few hundred to a few thousand SEK (background knowledge). Elevated capture with ground contact is outside lag 2016:319 §9 and outside aviation rules. No extra field time apart from optional pole passes.
option_comparison.complexity: Low to moderate. One 'context' source module (COPC/LAZ + GeoTIFF import), but it needs an optional LiDAR-to-SWEREF 99 transform. That can come from an RTK rover on the targets, or from a coarse registration of the BLK2GO terrain to the 1 m DTM (metre to decimetre level).
option_comparison.expected_quality_gain: Sweden only. Coarse terrain and orthophoto context around the plot (0.16 m orthophoto, 1-2 pts/m2), not photoreal crown tops. The mast adds mid-canopy viewpoints from 3-8 m without a drone. It adds nothing in the tropics.
option_comparison.risks: Georeferencing the GNSS-less BLK2GO frame. A visible terrain seam at the plot boundary. The open-data licence and resolution are unverified per product.
option_comparison.verdict: Try this as the cheap interim context option for Swedish sites before buying a drone. If it meets the overview need, the Swedish case for (c) becomes optional, and (c) stays aimed at tropical canopy-top documentation.

critic.recommended_option: (c), the drone as a separate aerial model registered into the shared LiDAR frame and shown as its own layer, is the recommended way to add drone support. It enters as an optional later phase on top of (a). (a), LiDAR + Insta360, stays the Phase-1 test and the default configuration. (b), one merged splat, is rejected as a product path. It survives only as an opt-in research 'merge' setting on a reconstruction group, to be tried at an open Swedish edge or clearing after (c) works and never in closed tropical canopy. The reasons are: no measured ground-view gain (Horizon-GS street parity; Horizon-GS mechanisms change street PSNR by only about 0.05 dB), unreliable aerial-ground SfM in forests, cm-pose requirements that the BLK2GO setup cannot meet, non-commercial reference code, hardware below vendor guidance, and a merged model that is drone-derived as a whole, so the Swedish dissemination permit would also block publication of the ground content. Before buying a drone for Swedish sites, test whether free Lantmäteriet open data (ALS, DTM, 0.16 m orthophoto) already covers the context need.
critic.drone_phase_timing:
Do not bring the drone forward. None of the six fact-checked topics found evidence for an earlier start, and the regulations add a gate of about 13 weeks after processing in Sweden.

Phase 1 (first test, LiDAR + Insta360):
- Build only the LiDAR and Insta360 modules.
- Place 4-6 dual-use targets anyway, as independent checkpoints for the splat-to-LiDAR edge and to test whether target centres can be detected in BLK2GO and Insta360 data.
- Ship a drone-module STUB: capability declarations, a probe for DJI EXIF/XMP (RtkFlag, RelativeAltitude, ellipsoidal heights), and a dissemination_clearance/lineage field. This exercises the anchor-frame policy and the source-combination UI early, using public sample DJI data and no flights.

Phase 2 (ground pipeline hardening and web delivery):
- In parallel, start the drone groundwork that has lead time: check Hexagon's procurement policy on DJI, register the operator, get the A1/A3 card, confirm liability insurance, set up a non-synced local data folder.
- Try the free Lantmäteriet open-data context layer (option a+).

Phase 3 (optional Swedish drone pilot, option c):
- Choose a plot that touches a clearing, track or edge.
- Start only when four conditions are met:
  1. Phase-1 checkpoint RMSE has been measured and target detection works.
  2. Ground splat-to-LiDAR alignment is validated.
  3. The viewer supports multiple layers (Spark joint sort, CHM partition, cross-fade).
  4. The legal checklist is done.
- Submit images to Lantmäteriet right after capture, and keep everything local until the permit is cleared.
- Optionally capture bridging images so a (b) research experiment stays possible.

Phase 4 (tropical campaigns):
- (c) has the most value here (canopy top), so run the Swedish pilot early enough to rehearse before the first tropical date.
- Start the country-specific legal review and arrange a local licensed operator months ahead.

Bring Phase 3 forward only if a tropical campaign date is fixed and close, or if drone-only or drone+Insta360 (no-LiDAR) projects become a hard requirement. Even then, the stub covers the frame logic without real flights.
new_risks: Swedish dissemination permit (Lantmäteriet spridningstillstånd, lag 2016:319 §9). Any drone-derived product (images, ortho, DSM, 3D model or splat) needs a permit before it is shared. The permit is free but takes about 65 working days. It cannot be applied for in advance, only with finished material. Lantmäteriet cannot retouch 3D models, so a model is approved or refused as a whole. Spreading without a permit is punishable by fines or up to 1 year in prison.

Dissemination is defined broadly: email, web publication, and storage on cloud or servers you do not fully control. The project folder is under C:\Users\Leonard Lind\Desktop, which Windows 11 often syncs to OneDrive. Raw drone data and drone-derived models must live in a non-synced local folder. They must stay out of Git remotes, LFS, CDNs, hosted viewers and LuciadRIA servers until the permit is cleared.

Lineage contamination. Any model trained on drone pixels inherits the drone's clearance status, so option (b) blocks publication of the ground content. A ground splat whose scale or poses came from a joint SfM with drone images is a grey zone. The source interface must track lineage, not just a per-source flag.

The Lantmäteriet forest exemption is narrow: the landowner must commission or take the material, with no vehicles, no non-forestry human activity, no power lines and no wider surroundings in view. The context/surroundings layer, which is the main purpose of (c), and frames showing the BLK2GO operator probably void it. Plan to apply.

Aviation compliance becomes a project dependency:
- Operator registration is required for any camera drone (190 SEK + 250 SEK/yr).
- The A1/A3 card is required for drones of 250 g or more; flying without it has been a crime since 1 Jan 2026.
- Liability insurance is mandatory for work flights (EU 785/2004).
- Check the LFV drone map, control zones (the 5 km and 50 m/10 m rules) and heliports within 1,000 m.
- Check nature reserve and national park take-off/landing bans and bird-season access bans.
- The A3 rule of 150 m from 'recreational areas' is undefined for public-access forests.

EASA Opinion 06/2026 (not yet adopted) would lower registration, Remote ID and training thresholds to 100 g, with first effects around mid-2028. Buy a class-labelled drone with Remote ID. Also, Mini 5 Pro and Antigravity A1 become C1 with the larger battery.

Skyddslag (2010:305) §7 can ban depicting or measuring a designated protected site (substations, military land), and it applies to ground LiDAR and 360 capture as well. Add a site check that covers every source module.

Tropical legal risk. Rules vary by country and are often closed to foreigners (Indonesia: local company only; Brazil RBAC 100 with SISANT/SARPAS/ANATEL; Malaysia CAAM ATF at least 14 working days plus JUPEM for mapping; Costa Rica DGAC plus SINAC/MINAE). EU certificates are generally not recognised. Expect months of lead time and a local operator. The details rest on secondary sources only.

No shared surfaces for registration under canopy. The drone sees crown tops, the BLK2GO and Insta360 see trunks and crown undersides. The target tie needs a clearing, track or edge within the BLK2GO loop, which constrains plot selection. Where none exists (closed tropical canopy), the only fallback is markerless registration at 0.2-0.6 m, or failure in dense canopy.

Targets may not be detectable by the LiDAR. White paint has about the same reflectivity as vegetation at LiDAR wavelengths, so B/W checkers may not stand out in BLK2GO intensity. Neither the cm-level centre accuracy of BLK2GO/Cyclone targets nor BLK2GO SLAM drift between the plot and a nearby clearing has been verified for forest.

GSD and target size are inconsistent with the proposed altitudes. The 2-5 cm drone-to-LiDAR estimate assumes 1-1.5 cm GSD. A mapping block at canopy+40-60 m over a 20-25 m canopy gives about 2.2-3+ cm GSD at 12 MP. This needs a dedicated low GCP pass over the clearing, or larger targets (at least 20x GSD on the diagonal for auto-detection).

Datum and height errors:
- ETRS89/SWEREF 99 vs WGS84/ITRF differ by about 0.9 m, growing about 2.5 cm/yr.
- Ellipsoidal, EGM96 and RH 2000 heights differ by tens of metres.
- Non-RTK DJI absolute altitude can be 5-50 m off.
- Metashape reads XMP AbsoluteAltitude first.
All of this must be handled explicitly in the frame graph, with float64 and CRS/epoch metadata.

Viewer composition risks:
- Double canopy or ghosting from decimetre misregistration if the aerial and ground layers overlap. A CHM-based volume partition is needed.
- One mobile splat budget of about 500K is shared by two layers.
- Spark's sort lags at least one frame during fast cross-fades.
- The Three.js 3D Tiles splat plugin (Gaussian Splat Lite, spz_2 only) cannot depth-sort together with Spark.
- KHR_gaussian_splatting_compression_spz_2 is not ratified.

Compute and packaging:
- An aerial set of 300-550 images adds SfM time.
- ODM/ODX needs about 16-32 GB RAM for 250-500 images, and the laptop's system RAM is unknown.
- TreeDGS used 32 GB VRAM for 365 images, so downscale and cap Gaussians.
- PPISP and the newer MCMC and pose features are only in gsplat 1.6 (Jan 2026, confirmed on the gsplat README), which has no prebuilt Windows wheel. A source build with CUDA 12.8 (not 13.2+) is needed.

Licensing traps on the merge path: Horizon-GS, UC-GS and INRIA 3DGS are non-commercial (Inria); CityGS-X has no licence; MASt3R is CC BY-NC-SA; SuperPoint is restrictive; the original VGGT-1B is non-commercial; ODM, ODX and OpenSplat are AGPL (acceptable as an external process). DJI Terra GS costs USD 3,700/yr.

Hardware, vendor and corporate policy:
- Hexagon may restrict DJI purchases (the US FCC status of DJI is unverified).
- Leica BLK2FLY no longer appears on Leica's product page, so there is no Hexagon-native aerial sensor (low confidence).
- Mini 4 Pro MSDK works only with the RC-N2 controller, and its Plus battery is not sold in the EU.
- Pixpro currently offers only single grids and orbits, so automating oblique crosshatches on C0 drones may need manual waypoints or Dronelink.
- The 2026 status of non-DJI alternatives (Autel) is unverified.

Scene inconsistency between captures: wind-driven foliage, possibly rotor downwash (inference), light changes beyond about 30-60 min, and season mismatch (a leaf-off drone flight vs a leaf-on ground walk). Brown 2024 found the best weather differs by goal: overcast for sparse-forest canopy height and for appearance, clear sky in autumn for DEMs.

Field safety and operations: DJI obstacle sensing does not reliably detect thin branches, so under-canopy flight is unsafe. Visual line of sight must be kept from clearings. Over a 30-50 m tropical canopy with taller emergent trees, the 120 m AGL cap leaves little altitude margin. The ground operator must be kept out of aerial frames (GDPR and loss of the exemption).

Test matrix growth. Three sources give 7 non-empty combinations, each with a different anchor frame and scale status (LiDAR, drone ENU/RTK, or arbitrary SfM). Drone + Insta360 without LiDAR has no reliable scale path under canopy unless targets or a scale bar are used. The UI must show per-layer scale, georeference, quality and clearance status.

Evidence risk. Almost all aerial-ground radiance-field evidence is synthetic or urban (MatrixCity, UC-GS, DRAGON, AerialMegaDepth; Horizon-GS has 2 real urban scenes). The only real forest LiDAR + UAV 3DGS paper was validated in open canopy only. The forest-specific conclusions are partly inference. The workflow's web-search budget ran out, so newer real-data studies may have been missed.

gaps.title: Lantmäteriet permit mechanics for splats derived from drone images, model versions and internal sharing
gaps.why_it_matters:
The permit decides whether (c)'s aerial layer can be iterated and shared at all. It also decides how lineage and clearance must be modelled in the source interface, and whether a drone + Insta360 project without LiDAR is legally workable. The topics disagree on several points:
- Whether derived 3D models from approved images need no separate review, or each model version needs a new application.
- Whether a Hexagon on-prem server counts as 'full control'.
- Whether a ground-only splat that only took poses or scale from drone SfM is covered.
- Whether the forest exemption survives the BLK2GO operator and targets being visible in the frames.
gaps.research_prompt:
Research Sweden's rules on dissemination of aerial imagery (lag 2016:319 om skydd för geografisk information §9; förordning 2016:320; Lantmäteriet's spridningstillstånd pages, FAQ (vanliga frågor), exemption (undantag) pages and the LMFS regulation on exemptions) as they apply to a Gaussian-splat 3D model trained from consumer-drone photos of a ~10x10 m forest plot plus a ~60x60 m buffer, as of October 2026. Answer each question with verbatim Swedish quotes and URLs:
(1) If the source JPGs are submitted and approved, may new splat or mesh versions trained from the returned images be published without a new application? Find the exact wording on 'följdprodukter'.
(2) If a finished 3D model is submitted instead, is it approved or refused as a whole, and does each retrained version need a new application?
(3) Is storage on a company-controlled on-premises server, a corporate OneDrive/SharePoint or a private Git remote 'dissemination' ('servrar som du inte själv har fullständig kontroll över')?
(4) Is a model built only from ground photos and handheld LiDAR, whose coordinate frame or scale came from a drone photogrammetry solution or from drone-visible targets, covered by §9?
(5) Does the forest exemption still apply if a person carrying a survey instrument, survey targets or a forest road is visible, and does it cover a buffer of surroundings?
(6) Current processing time and upload limits, and whether an approved case number can be cited publicly.
Also give the exact email or form for asking Lantmäteriet a pre-capture question, and draft that question in Swedish. Do not rely on blogs where a Lantmäteriet page exists, and say which answers are only inference.

gaps.title: Feasibility and accuracy of a shared-target tie between drone imagery and BLK2GO data under forest conditions
gaps.why_it_matters:
Every topic names physical targets as the primary drone-to-LiDAR tie (2-5 cm expected), and both (c) and any (b) attempt depend on it. Four things are unverified:
- Whether BLK2GO/Cyclone can extract target centres at cm level.
- Which target design shows up in BLK2GO intensity against vegetation and also in drone and 360 imagery.
- How much BLK2GO SLAM drifts between the plot interior and a clearing 10-30 m away.
- Which tool on Windows can run a bundle adjustment with GCPs given in a local, non-georeferenced frame.
The GSD the targets need also conflicts with the proposed flight altitudes.
gaps.research_prompt:
Research, as of October 2026, how to tie a drone photogrammetry block to a Leica BLK2GO handheld SLAM point cloud (no GNSS, Cyclone FIELD 360 / REGISTER 360 PLUS export) through shared ground targets. Find primary sources (Leica documentation, Leica/Hexagon release notes, peer-reviewed or vendor test reports) on:
(1) Whether Cyclone REGISTER 360 PLUS (BLK edition) or Cyclone FIELD 360 supports control points, checkerboard or B/W targets, or sphere targets for BLK2GO data, including any 'BLK2GO GCP' or georeferencing feature, its workflow, and its stated accuracy.
(2) The achievable target-centre accuracy in BLK2GO clouds (range noise ±3 mm, point spacing) for planar checkerboards, retro-reflective targets and spheres at 1-10 m range, and whether white paint and vegetation can be told apart in BLK2GO intensity.
(3) Measured BLK2GO SLAM drift or relative accuracy outdoors or in forests over 20-100 m loops, ideally with independent checkpoints.
(4) A dual-use target design that a camera drone at 1-3 cm GSD and the BLK2GO can both detect (size versus the Pix4D rule of 5-10x GSD manual and 20x GSD automatic).
(5) Software that can run bundle adjustment with GCPs in an arbitrary local Cartesian frame on Windows: Agisoft Metashape local coordinates, Leica Infinity, OpenDroneMap/OpenSfM with a fake projected CRS, or COLMAP plus pycolmap/pyceres with a custom GCP residual. For each, give the licence and whether it handles DJI XMP metadata.
Give numbers with URLs and mark what is unverified.

gaps.title: Real-data evidence on what aerial imagery adds to a forest splat, and what a drone actually sees of Swedish forest stands
gaps.why_it_matters: The decision against (b), and the value of (c) for Swedish plots, rests mostly on synthetic or urban studies (MatrixCity, UC-GS, DRAGON, AerialMegaDepth, Horizon-GS) plus inference about forests. Only one real forest LiDAR + UAV 3DGS paper was found, and it covered open canopy only. TreeDGS suggests oblique aerial images can recover stems in thinned pine, which might give (c) more value in Sweden than 'canopy only'. Whether (c) beats free Lantmäteriet open data for a 10x10 m plot also depends on this evidence.
gaps.research_prompt:
Find 2024-2026 papers, preprints, theses and credible practitioner case studies (arXiv, CVPR/ICCV/ECCV/WACV workshops, ISPRS, Remote Sensing, Forests, IEEE TGRS) that reconstruct REAL forests with NeRF or 3D Gaussian Splatting from BOTH drone/UAV images AND ground-level or under-canopy images, or from UAV images plus handheld or terrestrial LiDAR. Candidate searches include 'forest Gaussian splatting UAV terrestrial', 'aerial-ground 3DGS forest', 'TreeDGS', 'LiDAR-guided semantic 3D Gaussian splatting forest digital twin', 'under-canopy NeRF drone', 'ForestSplat', 'boreal forest 3DGS', and 'Gaussian splatting tropical forest canopy UAV'. For each paper, report:
- forest type and canopy density
- sensors, altitudes and overlaps
- how aerial and ground poses were tied (joint SfM, GNSS/RTK, LiDAR registration, targets)
- whether ground-level novel-view metrics (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS) were reported with and without aerial images
- the reported failure modes
- code licence
Separately, find measurements of how much stem or forest-floor area oblique drone photogrammetry recovers in Scots pine, Norway spruce and birch stands in Sweden or Finland, by stand density or canopy cover. Compare with the resolution and coverage of Lantmäteriet's open data (Laserdata NH/Skog point density, Markhöjdmodell 1 m, ortofoto 0.16 m; confirm the licence per product). Conclude whether a consumer-drone aerial splat adds information beyond that open data for a 10x10 m plot.

gaps.title: Drone procurement, automation and corporate-policy constraints for a C0/C1 versus RTK platform in 2026
gaps.why_it_matters: The topics disagree on the platform: C0 Mini 5 Pro, Mini 4 Pro for MSDK automation, or an RTK Matrice 4E. Current EU and Swedish prices were not verified. Whether Hexagon policy allows buying DJI is unknown, and so is whether BLK2FLY or any Hexagon aerial sensor is still available. Automating the nadir + oblique + orbit protocol on C0 drones is uncertain (Pixpro has no oblique multi-grid; MSDK works only with RC-N2). These factors set the cost and feasibility of (c).
gaps.research_prompt:
As of October 2026, compile a procurement comparison for a small-plot forest aerial-photogrammetry and Gaussian-splat drone to be flown in Sweden under EU Open-category rules by a Hexagon employee. Candidates: DJI Mini 4 Pro (RC-N2 bundle), DJI Mini 5 Pro, DJI Lito X1, DJI Air 3S, DJI Matrice 4E, Autel EVO II Pro (RTK) V3 or its successor, Parrot ANAFI UKR/Ai, and any Leica/Hexagon aerial capture product (check whether BLK2FLY is discontinued).
For each, give:
- current Swedish/EU retail price
- EASA class label and the configuration it depends on (battery)
- Remote ID
- sensor size, resolution and shutter type
- minimum photo interval at full and binned resolution
- RTK/PPK support
- MSDK or other SDK support and the required controller
- which mission apps (DJI Fly waypoints, DJI Pilot 2, Dronelink, Litchi Pilot/Hub, Pixpro Waypoints, UgCS, Pix4Dcapture successor) can fly a nadir grid, a 4-direction oblique grid at 45 deg, and multi-radius orbits with hover-and-shoot, and at what cost
Also find:
- any public Hexagon/Leica policy, or EU/Swedish public-sector or defence-industry guidance, restricting DJI products
- the current US FCC Covered List status of DJI and Autel, with its relevance to EU buyers
- the 2026 status of EASA Opinion 06/2026
Cite primary vendor and regulator pages and flag estimates.

conflicts.description: Flight altitude and GSD. aerial-ground-fusion: about 20-30 m above the canopy top. drone-forest-canopy: 30-70 m AGL, which its fact-checker called too low and wrongly referenced, recommending about 70-110 m AGL with at least 45-60 m canopy clearance. drone-capture-hardware: nadir at canopy+40-60 m, with orbits at canopy+15/30/45 m. drone-alignment's 2-5 cm accuracy assumes 1-1.5 cm GSD, which these mapping heights do not produce (a Mini at 12 MP is about D/27 cm). The EU 120 m AGL cap is measured from the closest terrain point, and over a 30-50 m tropical canopy it leaves little margin.
conflicts.suggested_resolution:
State heights as clearance above the canopy top:
- Mapping block (nadir plus obliques) at canopy+40-60 m, never above 120 m AGL.
- Orbits at canopy+15-45 m only where emergent trees leave safe clearance, for angular diversity.
- A separate low GCP pass over the target clearing at about 20-30 m above the clearing ground, giving about 1 cm GSD.
- Targets sized at least 20x GSD on the diagonal for the pass that measures them (60 cm or larger).
- In the tropics, fly from clearings or rivers, keep the mapping block at canopy+40 m or more within 120 m AGL, and do not fly low orbits among emergent trees.

conflicts.description: Still resolution and format. aerial-ground-fusion recommends 48 MP stills. drone-capture-hardware recommends 12 MP binned mode: readout 2-4x faster, a 2 s rather than 5 s minimum interval, and smaller files. drone-capture-hardware says JPEG is enough, while Pixpro recommends RAW.
conflicts.suggested_resolution: Use 12 MP 4:3 JPEG as the default, because training downsamples to 1600-2000 px anyway. Use 48/50 MP only with hover-and-shoot waypoints when crown detail or GCP measurement needs it. Never mix the two modes in one COLMAP camera group, since they have different intrinsics. Add DNG only if colour-matching with the Insta360 is planned.

conflicts.description:
Overlap, oblique angle and timing window.
- Overlap: 80/70 (aerial-ground-fusion), 90/80-85 (drone-forest-canopy), 85-90/75-80 (drone-capture-hardware), above 95% for best completeness (Frey 2018).
- Obliques: 30-45 deg off-nadir (fusion), 45-60 deg (canopy), -45 deg (hardware), 20-35 deg to reduce doming (alignment).
- Timing: within ±30 min (fusion), about 1 h (canopy), 30-60 min (hardware). Brown 2024 adds that clear autumn skies are best for DEMs.
conflicts.suggested_resolution:
Forest default:
- 90% front and 80% side overlap.
- An oblique crosshatch at about 45 deg off-nadir, which also controls doming, with orbits covering 30-50 deg.
- Same uniform-overcast window as the ground walk: under 30 min apart preferred, 60 min at most, canopy wind under about 3-4 m/s.
- If terrain or a DEM is the goal rather than appearance matching, schedule a separate flight.

conflicts.description: Whether RTK is needed, and which drone class. drone-alignment recommends an RTK/PPK drone (Matrice 4E, C2) if the drone phase goes ahead. drone-capture-hardware says RTK is optional and a C0 drone is enough. drone-regulations prefers C0/C1 in A1, because a C2 in A3 must keep 150 m from loosely defined 'recreational areas' or needs the A2 CofC. aerial-ground-fusion's fact-check prefers the Mini 5 Pro. drone-capture-hardware prefers the Mini 4 Pro for MSDK automation.
conflicts.suggested_resolution:
When LiDAR is present, the targets carry the tie and RTK only adds optional georeferencing. So start with a C0 drone and 6-8 targets with a full Sim(3) fit:
- Mini 5 Pro if DJI Fly waypoints or Pixpro can fly the protocol.
- Mini 4 Pro with RC-N2 if MSDK automation of the oblique grid is needed.
Move to the M4E (RTK, mechanical shutter) only for georeferenced drone-only or drone+Insta360 projects, or for multi-hectare tropical grids. Check Hexagon's DJI policy first (gap 4).

conflicts.description:
Number and design of targets.
- 3-5 GCPs (aerial-ground-fusion, drone-forest-canopy); 4-6 (drone-capture-hardware, and drone-alignment for Phase 1); 5-8 (drone-alignment for the drone phase). ODM and Pix4D call for at least 5 GCPs, each in at least 5 images.
- Design: 40-60 cm B/W checkers (alignment) or checkerboards of at least 0.5 m (canopy), but the alignment fact-check notes that vegetation is as bright as white paint in LiDAR intensity.
- Pole for elevated 360 capture: 3-5 m (canopy, fusion) vs 5-8 m (alignment).
conflicts.suggested_resolution: Phase 1: 4-6 targets as checkpoints. Drone phase: 6-8 (at least 5 control plus at least 2 held-out checkpoints), each seen in at least 5 drone images and passed by the BLK2GO in the same loop. Use dual-use targets: a B/W photogrammetric pattern plus a retro-reflective or raised plane or sphere for the LiDAR, validated in Phase 1. Pole height is a free parameter: start at 3-5 m and go higher only in open stands.

conflicts.description: Expected drone-to-LiDAR registration accuracy. drone-alignment estimates 2-5 cm at the targets. drone-forest-canopy expects 0.1-0.5 m residuals. aerial-ground-fusion quotes decimetre-level literature (0.05-0.25 m). The markerless figures (0.26-0.61 m) are LiDAR-to-LiDAR, which is optimistic for a photogrammetric canopy.
conflicts.suggested_resolution: Plan for two regimes. Near detectable targets, 2-5 cm (medium-to-low confidence until Phase-1 checkpoints measure it). For the plot interior far from the targets, and for markerless fallback, decimetres. Design (c)'s viewer so the content does not overlap (CHM partition plus height cross-fade) and tolerates at least 0.3 m error. (b)'s need for cm-level accuracy is a further reason to reject it.

conflicts.description: How a drone + Insta360 project without LiDAR gets scale. aerial-ground-fusion says joint SfM is the main way the ground splat obtains metric scale. drone-forest-canopy and drone-alignment say joint image matching is not viable under canopy, and the shared targets can instead tie the ground splat to the drone frame. drone-regulations says any model trained on drone pixels inherits the drone's clearance, and pose-only dependence is a grey zone. modular-architecture makes joint vs separate a reconstruction-group setting.
conflicts.suggested_resolution: Default to separate reconstruction groups. The ground splat gets metric scale and georeference from shared targets measured in both groups, or from a user-entered scale bar. Joint SfM stays opt-in. Track lineage in the frame graph and artefact records. Pixel lineage always inherits clearance, and pose or scale lineage is treated as 'pending' until Lantmäteriet clarifies (gap 1).

conflicts.description:
Lantmäteriet permit details.
- Derived products: drone-capture-hardware says derived 3D models of approved material need no separate review, so submit the images and train from the returned set. drone-regulations says applications are accepted only with finished material, 3D models are approved or refused whole, and each new model version probably needs a new application (inference). drone-forest-canopy says only returned material may be used for derivatives.
- Forest exemption: drone-capture-hardware and drone-forest-canopy present it as available, while drone-regulations and drone-alignment say it is narrow (no vehicles, human activity, power lines or surroundings).
- Internal sharing: drone-regulations suggests a Hexagon on-prem server might count as internal, while drone-capture-hardware says only the user's own machine is safe.
conflicts.suggested_resolution: Submit the source images (which count as finished material) right after capture, with a map of the area. Build every splat or mesh from the returned images, relying on the 'skapa följdprodukter' wording. Do not count on the forest exemption for a context layer. Treat everything off the local laptop, including the on-prem server, as dissemination until Lantmäteriet confirms otherwise (gap 1).

conflicts.description: Viewer and delivery path. modular-architecture proposed 3D Tiles (KHR_gaussian_splatting + spz_2) as part of 'the same viewer' for local, public and Luciad use. Its fact-check and drone-forest-canopy found three problems: Spark sorts multiple SplatMeshes in one global sort with joint LoD, the Three.js 3D Tiles splat plugin uses Gaussian Splat Lite, accepts only spz_2 and cannot co-sort with Spark, and spz_2 is not ratified. Budget figures also differ: Spark 1.5M desktop / 500K mobile (fusion) vs 500K-2.5M (canopy), and PlayCanvas about 1M mobile.
conflicts.suggested_resolution: The web viewer renders both the ground and aerial splat layers through Spark, using one sort, one joint LoD budget and SplatMesh.opacity fades. 3D Tiles is only an interchange export for LuciadRIA and Cesium, validated per release with a pinned spz encoder. Budget the mobile total at about 500K, split between layers (for example about 350K ground and 150K aerial), and tune it after testing.

conflicts.description: gsplat features vs Windows packaging. aerial-ground-fusion relies on gsplat PPISP (per-camera ISP compensation), antialiasing, MCMC and pose_opt for the drone layer and any merge. modular-architecture found that prebuilt Windows wheels stop at gsplat 1.5.3+pt24cu124, and that main/1.6 needs a source build. Checked in this pass: the gsplat README says PPISP was integrated in Jan 2026 in v1.6.0, so it is not in any prebuilt Windows wheel.
conflicts.suggested_resolution: Decide in Phase 1. Either source-build gsplat 1.6 on Windows (VS Build Tools, CUDA 12.8, not 13.2+), which also unlocks PPISP for multi-camera appearance work, or pin 1.5.3 and use bilateral grid or app_opt (check that 1.5.3 has them). For (c), each model has one camera type, so PPISP matters less. It is needed mainly for (b).

conflicts.description: Compute headroom. aerial-ground-fusion says VRAM is not the bottleneck at 10x10 m. drone-forest-canopy's fact-check notes TreeDGS used 32 GB VRAM for 365 images. drone-capture-hardware notes that INRIA keeps all images on the GPU (about 6.9 GB for 300) and that ODM needs 16-32 GB RAM for 250-500 images. The fusion vendor recommends an RTX 3090/4090 and at least 64 GB RAM. The laptop's system RAM is unknown.
conflicts.suggested_resolution: For (c) on the laptop: train with gsplat, keeping images on the host or disk (never INRIA with data_device=cuda), at 1600-2000 px, with an MCMC cap of about 1-3M for the aerial layer. Run SfM in COLMAP with the spatial matcher and GPS priors. Measure the laptop's RAM. If it is 32 GB or less, cap the aerial set at about 300-400 images and use ODX only for small orthophoto/DSM jobs.

conflicts.description: Drone SfM and GCP tooling. drone-alignment recommends GCP-constrained bundle adjustment in ODM/OpenSfM, Metashape or Leica Infinity. Its fact-check found that local-frame GCPs are unproven in ODM/OpenSfM, that ODM --align does not fit (it needs a CRS and a matching DSM, with scale fixed), and that COLMAP has no GCP term in BA. drone-capture-hardware suggests ODX/WebODM as an external process. modular-architecture suggests a NodeODM wrapper. drone-forest-canopy mentions DJI Terra GS (USD 3,700/yr).
conflicts.suggested_resolution: Default path, all open-source and Windows-native: COLMAP with EXIF GNSS pose priors, then triangulate the target centres, then a robust Umeyama Sim(3), with an optional pyceres BA that adds GCP residuals. Use ODX/WebODM (AGPL, external process) only for the aerial ortho and DSM. Use Metashape, Infinity or Terra only if Hexagon already holds licences (gap 2 checks local-frame GCP support).

gap.title: Lantmäteriet permit mechanics for splats derived from drone images, model versions and internal sharing
gap.why_it_matters:
The permit decides whether (c)'s aerial layer can be iterated and shared at all. It also decides how lineage and clearance must be modelled in the source interface, and whether a drone + Insta360 project without LiDAR is legally workable. The topics disagree on several points:
- Whether derived 3D models from approved images need no separate review, or each model version needs a new application.
- Whether a Hexagon on-prem server counts as 'full control'.
- Whether a ground-only splat that only took poses or scale from drone SfM is covered.
- Whether the forest exemption survives the BLK2GO operator and targets being visible in the frames.
gap.research_prompt:
Research Sweden's rules on dissemination of aerial imagery (lag 2016:319 om skydd för geografisk information §9; förordning 2016:320; Lantmäteriet's spridningstillstånd pages, FAQ (vanliga frågor), exemption (undantag) pages and the LMFS regulation on exemptions) as they apply to a Gaussian-splat 3D model trained from consumer-drone photos of a ~10x10 m forest plot plus a ~60x60 m buffer, as of October 2026. Answer each question with verbatim Swedish quotes and URLs:
(1) If the source JPGs are submitted and approved, may new splat or mesh versions trained from the returned images be published without a new application? Find the exact wording on 'följdprodukter'.
(2) If a finished 3D model is submitted instead, is it approved or refused as a whole, and does each retrained version need a new application?
(3) Is storage on a company-controlled on-premises server, a corporate OneDrive/SharePoint or a private Git remote 'dissemination' ('servrar som du inte själv har fullständig kontroll över')?
(4) Is a model built only from ground photos and handheld LiDAR, whose coordinate frame or scale came from a drone photogrammetry solution or from drone-visible targets, covered by §9?
(5) Does the forest exemption still apply if a person carrying a survey instrument, survey targets or a forest road is visible, and does it cover a buffer of surroundings?
(6) Current processing time and upload limits, and whether an approved case number can be cited publicly.
Also give the exact email or form for asking Lantmäteriet a pre-capture question, and draft that question in Swedish. Do not rely on blogs where a Lantmäteriet page exists, and say which answers are only inference.

gap.title: Feasibility and accuracy of a shared-target tie between drone imagery and BLK2GO data under forest conditions
gap.why_it_matters:
Every topic names physical targets as the primary drone-to-LiDAR tie (2-5 cm expected), and both (c) and any (b) attempt depend on it. Four things are unverified:
- Whether BLK2GO/Cyclone can extract target centres at cm level.
- Which target design shows up in BLK2GO intensity against vegetation and also in drone and 360 imagery.
- How much BLK2GO SLAM drifts between the plot interior and a clearing 10-30 m away.
- Which tool on Windows can run a bundle adjustment with GCPs given in a local, non-georeferenced frame.
The GSD the targets need also conflicts with the proposed flight altitudes.
gap.research_prompt:
Research, as of October 2026, how to tie a drone photogrammetry block to a Leica BLK2GO handheld SLAM point cloud (no GNSS, Cyclone FIELD 360 / REGISTER 360 PLUS export) through shared ground targets. Find primary sources (Leica documentation, Leica/Hexagon release notes, peer-reviewed or vendor test reports) on:
(1) Whether Cyclone REGISTER 360 PLUS (BLK edition) or Cyclone FIELD 360 supports control points, checkerboard or B/W targets, or sphere targets for BLK2GO data, including any 'BLK2GO GCP' or georeferencing feature, its workflow, and its stated accuracy.
(2) The achievable target-centre accuracy in BLK2GO clouds (range noise ±3 mm, point spacing) for planar checkerboards, retro-reflective targets and spheres at 1-10 m range, and whether white paint and vegetation can be told apart in BLK2GO intensity.
(3) Measured BLK2GO SLAM drift or relative accuracy outdoors or in forests over 20-100 m loops, ideally with independent checkpoints.
(4) A dual-use target design that a camera drone at 1-3 cm GSD and the BLK2GO can both detect (size versus the Pix4D rule of 5-10x GSD manual and 20x GSD automatic).
(5) Software that can run bundle adjustment with GCPs in an arbitrary local Cartesian frame on Windows: Agisoft Metashape local coordinates, Leica Infinity, OpenDroneMap/OpenSfM with a fake projected CRS, or COLMAP plus pycolmap/pyceres with a custom GCP residual. For each, give the licence and whether it handles DJI XMP metadata.
Give numbers with URLs and mark what is unverified.

gap.title: Real-data evidence on what aerial imagery adds to a forest splat, and what a drone actually sees of Swedish forest stands
gap.why_it_matters: The decision against (b), and the value of (c) for Swedish plots, rests mostly on synthetic or urban studies (MatrixCity, UC-GS, DRAGON, AerialMegaDepth, Horizon-GS) plus inference about forests. Only one real forest LiDAR + UAV 3DGS paper was found, and it covered open canopy only. TreeDGS suggests oblique aerial images can recover stems in thinned pine, which might give (c) more value in Sweden than 'canopy only'. Whether (c) beats free Lantmäteriet open data for a 10x10 m plot also depends on this evidence.
gap.research_prompt:
Find 2024-2026 papers, preprints, theses and credible practitioner case studies (arXiv, CVPR/ICCV/ECCV/WACV workshops, ISPRS, Remote Sensing, Forests, IEEE TGRS) that reconstruct REAL forests with NeRF or 3D Gaussian Splatting from BOTH drone/UAV images AND ground-level or under-canopy images, or from UAV images plus handheld or terrestrial LiDAR. Candidate searches include 'forest Gaussian splatting UAV terrestrial', 'aerial-ground 3DGS forest', 'TreeDGS', 'LiDAR-guided semantic 3D Gaussian splatting forest digital twin', 'under-canopy NeRF drone', 'ForestSplat', 'boreal forest 3DGS', and 'Gaussian splatting tropical forest canopy UAV'. For each paper, report:
- forest type and canopy density
- sensors, altitudes and overlaps
- how aerial and ground poses were tied (joint SfM, GNSS/RTK, LiDAR registration, targets)
- whether ground-level novel-view metrics (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS) were reported with and without aerial images
- the reported failure modes
- code licence
Separately, find measurements of how much stem or forest-floor area oblique drone photogrammetry recovers in Scots pine, Norway spruce and birch stands in Sweden or Finland, by stand density or canopy cover. Compare with the resolution and coverage of Lantmäteriet's open data (Laserdata NH/Skog point density, Markhöjdmodell 1 m, ortofoto 0.16 m; confirm the licence per product). Conclude whether a consumer-drone aerial splat adds information beyond that open data for a 10x10 m plot.

gap.title: Drone procurement, automation and corporate-policy constraints for a C0/C1 versus RTK platform in 2026
gap.why_it_matters: The topics disagree on the platform: C0 Mini 5 Pro, Mini 4 Pro for MSDK automation, or an RTK Matrice 4E. Current EU and Swedish prices were not verified. Whether Hexagon policy allows buying DJI is unknown, and so is whether BLK2FLY or any Hexagon aerial sensor is still available. Automating the nadir + oblique + orbit protocol on C0 drones is uncertain (Pixpro has no oblique multi-grid; MSDK works only with RC-N2). These factors set the cost and feasibility of (c).
gap.research_prompt:
As of October 2026, compile a procurement comparison for a small-plot forest aerial-photogrammetry and Gaussian-splat drone to be flown in Sweden under EU Open-category rules by a Hexagon employee. Candidates: DJI Mini 4 Pro (RC-N2 bundle), DJI Mini 5 Pro, DJI Lito X1, DJI Air 3S, DJI Matrice 4E, Autel EVO II Pro (RTK) V3 or its successor, Parrot ANAFI UKR/Ai, and any Leica/Hexagon aerial capture product (check whether BLK2FLY is discontinued).
For each, give:
- current Swedish/EU retail price
- EASA class label and the configuration it depends on (battery)
- Remote ID
- sensor size, resolution and shutter type
- minimum photo interval at full and binned resolution
- RTK/PPK support
- MSDK or other SDK support and the required controller
- which mission apps (DJI Fly waypoints, DJI Pilot 2, Dronelink, Litchi Pilot/Hub, Pixpro Waypoints, UgCS, Pix4Dcapture successor) can fly a nadir grid, a 4-direction oblique grid at 45 deg, and multi-radius orbits with hover-and-shoot, and at what cost
Also find:
- any public Hexagon/Leica policy, or EU/Swedish public-sector or defence-industry guidance, restricting DJI products
- the current US FCC Covered List status of DJI and Autel, with its relevance to EU buyers
- the 2026 status of EASA Opinion 06/2026
Cite primary vendor and regulator pages and flag estimates.
